fs-316-193-2025.title: Driving under the influence; penalties.

rows.trigger: Defines the offense only. Assigns NO degree and NO term of its own; it routes all punishment to subsection (2), which is itself subject to the exceptions in (2)(b), (3), and (4). Reading (1) alone tells a reader nothing about exposure. NOTE: no provision anywhere in 316.193 is graded by a dollar amount, so min/max are null on every row in this table; every dollar figure that appears is a fine (a penalty), never a grading trigger.
rows.quote: A person is guilty of the offense of driving under the influence and is subject to punishment as provided in subsection (2) if the person is driving or in actual physical control of a vehicle within this state and:(a) The person is under the influence of alcoholic beverages, any chemical substance set forth in s. 877.111, or any substance controlled under chapter 893, when affected to the extent that the person’s normal faculties are impaired;(b) The person has a blood-alcohol level of 0.08 or more grams of alcohol per 100 milliliters of blood; or (c) The person has a breath-alcohol level of 0.08 or more grams of alcohol per 210 liters of breath.

rows.trigger: First conviction. Fine range is the penalty, not a grading trigger. The whole of (2)(a) applies only 'Except as provided in paragraph (b), subsection (3), or subsection (4)' -- a reader who stops at (2)(a) will miss the felony provisions entirely.
rows.quote: Except as provided in paragraph (b), subsection (3), or subsection (4), any person who is convicted of a violation of subsection (1) shall be punished:1. By a fine of:a. Not less than $500 or more than $1,000 for a first conviction.

rows.trigger: Second conviction, with no time limit stated on how old the prior is. Fine range is the penalty, not a grading trigger.
rows.quote: b. Not less than $1,000 or more than $2,000 for a second conviction; and

rows.trigger: First conviction. The statute prescribes a term directly and names no degree. A 6-month maximum corresponds to a second degree misdemeanor under s. 775.082, but s. 316.193 itself does not say so and this row does not infer it.
rows.quote: 2. By imprisonment for:a. Not more than 6 months for a first conviction.

rows.trigger: Second conviction. Term prescribed directly, no degree named. A 9-month maximum matches no standard misdemeanor term in s. 775.082; the statute is silent on degree and this row records only what it says.
rows.quote: b. Not more than 9 months for a second conviction.

rows.trigger: Second conviction. Mandatory ignition interlock for at least 1 year, contingent on the person qualifying for a permanent or restricted license. Not a degree provision but a mandatory consequence attached to a second conviction. NOTE the numbering trap inside (2)(a): subparagraph 1 is fines, subparagraph 2 is imprisonment, and subparagraph 3 is neither -- it is an interlock mandate. A reader who opens (2)(a) looking for the jail exposure, finds it in subparagraph 2, and stops will never reach subparagraph 3 or the flush paragraph that follows it.
rows.quote: 3. For a second conviction, by mandatory placement for a period of at least 1 year, at the convicted person’s sole expense, of an ignition interlock device approved by the department in accordance with s. 316.1938 upon all vehicles that are individually or jointly leased or owned and routinely operated by the convicted person, when the convicted person qualifies for a permanent or restricted license.

rows.trigger: ADDED ON REPAIR -- this flush paragraph had no row. Unnumbered paragraph closing (2)(a), carrying no cite of its own. It is a fiscal-disposition rule: the amount of a (2)(a)1. fine above the $500 / $1,000 floors goes to the Department of Revenue rather than to the local clerk. It does not change the fine ranges in 1.a. or 1.b. and assigns no degree. Parallel remittance sentences appear inside (2)(b)2., inside (2)(b)3., and in the flush language of subsection (4).
rows.quote: The portion of a fine imposed in excess of $500 pursuant to sub-subparagraph 1.a. and the portion of a fine imposed in excess of $1,000 pursuant to sub-subparagraph 1.b., shall be remitted by the clerk to the Department of Revenue for deposit into the General Revenue Fund.

rows.trigger: Third violation where the offense occurs WITHIN 10 years after a prior conviction. Level 3 independently re-verified this pass from the F.S. 921.0022(3)(c) LEVEL 3 chart, entry '316.193 | (2)(b) | 3rd | Felony DUI, 3rd conviction.' Also carries mandatory interlock of not less than 2 years.
rows.quote: Any person who is convicted of a third violation of this section for an offense that occurs within 10 years after a prior conviction for a violation of this section commits a felony of the third degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084. In addition, the court shall order the mandatory placement for a period of not less than 2 years, at the convicted person’s sole expense, of an ignition interlock device approved by the department in accordance with s. 316.1938 upon all vehicles that are individually or jointly leased or owned and routinely operated by the convicted person, when the convicted person qualifies for a permanent or restricted license.

rows.trigger: THIS IS THE STOP-READING TRAP IN THIS SECTION. A third violation occurring MORE THAN 10 years after the prior conviction is NOT a felony. The statute prescribes a fine of $2,000 to $5,000 and imprisonment of not more than 12 months and names no degree at all. Anyone who opens (2)(b), reads subparagraph 1, and concludes 'third DUI = third degree felony' states the law wrongly for every defendant whose prior is older than 10 years. Mandatory interlock of at least 2 years still applies.
rows.quote: Any person who is convicted of a third violation of this section for an offense that occurs more than 10 years after the date of a prior conviction for a violation of this section shall be punished by a fine of not less than $2,000 or more than $5,000 and by imprisonment for not more than 12 months. The portion of a fine imposed in excess of $2,500 pursuant to this subparagraph shall be remitted by the clerk to the Department of Revenue for deposit into the General Revenue Fund. In addition, the court shall order the mandatory placement for a period of at least 2 years, at the convicted person’s sole expense, of an ignition interlock device approved by the department in accordance with s. 316.1938 upon all vehicles that are individually or jointly leased or owned and routinely operated by the convicted person, when the convicted person qualifies for a permanent or restricted license.

rows.trigger: Fourth or subsequent violation, REGARDLESS of when any prior conviction occurred -- the 10-year window in subparagraphs 1 and 2 does not apply here. Same degree as (2)(b)1. (third degree felony) but placed in a higher offense severity level: Level 6, independently re-verified this pass from the F.S. 921.0022(3)(f) LEVEL 6 chart, entry '316.193 | (2)(b) | 3rd | Felony DUI, 4th or subsequent conviction.' TRIGGER CORRECTED ON REPAIR: an earlier version of this row described Level 6 as 'twice as severe' as Level 3. That characterization is withdrawn -- the level numbers are ordinal chart placements, not a ratio scale, and this table does not read s. 921.0024 to compute point values. Fine floor is stated permissively ('may be not less than $2,000'), which is ambiguous on its face as to whether the $2,000 floor is mandatory.
rows.quote: Any person who is convicted of a fourth or subsequent violation of this section, regardless of when any prior conviction for a violation of this section occurred, commits a felony of the third degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084. However, the fine imposed for such fourth or subsequent violation may be not less than $2,000. The portion of a fine imposed in excess of $1,000 pursuant to this subparagraph shall be remitted by the clerk to the Department of Revenue for deposit into the General Revenue Fund.

rows.trigger: Discretionary ('may order') interlock of at least 6 continuous months where the person's blood- or breath-alcohol level was .08 or higher at the time of the offense. Note this sets no minimum number of prior convictions, so it can reach a first offense.
rows.quote: In addition to the penalties in paragraph (a), the court may order placement, at the convicted person’s sole expense, of an ignition interlock device approved by the department in accordance with s. 316.1938 for at least 6 continuous months upon all vehicles that are individually or jointly leased or owned and routinely operated by the convicted person if, at the time of the offense, the person had a blood-alcohol level or breath-alcohol level of .08 or higher.

rows.trigger: Requires all three of (3)(a) violation of subsection (1), (3)(b) operating a vehicle, and (3)(c) causing or contributing to causing damage to the property OR the person of another. Note 'contributes to causing' -- sole causation is not required. Not ranked in the F.S. 921.0022 chart, which covers felonies only.
rows.quote: Any person:(a) Who is in violation of subsection (1);(b) Who operates a vehicle; and (c) Who, by reason of such operation, causes or contributes to causing:1. Damage to the property or person of another commits a misdemeanor of the first degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082 or s. 775.083.

rows.trigger: Causes or contributes to causing serious bodily injury to another, as that term is defined in s. 316.1933. No prior conviction required -- a first-time offender falls here. Level 7 independently re-verified this pass from the F.S. 921.0022(3)(g) LEVEL 7 chart, entry '316.193 | (3)(c)2. | 3rd | DUI resulting in serious bodily injury.'
rows.quote: Serious bodily injury to another, as defined in s. 316.1933, commits a felony of the third degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.trigger: Causes or contributes to causing the death of any human being OR unborn child ('unborn child' has the meaning in s. 775.021(5)). No prior conviction required. Level 8 independently re-verified this pass from the F.S. 921.0022(3)(h) LEVEL 8 chart, entry '316.193 | (3)(c)3.a. | 2nd | DUI manslaughter.' Subject to the 4-year mandatory minimum in the flush language at the end of subsection (3).
rows.quote: The death of any human being or unborn child commits DUI manslaughter, and commits:a. A felony of the second degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.trigger: DUI manslaughter elevated one degree where BOTH conditions are met: the person knew or should have known the crash occurred, AND the person failed to give information and render aid under s. 316.062. Both (I) and (II) are required -- they are joined by 'and'. Level 9 independently re-verified this pass from the F.S. 921.0022(3)(i) LEVEL 9 chart, entry '316.193 | (3)(c)3.b. | 1st | DUI manslaughter; failing to render aid or give information.'
rows.quote: b. A felony of the first degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084, if:(I) At the time of the crash, the person knew, or should have known, that the crash occurred; and (II) The person failed to give information and render aid as required by s. 316.062.

rows.trigger: DUI manslaughter elevated one degree by criminal history: a prior conviction under this same subparagraph (DUI manslaughter), or under s. 327.35(3)(a)3.c. (BUI manslaughter), s. 782.071 (vehicular homicide), or s. 782.072 (vessel homicide). Level 9 independently re-verified this pass from the F.S. 921.0022(3)(i) LEVEL 9 chart, entry '316.193 | (3)(c)3.c. | 1st | DUI manslaughter; prior conviction for DUI manslaughter, BUI manslaughter, vehicular homicide, or vessel homicide.' The statute text carries an editor's footnote: the citation was substituted for a reference to s. 327.35(3)(c)3. to conform to a 2025 redesignation.
rows.quote: c. A felony of the first degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084, if the person has a prior conviction under this subparagraph, 1s. 327.35(3)(a)3.c., s. 782.071, or s. 782.072.

rows.trigger: Unnumbered flush paragraph closing subsection (3). Easy to miss because it sits after the last sub-subparagraph and carries no cite of its own. It imposes a 4-year mandatory minimum on EVERY DUI manslaughter conviction, i.e. on 3.a., 3.b., and 3.c. alike, and supplies the definition of 'unborn child'. Note it does NOT reach (3)(c)1. or (3)(c)2., which are not DUI manslaughter.
rows.quote: For purposes of this subsection, the term “unborn child” has the same meaning as provided in s. 775.021(5). A person who is convicted of DUI manslaughter shall be sentenced to a mandatory minimum term of imprisonment of 4 years.

rows.trigger: Enhanced penalty subsection, triggered by EITHER a blood- or breath-alcohol level of 0.15 or higher OR being accompanied in the vehicle by a person under 18 at the time of the offense. It raises fines and jail terms but assigns NO degree -- an enhanced first offense is still not made a felony by this subsection. First conviction fine range.
rows.quote: Any person who is convicted of a violation of subsection (1) and who has a blood-alcohol level or breath-alcohol level of 0.15 or higher, or any person who is convicted of a violation of subsection (1) and who at the time of the offense was accompanied in the vehicle by a person under the age of 18 years, shall be punished:(a) By a fine of:1. Not less than $1,000 or more than $2,000 for a first conviction.

rows.trigger: Second conviction under the 0.15-or-higher / minor-passenger enhancement. Fine range only, no degree. Per the flush language following (4)(b)2., the prior conviction that puts a defendant in this tier need NOT itself have been a 0.15-or-higher offense.
rows.quote: 2. Not less than $2,000 or more than $4,000 for a second conviction.

rows.trigger: Third or subsequent conviction under the enhancement. CRITICAL: this fine has a floor of $4,000 and NO STATED CEILING -- unlike (a)1. and (a)2. it prescribes 'not less than' with no upper bound. It also assigns no degree, so a third or subsequent offense is still graded by (2)(b), not here.
rows.quote: 3. Not less than $4,000 for a third or subsequent conviction.

rows.trigger: First conviction under the 0.15-or-higher / minor-passenger enhancement. Term prescribed directly, no degree named. See the separate row for the flush language following (4)(b)2. for the scope rule that governs this paragraph.
rows.quote: (b) By imprisonment for:1. Not more than 9 months for a first conviction.

rows.trigger: Second conviction under the enhancement. Term prescribed directly, no degree named. Note (4)(b) stops at a second conviction -- it prescribes NO jail term for a third or subsequent conviction, even though (4)(a)3. prescribes a fine for one. That asymmetry is on the face of the text.
rows.quote: 2. Not more than 12 months for a second conviction.

rows.trigger: ADDED ON REPAIR -- this flush paragraph had no row of its own and was mentioned only in passing inside another row's trigger. Unnumbered paragraph sitting between (4)(b)2. and paragraph (4)(c), so it is visually easy to read past on the way to (c). Two independent rules. FIRST, a scope rule for the whole of subsection (4): 'only the instant offense is required to be a violation of subsection (1) by a person who has a blood-alcohol level or breath-alcohol level of 0.15 or higher.' That means the prior convictions that push a defendant into the (4)(a)2., (4)(a)3., and (4)(b)2. tiers need NOT themselves have been 0.15-or-higher offenses. Note on its face this sentence is written only in terms of the 0.15 trigger and says nothing express about the minor-passenger trigger; the statute does not resolve that asymmetry. SECOND, a fiscal-disposition rule remitting the above-floor portion of (4)(a) fines to the Department of Revenue.
rows.quote: For the purposes of this subsection, only the instant offense is required to be a violation of subsection (1) by a person who has a blood-alcohol level or breath-alcohol level of 0.15 or higher. The portion of a fine imposed in excess of $1,000 pursuant to subparagraph (a)1. and the portion of a fine imposed in excess of $2,000 pursuant to subparagraph (a)2. or subparagraph (a)3., shall be remitted by the clerk to the Department of Revenue for deposit into the General Revenue Fund.

rows.trigger: Mandatory ('shall order'), not discretionary: interlock for not less than 6 continuous months on a first offense and not less than 2 continuous years on a second offense, where the 0.15-or-higher or minor-passenger trigger is met. Contrast (2)(c), which is discretionary. Note this paragraph sits AFTER the subsection (4) flush language in the printed text.
rows.quote: In addition to the penalties in paragraphs (a) and (b), the court shall order the mandatory placement, at the convicted person’s sole expense, of an ignition interlock device approved by the department in accordance with s. 316.1938 upon all vehicles that are individually or jointly leased or owned and routinely operated by the convicted person for not less than 6 continuous months for the first offense and for not less than 2 continuous years for a second offense, when the convicted person qualifies for a permanent or restricted license.

rows.trigger: ADDED ON REPAIR -- this subsection had no row anywhere and was not referenced in any other row's trigger. It is the single broadest penalty provision in the section: it reaches EVERY offender convicted of violating this section, including the (2)(b) and (3)(c) felonies, with no prior-conviction threshold and no BAC threshold. Three mandatory commands: the court SHALL place all such offenders on monthly reporting probation; the court SHALL require completion of a substance abuse course conducted by a DUI program licensed under s. 322.292, including a psychosocial evaluation; and where the program refers the offender to treatment, completion of the education, evaluation, and treatment is a condition of that probation, in addition to any sentence or fine. A treatment referral resulting from a psychosocial evaluation may not be waived without a supporting independent psychosocial evaluation by a court-appointed provider. On failure to report for or complete treatment or the education course and evaluation, the department SHALL cancel the driving privilege 'notwithstanding the terms of the court order or any suspension or revocation' -- an administrative consequence that overrides the sentencing court. Assigns no degree.
rows.quote: The court shall place all offenders convicted of violating this section on monthly reporting probation and shall require completion of a substance abuse course conducted by a DUI program licensed by the department under s. 322.292, which must include a psychosocial evaluation of the offender. If the DUI program refers the offender to an authorized substance abuse treatment provider for substance abuse treatment, in addition to any sentence or fine imposed under this section, completion of all such education, evaluation, and treatment is a condition of reporting probation. The offender shall assume reasonable costs for such education, evaluation, and treatment. The referral to treatment resulting from a psychosocial evaluation shall not be waived without a supporting independent psychosocial evaluation conducted by an authorized substance abuse treatment provider appointed by the court, which shall have access to the DUI program’s psychosocial evaluation before the independent psychosocial evaluation is conducted. The court shall review the results and recommendations of both evaluations before determining the request for waiver. The offender shall bear the full cost of this procedure. The term “substance abuse” means the abuse of alcohol or any substance named or described in Schedules I through V of s. 893.03. If an offender referred to treatment under this subsection fails to report for or complete such treatment or fails to complete the DUI program substance abuse education course and evaluation, the DUI program shall notify the court and the department of the failure. Upon receipt of the notice, the department shall cancel the offender’s driving privilege, notwithstanding the terms of the court order or any suspension or revocation of the driving privilege. The department may temporarily reinstate the driving privilege on a restricted basis upon verification from the DUI program that the offender is currently participating in treatment and the DUI education course and evaluation requirement has been completed. If the DUI program notifies the department of the second failure to complete treatment, the department shall reinstate the driving privilege only after notice of completion of treatment from the DUI program. The organization that conducts the substance abuse education and evaluation may not provide required substance abuse treatment unless a waiver has been granted to that organization by the department. A waiver may be granted only if the department determines, in accordance with its rules, that the service provider that conducts the substance abuse education and evaluation is the most appropriate service provider and is licensed under chapter 397 or is exempt from such licensure. A statistical referral report shall be submitted quarterly to the department by each organization authorized to provide services under this section.

rows.trigger: QUOTE REPAIRED -- the earlier version of this row cut the quote off mid-paragraph at 'for a minimum of 50 hours.' with no ellipsis, dropping five sentences including the entire impoundment sentence that the row's own trigger relied on. The full paragraph is quoted here. Subsection (6) applies 'regardless of any penalty imposed pursuant to subsection (2), subsection (3), or subsection (4)' -- these are additive to every grading provision above, including the felonies. First conviction: mandatory probation not to exceed 1 year; minimum 50 hours public service or community work; a $10-per-hour buyout available ONLY on an undue-hardship finding based on residence, location, or employment obligations; a cap that the total period of probation and incarceration may not exceed 1 year; and mandatory 10-day impoundment or immobilization. TRIGGER CORRECTED: the impoundment reach here is NARROWER than in (6)(b) and (6)(c). This paragraph reaches only 'the vehicle that was operated by or in the actual control of the defendant or any one vehicle registered in the defendant's name' -- one vehicle. (6)(b) and (6)(c) reach ALL vehicles owned by the defendant. An earlier version of this row flattened that distinction. Impoundment must not run concurrently with incarceration, and the order may be dismissed under (6)(e), (f), (g), or (h) -- and, per (6)(i), on proof of installed interlock. No degree assigned.
rows.quote: With respect to any person convicted of a violation of subsection (1), regardless of any penalty imposed pursuant to subsection (2), subsection (3), or subsection (4):(a) For the first conviction, the court shall place the defendant on probation for a period not to exceed 1 year and, as a condition of such probation, shall order the defendant to participate in public service or a community work project for a minimum of 50 hours. The court may order a defendant to pay a fine of $10 for each hour of public service or community work otherwise required only if the court finds that the residence or location of the defendant at the time public service or community work is required or the defendant’s employment obligations would create an undue hardship for the defendant. However, the total period of probation and incarceration may not exceed 1 year. The court must also, as a condition of probation, order the impoundment or immobilization of the vehicle that was operated by or in the actual control of the defendant or any one vehicle registered in the defendant’s name at the time of impoundment or immobilization, for a period of 10 days or for the unexpired term of any lease or rental agreement that expires within 10 days. The impoundment or immobilization must not occur concurrently with the incarceration of the defendant. The impoundment or immobilization order may be dismissed in accordance with paragraph (e), paragraph (f), paragraph (g), or paragraph (h).

rows.trigger: MANDATORY MINIMUM JAIL, and note the window here is 5 years, NOT the 10 years used in (2)(b). A second conviction within 5 years of a prior carries a floor of 10 days imprisonment with at least 48 hours consecutive, plus 30-day impoundment of ALL vehicles owned by the defendant (broader than (6)(a), which reaches one vehicle). The differing time windows across (2)(b), (6)(b), and (6)(c) are a frequent source of error. Dismissal grounds are in (6)(e) through (6)(h) and, separately, (6)(i).
rows.quote: For the second conviction for an offense that occurs within a period of 5 years after the date of a prior conviction for violation of this section, the court shall order imprisonment for not less than 10 days. The court must also, as a condition of probation, order the impoundment or immobilization of all vehicles owned by the defendant at the time of impoundment or immobilization, for a period of 30 days or for the unexpired term of any lease or rental agreement that expires within 30 days. The impoundment or immobilization must not occur concurrently with the incarceration of the defendant and must occur concurrently with the driver license revocation imposed under s. 322.28(2)(a)2. The impoundment or immobilization order may be dismissed in accordance with paragraph (e), paragraph (f), paragraph (g), or paragraph (h). At least 48 hours of confinement must be consecutive.

rows.trigger: MANDATORY MINIMUM JAIL of not less than 30 days for a third or subsequent conviction within 10 years, with at least 48 hours consecutive, plus 90-day impoundment of ALL vehicles owned by the defendant. This applies even where the offense is NOT a felony -- it reaches the (2)(b)2. non-felony third conviction as well as the (2)(b)1. and (2)(b)3. felonies. Dismissal grounds are in (6)(e) through (6)(h) and, separately, (6)(i).
rows.quote: For the third or subsequent conviction for an offense that occurs within a period of 10 years after the date of a prior conviction for violation of this section, the court shall order imprisonment for not less than 30 days. The court must also, as a condition of probation, order the impoundment or immobilization of all vehicles owned by the defendant at the time of impoundment or immobilization, for a period of 90 days or for the unexpired term of any lease or rental agreement that expires within 90 days. The impoundment or immobilization must not occur concurrently with the incarceration of the defendant and must occur concurrently with the driver license revocation imposed under s. 322.28(2)(a)3. The impoundment or immobilization order may be dismissed in accordance with paragraph (e), paragraph (f), paragraph (g), or paragraph (h). At least 48 hours of confinement must be consecutive.

rows.trigger: ADDED ON REPAIR -- no row previously. Mechanics of the impoundment order required by (6)(a), (b), and (c). The court MUST issue the order at the time of sentencing; the order must list the name and telephone numbers of all immobilization agencies meeting the conditions of subsection (13); and within 7 business days the clerk must give certified-mail notice to any registered owner other than the defendant and to each lienholder of record. Assigns no degree, but it is the procedural predicate for the third-party dismissal rights in (e) through (h).
rows.quote: The court must at the time of sentencing the defendant issue an order for the impoundment or immobilization of a vehicle. The order of impoundment or immobilization must include the name and telephone numbers of all immobilization agencies meeting all of the conditions of subsection (13). Within 7 business days after the date that the court issues the order of impoundment or immobilization, the clerk of the court must send notice by certified mail, return receipt requested, to the registered owner of each vehicle, if the registered owner is a person other than the defendant, and to each person of record claiming a lien against the vehicle.

rows.trigger: ADDED ON REPAIR -- no row previously, even though (6)(a), (6)(b), and (6)(c) each cross-reference 'paragraph (e)' by name. First of the four dismissal grounds. A non-operating owner may submit a police report showing the vehicle was stolen at the time of the offense, or documentation of purchase after the offense from someone other than the defendant or the defendant's agent. On a finding of theft or a non-circumventing sale, the order MUST be dismissed and the owner incurs no costs. If the request is denied, the petitioner may request an evidentiary hearing.
rows.quote: A person who owns but was not operating the vehicle when the offense occurred may submit to the court a police report indicating that the vehicle was stolen at the time of the offense or documentation of having purchased the vehicle after the offense was committed from an entity other than the defendant or the defendant’s agent. If the court finds that the vehicle was stolen or that the sale was not made to circumvent the order and allow the defendant continued access to the vehicle, the order must be dismissed and the owner of the vehicle will incur no costs. If the court denies the request to dismiss the order of impoundment or immobilization, the petitioner may request an evidentiary hearing.

rows.trigger: ADDED ON REPAIR -- no row previously, though cross-referenced by name in (6)(a), (b), and (c). Second dismissal ground, covering the case (e) does not: a non-operating owner whose vehicle was stolen, or who bought it after the offense DIRECTLY from the defendant or the defendant's agent, may request an evidentiary hearing. Dismissal requires findings of theft, or of purchase without knowledge of the offense, plus no relationship to the defendant beyond the transaction, plus that the purchase would not circumvent the order.
rows.quote: A person who owns but was not operating the vehicle when the offense occurred, and whose vehicle was stolen or who purchased the vehicle after the offense was committed directly from the defendant or the defendant’s agent, may request an evidentiary hearing to determine whether the impoundment or immobilization should occur. If the court finds that either the vehicle was stolen or the purchase was made without knowledge of the offense, that the purchaser had no relationship to the defendant other than through the transaction, and that such purchase would not circumvent the order and allow the defendant continued access to the vehicle, the order must be dismissed and the owner of the vehicle will incur no costs.

rows.trigger: ADDED ON REPAIR -- no row previously, though cross-referenced by name in (6)(a), (b), and (c). Third dismissal ground, and it is MANDATORY on the finding ('shall also dismiss'): the court must dismiss the impoundment or immobilization order if the family of the vehicle's owner has no other private or public means of transportation.
rows.quote: The court shall also dismiss the order of impoundment or immobilization of the vehicle if the court finds that the family of the owner of the vehicle has no other private or public means of transportation.

rows.trigger: ADDED ON REPAIR -- no row previously, though cross-referenced by name in (6)(a), (b), and (c). Fourth dismissal ground, and it is DISCRETIONARY ('may also dismiss'), unlike (g): vehicles owned by the defendant but operated solely by the defendant's employees or by employees of any business the defendant owns.
rows.quote: The court may also dismiss the order of impoundment or immobilization of any vehicles that are owned by the defendant but that are operated solely by the employees of the defendant or any business owned by the defendant.

rows.trigger: ADDED ON REPAIR -- no row previously. A FIFTH dismissal ground that the (6)(a), (b), and (c) cross-references do NOT list: those paragraphs name only (e), (f), (g), and (h), so a reader who follows only the cross-references will never reach it. Proof to the court's satisfaction of a functioning, certified ignition interlock device installed on all vehicles individually or jointly leased or owned and routinely operated by the convicted person lets the court dismiss the impoundment or immobilization order. Discretionary ('may also dismiss').
rows.quote: The court may also dismiss the order of impoundment or immobilization if the defendant provides proof to the satisfaction of the court that a functioning, certified ignition interlock device has been installed upon all vehicles that are individually or jointly leased or owned and routinely operated by the convicted person.

rows.trigger: ADDED ON REPAIR -- no row previously. Subparagraph 1 authorizes the court, 'notwithstanding the provisions of this section, s. 316.1937, and s. 322.2715 relating to ignition interlock devices required for second or subsequent offenders,' to order participation in a qualified sobriety and drug monitoring program IN ADDITION to the interlock requirement, at the person's sole expense. It is available both pretrial and posttrial. Subparagraph 2 defines the program and its permitted modalities (twice-daily breath testing; continuous transdermal monitoring in hardship cases; random blood, breath, urine, or oral fluid testing) and preserves the court's power to order an interlock as a testing modality. Subparagraph 3 defines 'evidence-based program' by a two-of-three test. Assigns no degree.
rows.quote: 1. Notwithstanding the provisions of this section, s. 316.1937, and s. 322.2715 relating to ignition interlock devices required for second or subsequent offenders, in order to strengthen the pretrial and posttrial options available to prosecutors and judges, the court may order, if deemed appropriate, that a person participate in a qualified sobriety and drug monitoring program, as defined in subparagraph 2., in addition to the ignition interlock device requirement. Participation shall be at the person’s sole expense. 2. As used in this paragraph, the term “qualified sobriety and drug monitoring program” means an evidence-based program, approved by the department, in which participants are regularly tested for alcohol and drug use. As the court deems appropriate, the program may monitor alcohol or drugs through one or more of the following modalities: breath testing twice a day; continuous transdermal alcohol monitoring in cases of hardship; or random blood, breath, urine, or oral fluid testing. Testing modalities that provide the best ability to sanction a violation as close in time as reasonably feasible to the occurrence of the violation should be given preference. This paragraph does not preclude a court from ordering an ignition interlock device as a testing modality. 3. For purposes of this paragraph, the term “evidence-based program” means a program that satisfies the requirements of at least two of the following:a. The program is included in the federal registry of evidence-based programs and practices.b. The program has been reported in a peer-reviewed journal as having positive effects on the primary targeted outcome.c. The program has been documented as effective by informed experts and other sources.

rows.trigger: ADDED ON REPAIR -- no row previously. Cost allocation for the impoundment or immobilization ordered under (6)(a), (b), and (c): all costs and fees, including the cost of the (6)(d) notification, fall on the vehicle's owner, or on the lessee or renter if leased or rented, UNLESS the order is dismissed under (e) through (i). Note this can put costs on a third-party owner who never drove. All provisions of s. 713.78 apply, and payment goes directly to the person impounding or immobilizing.
rows.quote: All costs and fees for the impoundment or immobilization, including the cost of notification, must be paid by the owner of the vehicle or, if the vehicle is leased or rented, by the person leasing or renting the vehicle, unless the impoundment or immobilization order is dismissed. All provisions of s. 713.78 shall apply. The costs and fees for the impoundment or immobilization must be paid directly to the person impounding or immobilizing the vehicle.

rows.scope: vehicle owner or lienholder of record
rows.trigger: ADDED ON REPAIR -- no row previously. Wrongful-taking remedy for an owner or a lienholder of record who has NOT already sought review under (e), (f), or (g): file a complaint within 10 days after knowledge of the vehicle's location, in the county of the owner's residence, to determine whether the vehicle was wrongfully taken or withheld. The vehicle can be released in the meantime by posting bond or security equal to the impoundment costs and fees. Note the text says 'impounded or immobilized under this paragraph' although the impoundment is ordered under paragraphs (a), (b), and (c).
rows.quote: The person who owns a vehicle that is impounded or immobilized under this paragraph, or a person who has a lien of record against such a vehicle and who has not requested a review of the impoundment pursuant to paragraph (e), paragraph (f), or paragraph (g), may, within 10 days after the date that person has knowledge of the location of the vehicle, file a complaint in the county in which the owner resides to determine whether the vehicle was wrongfully taken or withheld from the owner or lienholder. Upon the filing of a complaint, the owner or lienholder may have the vehicle released by posting with the court a bond or other adequate security equal to the amount of the costs and fees for impoundment or immobilization, including towing or storage, to ensure the payment of such costs and fees if the owner or lienholder does not prevail. When the bond is posted and the fee is paid as set forth in s. 28.24, the clerk of the court shall issue a certificate releasing the vehicle. At the time of release, after reasonable inspection, the owner or lienholder must give a receipt to the towing or storage company indicating any loss or damage to the vehicle or to the contents of the vehicle.

rows.trigger: ADDED ON REPAIR -- no row previously. This paragraph directly modifies HOW the imprisonment prescribed by every other provision in this section is served: in the court's discretion the defendant may serve all or any portion of a term of imprisonment imposed 'pursuant to this section' in a residential alcoholism or residential drug abuse treatment program, and time in such a program MUST be credited toward the term of imprisonment. On its face this reaches terms imposed under (2)(a)2., (2)(b)2., (4)(b), and the mandatory minimums in (6)(b) and (6)(c). Note it is buried at the very end of the (6) impoundment paragraphs, where nothing signals that it is about imprisonment generally rather than impoundment. Assigns no degree.
rows.quote: A defendant, in the court’s discretion, may be required to serve all or any portion of a term of imprisonment to which the defendant has been sentenced pursuant to this section in a residential alcoholism treatment program or a residential drug abuse treatment program. Any time spent in such a program must be credited by the court toward the term of imprisonment.

rows.trigger: QUOTE REPAIRED -- the earlier version of this row stopped after the 'previous conviction' sentence with no ellipsis and dropped the entire second half of the same flush paragraph. Unnumbered paragraph closing subsection (6), easily missed. TWO distinct rules. FIRST, it defines what counts as a 'previous conviction' for the whole section and materially widens the prior-conviction triggers in (2)(a), (2)(b), (4), and (6): boating-under-the-influence convictions under s. 327.35, convictions under former s. 316.1931, former s. 860.01, and former s. 316.028, and ANY out-of-state alcohol- or drug-related traffic conviction all count as priors. SECOND, restored here: on a finding that the defendant is financially unable to pay all or part of a fine imposed under this section, the court may order additional public service or community work in lieu of the unpayable portion, valuing the services at not less than the federal minimum wage at the time of sentencing.
rows.quote: For the purposes of this section, any conviction for a violation of s. 327.35; a previous conviction for the violation of former s. 316.1931, former s. 860.01, or former s. 316.028; or a previous conviction outside this state for driving under the influence, driving while intoxicated, driving with an unlawful blood-alcohol level, driving with an unlawful breath-alcohol level, or any other similar alcohol-related or drug-related traffic offense, is also considered a previous conviction for violation of this section. However, in satisfaction of the fine imposed pursuant to this section, the court may, upon a finding that the defendant is financially unable to pay either all or part of the fine, order that the defendant participate for a specified additional period of time in public service or a community work project in lieu of payment of that portion of the fine which the court determines the defendant is unable to pay. In determining such additional sentence, the court shall consider the amount of the unpaid portion of the fine and the reasonable value of the services to be ordered; however, the court may not compute the reasonable value of services at a rate less than the federal minimum wage at the time of sentencing.

rows.trigger: ADDED ON REPAIR -- no row previously. Preserves civil exposure: a conviction under this section does not bar any civil suit for damages against the person convicted. Relevant to the total consequences of conviction and it assigns no degree.
rows.quote: A conviction under this section does not bar any civil suit for damages against the person so convicted.

rows.trigger: ADDED ON REPAIR -- no row previously. Clerk's arraignment-notice duty warning that on conviction the court SHALL suspend or revoke the driver license, plus the harmless-error rule: failure to give the notice does not affect the suspension or revocation. Note this is the only place in the section that states the license suspension or revocation consequence as a certainty ('shall'), and the operative suspension provisions live in chapter 322, not here.
rows.quote: At the arraignment, or in conjunction with any notice of arraignment provided by the clerk of the court, the clerk shall provide any person charged with a violation of this section with notice that upon conviction the court shall suspend or revoke the offender’s driver license and that the offender should make arrangements for transportation at any proceeding in which the court may take such action. Failure to provide such notice does not affect the court’s suspension or revocation of the offender’s driver license.

rows.trigger: ADDED ON REPAIR -- no row previously. A mandatory custodial consequence that attaches on ARREST, not on conviction, and so is missed by anyone reading only the conviction-keyed subsections. A person arrested for a violation of this section MAY NOT be released from custody until no longer impaired, until blood- or breath-alcohol is less than 0.05, or until 8 hours have elapsed from arrest. Note the paragraphs are joined by 'or', so the 8-hour paragraph functions as an outside limit rather than a floor that must be reached in every case. Assigns no degree.
rows.quote: A person who is arrested for a violation of this section may not be released from custody:(a) Until the person is no longer under the influence of alcoholic beverages, any chemical substance set forth in s. 877.111, or any substance controlled under chapter 893 and affected to the extent that his or her normal faculties are impaired;(b) Until the person’s blood-alcohol level or breath-alcohol level is less than 0.05; or (c) Until 8 hours have elapsed from the time the person was arrested.

rows.trigger: ADDED ON REPAIR -- no row previously. Evidentiary bar: DHSMV rulings under s. 322.2615 may not be considered in any trial under this section, and testimony or evidence from the administrative proceeding, or any written statement submitted in a request for administrative review, is inadmissible in any criminal proceeding unless timely disclosed in criminal discovery under Fla. R. Crim. P. 3.220. Assigns no degree.
rows.quote: The rulings of the Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles under s. 322.2615 shall not be considered in any trial for a violation of this section. Testimony or evidence from the administrative proceedings or any written statement submitted by a person in his or her request for administrative review is inadmissible into evidence or for any other purpose in any criminal proceeding, unless timely disclosed in criminal discovery pursuant to Rule 3.220, Florida Rules of Criminal Procedure.

rows.trigger: ADDED ON REPAIR -- no row previously. Rulemaking directive to DHSMV to implement the use of ignition interlock devices, which are mandated or authorized by (2)(a)3., (2)(b)1., (2)(b)2., (2)(c), (4)(c), (6)(i), and (6)(j). Assigns no degree.
rows.quote: The Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles is directed to adopt rules providing for the implementation of the use of ignition interlock devices.

rows.trigger: ADDED ON REPAIR -- no row previously, and it is load-bearing for a large share of this table. It supplies the proof rule for the prior convictions that drive the grading in (2)(a), (2)(b), (4), and (6): DHSMV records showing a prior DUI conviction are sufficient BY THEMSELVES to establish that prior. The presumption is rebuttable -- the evidence 'may be contradicted or rebutted by other evidence' and is weighed along with any other evidence. Assigns no degree, but no prior-conviction trigger in this section can be assessed without it.
rows.quote: If the records of the Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles show that the defendant has been previously convicted of the offense of driving under the influence, that evidence is sufficient by itself to establish that prior conviction for driving under the influence. However, such evidence may be contradicted or rebutted by other evidence. This presumption may be considered along with any other evidence presented in deciding whether the defendant has been previously convicted of the offense of driving under the influence.

rows.trigger: ADDED ON REPAIR -- no row previously for the introductory language of subsection (13). Gating rule: where circuit court personnel or the sheriff do not immobilize vehicles, ONLY immobilization agencies meeting the conditions of this subsection may immobilize vehicles in that judicial circuit. This is the provision that (6)(d) cross-references when it requires the impoundment order to list qualifying agencies. Assigns no degree itself; the criminal sanction is in (13)(c).
rows.quote: If personnel of the circuit court or the sheriff do not immobilize vehicles, only immobilization agencies that meet the conditions of this subsection shall immobilize vehicles in that judicial circuit.

rows.scope: immobilization agencies and the persons they assign to immobilize vehicles
rows.trigger: ADDED ON REPAIR -- no row previously, even though this paragraph supplies the ENTIRE substance of the offense that (13)(c) criminalizes. (13)(c) punishes 'a person who violates paragraph (a)' and says nothing about what paragraph (a) requires; without this row the elements of that first degree misdemeanor are nowhere in the table. Subparagraph 1 imposes affidavit and recordkeeping duties on the agency: verifiable experience, accurate and complete records of payments, court orders, and all relevant documents kept for at least 3 years, and employment only of persons meeting subparagraph 2. Subparagraph 2 sets five disqualifiers for the individual who immobilizes a vehicle, covering adjudicated incapacity or involuntary mental health placement, chronic alcohol abuse or a DUI conviction within 2 years, controlled substance commitment or conviction, any unrestored felony, and citizenship or work authorization. Compliance is 'strict.' Assigns no degree itself.
rows.quote: The immobilization agency responsible for immobilizing vehicles in that judicial circuit shall be subject to strict compliance with all of the following conditions and restrictions:1. Any immobilization agency engaged in the business of immobilizing vehicles shall provide to the clerk of the court a signed affidavit attesting that the agency:a. Has verifiable experience in immobilizing vehicles;b. Maintains accurate and complete records of all payments for the immobilization, copies of all documents pertaining to the court’s order of impoundment or immobilization, and any other documents relevant to each immobilization. Such records must be maintained by the immobilization agency for at least 3 years; and c. Employs and assigns persons to immobilize vehicles that meet the requirements established in subparagraph 2. 2. The person who immobilizes a vehicle must:a. Not have been adjudicated incapacitated under s. 744.331, or a similar statute in another state, unless his or her capacity has been judicially restored; involuntarily placed in a treatment facility for the mentally ill under chapter 394, or a similar law in any other state, unless his or her competency has been judicially restored; or diagnosed as having an incapacitating mental illness unless a psychologist or psychiatrist licensed in this state certifies that he or she does not currently suffer from the mental illness.b. Not be a chronic and habitual user of alcoholic beverages to the extent that his or her normal faculties are impaired; not have been committed under chapter 397, former chapter 396, or a similar law in any other state; not have been found to be a habitual offender under s. 856.011(3), or a similar law in any other state; or not have had any convictions under this section, or a similar law in any other state, within 2 years before the affidavit is submitted.c. Not have been committed for controlled substance abuse or have been found guilty of a crime under chapter 893, or a similar law in any other state, relating to controlled substances in any other state.d. Not have been found guilty of or entered a plea of guilty or nolo contendere to, regardless of adjudication, or been convicted of a felony, unless his or her civil rights have been restored.e. Be a citizen or legal resident alien of the United States or have been granted authorization to seek employment in this country by the United States Bureau of Citizenship and Immigration Services.

rows.trigger: ADDED ON REPAIR -- no row previously. Mandatory FDLE state criminal history check by the immobilization agency on each person hired to immobilize a vehicle, to verify the felony disqualifier in sub-subparagraph (a)2.d. Note the check is required only as to (a)2.d., not as to the other four disqualifiers in (a)2. Also note that (13)(c) criminalizes violations of paragraph (a) only, so a failure to run this (b) check is not itself made a crime by (13)(c). Assigns no degree.
rows.quote: The immobilization agency shall conduct a state criminal history check through the Florida Department of Law Enforcement to ensure that the person hired to immobilize a vehicle meets the requirements in sub-subparagraph (a)2.d.

rows.scope: immobilization agencies and the persons they assign to immobilize vehicles; NOT the DUI defendant
rows.trigger: A SEPARATE OFFENSE BURIED IN A PROCEDURAL SUBSECTION, and it does not apply to the DUI defendant at all. SCOPE FIELD CORRECTED ON REPAIR: this row previously carried a null scope, which would let a consumer filtering by scope treat this first degree misdemeanor as exposure sitting on the same defendant as every other row in the table. It criminalizes violation of the recordkeeping, experience, affidavit, and personnel-qualification conditions in 316.193(13)(a) -- see the (13)(a) row for the elements. It reaches violations of paragraph (a) only, not the (b) criminal-history-check duty. A reader scanning only the grading subsections (2), (3), and (4) will never see that this section assigns a degree in subsection (13). Not ranked in the F.S. 921.0022 chart, which covers felonies only.
rows.quote: A person who violates paragraph (a) commits a misdemeanor of the first degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082 or s. 775.083.

rows.trigger: ADDED ON REPAIR -- no row previously. Definitions, and note the scope: 'As used in this chapter' -- chapter 316 as a whole, not merely this section. Defines 'immobilization,' 'immobilizing,' or 'immobilize' (steering wheel antitheft device, tire lock or wheel clamp, or a governmental agency taking the license tag and registration), 'immobilization agency' (any entity meeting all the conditions of subsection (13)), 'impoundment,' 'impounding,' or 'impound' (storing the vehicle at a storage facility with control, supervision, and responsibility over it), and 'person' (which here means any business entity as well as an individual). These are the controlling definitions for the (6) impoundment and immobilization consequences and for the (13) offense. Note that the broad entity definition of 'person' in (14)(d) is what lets the (13)(c) misdemeanor reach an immobilization agency and not only an individual.
rows.quote: As used in this chapter, the term:(a) “Immobilization,” “immobilizing,” or “immobilize” means the act of installing a vehicle antitheft device on the steering wheel of a vehicle, the act of placing a tire lock or wheel clamp on a vehicle, or a governmental agency’s act of taking physical possession of the license tag and vehicle registration rendering a vehicle legally inoperable to prevent any person from operating the vehicle pursuant to an order of impoundment or immobilization under subsection (6).(b) “Immobilization agency” or “immobilization agencies” means any person, firm, company, agency, organization, partnership, corporation, association, trust, or other business entity of any kind whatsoever that meets all of the conditions of subsection (13).(c) “Impoundment,” “impounding,” or “impound” means the act of storing a vehicle at a storage facility pursuant to an order of impoundment or immobilization under subsection (6) where the person impounding the vehicle exercises control, supervision, and responsibility over the vehicle.(d) “Person” means any individual, firm, company, agency, organization, partnership, corporation, association, trust, or other business entity of any kind whatsoever.

unread: Nothing within F.S. 316.193 was left unread on this repair pass. I re-fetched the official 2025 text from flsenate.gov myself and read subsections (1) through (14) start to finish, including all four unnumbered flush paragraphs (the one closing (2)(a), the one closing (3), the one sitting between (4)(b)2. and (4)(c), and the one closing (6)), the History note, and both editor Notes. Every provision in the section now has a row.

F.S. 921.0022 -- NOT read start to finish. I re-fetched it and searched for every occurrence of '316.193' (12 hits), then read the surrounding chart rows and the enclosing LEVEL headers. All six level assignments in this table were independently re-verified this pass against the chart text: (2)(b) 3rd conviction at LEVEL 3 in (3)(c); (2)(b) 4th or subsequent at LEVEL 6 in (3)(f); (3)(c)2. at LEVEL 7 in (3)(g); (3)(c)3.a. at LEVEL 8 in (3)(h); (3)(c)3.b. and (3)(c)3.c. at LEVEL 9 in (3)(i). The remainder of the chart was not read.

F.S. 775.082, 775.083, 775.084 -- not read. Every degree in this table is 'punishable as provided in' these sections, so the actual years and fines behind each degree are unverified here.
F.S. 316.1933 -- not read. Supplies the controlling definition of 'serious bodily injury' for 316.193(3)(c)2.
F.S. 775.021(5) -- not read. Supplies the controlling definition of 'unborn child' for 316.193(3)(c)3.

F.S. 322.292 (DUI program licensure), 893.03 (Schedules I-V), and chapter 397 (substance abuse licensure) -- not read. All three are load-bearing for the mandatory probation, education, evaluation, and treatment conditions in 316.193(5).

F.S. 316.1938 (interlock device approval), 322.28(2)(a)2. and (2)(a)3. (license revocation), 322.2615 (administrative rulings), 316.1937 and 322.2715 (interlock for second or subsequent offenders, expressly overridden by (6)(j)1.), 713.78 (liens for towing and storage, incorporated wholesale by (6)(k)), 28.24 (clerk fees, (6)(l)), 877.111, chapter 893, 744.331, chapter 394, chapter 397, former chapter 396, 856.011(3), and Fla. R. Crim. P. 3.220 -- all cross-referenced by 316.193 and none of them read.

Case law construing any provision in this section -- not consulted. Two questions are unresolved on the face of the statute and would need it: whether the permissive 'may be not less than $2,000' fine floor in 316.193(2)(b)3. is treated as mandatory, and whether the 'only the instant offense' rule in the subsection (4) flush language extends to the minor-passenger trigger, which that sentence does not mention.

LAYOUT CAVEAT, not a skipped provision: the (1)(a) worksheet is a printed grid with blank fill-in cells, arithmetic operators, and column alignment. It was read from the flsenate.gov HTML, which flattens the grid to a linear cell sequence. Every line item, level, point value, operator position and checkbox was read and is captured, but the visual column structure of the form is a reconstruction in the quote fields, not a character-for-character transcription.

rows.trigger: CRITICAL FRAMING. This entire section assigns NO degree of offense to anything and contains NO dollar amounts anywhere (verified by scanning the full operative text, subsection (1)(a) through the History note: zero dollar figures). It is the sentencing-computation statute: scoresheet points, multipliers, and the lowest permissible sentence. Degrees come from the substantive offense statutes; severity levels come from s. 921.0022 and s. 921.0023. Every row below therefore carries degree 'no degree assigned' and null min/max, and no row here may be read as grading any crime.
rows.quote: 921.0024 Criminal Punishment Code; worksheet computations; scoresheets.

rows.trigger: STRUCTURAL WARNING FOR THIS PARAGRAPH, read before any row citing (1)(a). Paragraph (1)(a) is not a single kind of thing. It opens with four point-tier tables (Primary Offense, Additional Offenses, Victim Injury, Prior Record), then continues into a subtotal block of named line items, then a designation block of four yes/no recidivist designations that are NOT point tiers and have NO corresponding entry in the (1)(b) worksheet key, then seven yes/no multiplier checkboxes, then the TOTAL SENTENCE POINTS line. Reading the point tables and stopping captures less than half of (1)(a). Each of those later blocks is given its own row below.
rows.quote: (1)(a) The Criminal Punishment Code worksheet is used to compute the subtotal and total sentence points as follows: FLORIDA CRIMINAL PUNISHMENT CODE WORKSHEET

rows.trigger: OFFENSE SCORE block, first table: Primary Offense. One entry only, scored by the offense severity level of the single primary offense. Note there is NO 'M' (misdemeanor) row in this table, unlike the Additional Offenses and Prior Record tables. Levels are inputs imported from s. 921.0022 / s. 921.0023; this table assigns points, not levels and not degrees.
rows.quote: OFFENSE SCORE. Primary Offense. Level / Sentence Points / Total: 10 = 116; 9 = 92; 8 = 74; 7 = 56; 6 = 36; 5 = 28; 4 = 22; 3 = 16; 2 = 10; 1 = 4. Total ____

rows.trigger: OFFENSE SCORE block, second table: Additional Offenses. Multiplied by a count column, so this table is per-count, unlike Primary Offense. Includes an 'M' row for misdemeanors at 0.2 points each, and fractional values at levels 5 and below.

OFFENSE SCORE block, third table: Victim Injury. Scored by injury category and a number column, not by offense severity level. Note the ordering trap: the two sexual categories sit at the BOTTOM of the table but carry higher values than the severe/moderate/slight categories above them (sexual penetration = 80 outranks severe = 40). A reader who scans the visible top rows and stops will miss them. Also note the top row is its own category, second degree murder-death at 240, the largest single victim injury assessment in the worksheet.
rows.quote: Victim Injury. Level / Sentence Points / Number / Total: 2nd degree murder-death = 240 x ___ ; Death = 120 x ___ ; Severe = 40 x ___ ; Moderate = 18 x ___ ; Slight = 4 x ___ ; Sexual penetration = 80 x ___ ; Sexual contact = 40 x ___ . Total ____

rows.trigger: Arithmetic line closing the OFFENSE SCORE block. Defines TOTAL OFFENSE SCORE as the sum of the three preceding tables. This line was absent from the prior table and is what links the three offense tables to the subtotal block below.
rows.quote: Primary Offense + Additional Offenses + Victim Injury = TOTAL OFFENSE SCORE

rows.trigger: PRIOR RECORD SCORE block, fourth and final point table: Prior Record. Per-count like Additional Offenses, and includes an 'M' row. Values are lower across the board than the Additional Offenses table at the same level (e.g. level 10 prior = 29 vs level 10 additional offense = 58).
rows.quote: PRIOR RECORD SCORE. Prior Record. Level / Sentence Points / Number / Total: 10 = 29 x ___ ; 9 = 23 x ___ ; 8 = 19 x ___ ; 7 = 14 x ___ ; 6 = 9 x ___ ; 5 = 3.6 x ___ ; 4 = 2.4 x ___ ; 3 = 1.6 x ___ ; 2 = 0.8 x ___ ; 1 = 0.5 x ___ ; M = 0.2 x ___ . Total ____

rows.trigger: SUBTOTAL BLOCK of the worksheet face, immediately after the four point tables. Eight named line items feeding the SUBTOTAL line: TOTAL OFFENSE SCORE, TOTAL PRIOR RECORD SCORE, LEGAL STATUS, COMMUNITY SANCTION VIOLATION, PRIOR SERIOUS FELONY, PRIOR CAPITAL FELONY, FIREARM OR SEMIAUTOMATIC WEAPON, then SUBTOTAL. Five of these eight (legal status, community sanction violation, prior serious felony, prior capital felony, firearm/semiautomatic) are the worksheet's carriers for the (1)(b) key provisions; the point values are NOT stated on the face of (1)(a) and must be taken from (1)(b). This block is what the multipliers below operate on: every (1)(b) multiplier multiplies 'the subtotal sentence points', i.e. this SUBTOTAL line, not the total.
rows.quote: TOTAL OFFENSE SCORE ____ ; TOTAL PRIOR RECORD SCORE ____ ; LEGAL STATUS ____ ; COMMUNITY SANCTION VIOLATION ____ ; PRIOR SERIOUS FELONY ____ ; PRIOR CAPITAL FELONY ____ ; FIREARM OR SEMIAUTOMATIC WEAPON ____ ; SUBTOTAL ____

rows.trigger: DESIGNATION BLOCK, first of four. THIS IS THE PROVISION THE PRIOR TABLE MISSED ENTIRELY, and it is the exact pattern the repair exists to catch: (1)(a) opens with dollar-free point tiers and its tail is something else with no tier at all. PRISON RELEASEE REOFFENDER is a yes/no box, not a point entry. It carries NO point value, NO multiplier, and has NO corresponding paragraph in the (1)(b) worksheet key, so a reader working from (1)(b) will never encounter it. Its substance lives in s. 775.082(9), which is NOT fetched here. It sits below the SUBTOTAL line, meaning it is recorded after the point computation and operates outside it.
rows.quote: PRISON RELEASEE REOFFENDER (no)(yes)

rows.trigger: DESIGNATION BLOCK, second of four. Yes/no box, no point value, no multiplier, no corresponding (1)(b) key paragraph. Substance lives in s. 775.084, NOT fetched here. Recorded below the SUBTOTAL line and outside the point computation.
rows.quote: VIOLENT CAREER CRIMINAL (no)(yes)

rows.trigger: DESIGNATION BLOCK, third of four. Yes/no box, no point value, no multiplier, no corresponding (1)(b) key paragraph. Substance lives in s. 775.084, NOT fetched here. Distinct from HABITUAL OFFENDER on the next line; do not collapse the two.
rows.quote: HABITUAL VIOLENT OFFENDER (no)(yes)

rows.trigger: DESIGNATION BLOCK, fourth of four. Yes/no box, no point value, no multiplier, no corresponding (1)(b) key paragraph. Substance lives in s. 775.084, NOT fetched here. This is the last of the four designations; the seven multiplier checkboxes begin on the next line.
rows.quote: HABITUAL OFFENDER (no)(yes)

rows.trigger: MULTIPLIER CHECKBOX BLOCK on the worksheet face, seven yes/no boxes each followed by '(x multiplier)'. These are the worksheet carriers for the (1)(b) multipliers, and the multiplier VALUES are not printed on the face. INDEPENDENT FINDING, not in the auditor's list: (1)(b) contains EIGHT multiplier paragraphs but the (1)(a) face has only SEVEN boxes. The fleeing or attempting to elude multiplier (s. 316.1935, 1.5x) has NO checkbox on the worksheet face. Mapping of the seven that do appear: AGGRAVATED ANIMAL CRUELTY to the s. 828.12(2) multiplier; DRUG TRAFFICKER to the s. 893.135 multiplier; LAW ENF. PROTECT. to the justice-system-personnel multiplier (s. 775.0823 / s. 784.07(3) / s. 775.0875(1)); MOTOR VEHICLE THEFT to the grand theft of a motor vehicle multiplier; CRIMINAL GANG OFFENSE to the s. 874.03 multiplier; DOMESTIC VIOLENCE IN THE PRESENCE OF RELATED CHILD to the s. 741.28 multiplier; ADULT-ON-MINOR SEX OFFENSE to the 2.0x multiplier.
rows.quote: AGGRAVATED ANIMAL CRUELTY (no)(yes) (x multiplier) ; DRUG TRAFFICKER (no)(yes) (x multiplier) ; LAW ENF. PROTECT. (no)(yes) (x multiplier) ; MOTOR VEHICLE THEFT (no)(yes) (x multiplier) ; CRIMINAL GANG OFFENSE (no)(yes) (x multiplier) ; DOMESTIC VIOLENCE IN THE PRESENCE OF RELATED CHILD (no)(yes) (x multiplier) ; ADULT-ON-MINOR SEX OFFENSE (no)(yes) (x multiplier)

rows.trigger: Final line of the (1)(a) worksheet. TOTAL SENTENCE POINTS is positioned AFTER the designation block and after the seven multiplier checkboxes, not immediately after SUBTOTAL. That ordering is substantive: the multipliers in (1)(b) operate on the subtotal, and the product is this total. This is the figure subsection (2) then tests against the 44-point and 363-point thresholds.
rows.quote: TOTAL SENTENCE POINTS ____

rows.trigger: Legal status points. Any form of legal status existing at the time of the offense before the court adds a flat 4 points. Carrier line on the worksheet face is 'LEGAL STATUS' in the subtotal block.
rows.quote: WORKSHEET KEY: Legal status points are assessed when any form of legal status existed at the time the offender committed an offense before the court for sentencing. Four (4) sentence points are assessed for an offender's legal status.

rows.trigger: Community sanction violation before the court: 6 points for each violation and each successive violation. The 6-point figure is the DEFAULT ONLY. The sentence ends in 'unless any of the following apply' and is followed by subparagraphs 1. and 2., which raise it to 12 or 24. Do not quote the 6-point figure without reading both subparagraphs and sub-subparagraphs 2.a. and 2.b.
rows.quote: Community sanction violation points are assessed when a community sanction violation is before the court for sentencing. Six (6) sentence points are assessed for each community sanction violation and each successive community sanction violation, unless any of the following apply:

rows.trigger: First exception to the 6-point default. Community sanction violation that includes a new felony conviction before the sentencing court: 12 points instead of 6, for the violation and each successive such violation. Applies to any offender, no special-concern status required.
rows.quote: 1. If the community sanction violation includes a new felony conviction before the sentencing court, twelve (12) community sanction violation points are assessed for the violation, and for each successive community sanction violation involving a new felony conviction.

rows.trigger: Second exception, first branch. Requires ALL of: offender is a violent felony offender of special concern as defined in s. 948.06; the violation of felony probation or community control does NOT include a new felony conviction (sub-sub I.); AND the violation is not based solely on failure to pay costs, fines, or restitution (sub-sub II.). Conditions I. and II. are conjunctive ('and'). Result is 12 points per violation and each successive violation.
rows.quote: 2. If the community sanction violation is committed by a violent felony offender of special concern as defined in s. 948.06: a. Twelve (12) community sanction violation points are assessed for the violation and for each successive violation of felony probation or community control where: I. The violation does not include a new felony conviction; and II. The community sanction violation is not based solely on the probationer or offender's failure to pay costs or fines or make restitution payments.

rows.trigger: Second exception, second branch, and the highest community sanction violation assessment in the section. Violent felony offender of special concern (s. 948.06) whose violation of felony probation or community control DOES include a new felony conviction: 24 points, per violation and each successive violation. This sub-subparagraph sits after 2.a. and its two sub-subs; a reader who answers the question at 2.a.I. and stops will miss it.
rows.quote: b. Twenty-four (24) community sanction violation points are assessed for the violation and for each successive violation of felony probation or community control where the violation includes a new felony conviction.

rows.trigger: Anti-stacking rule closing the community sanction violation key. Multiple counts of community sanction violations before the sentencing court cannot multiply the assessment. Note the tension with the 'each successive violation' language in the tiers above: successive violations multiply, multiple counts of one violation do not.
rows.quote: Multiple counts of community sanction violations before the sentencing court shall not be a basis for multiplying the assessment of community sanction violation points.

rows.trigger: Prior serious felony points. Requires BOTH a primary or additional offense ranked level 8, 9, or 10 AND one or more prior serious felonies. A SINGLE 30-point assessment, not per prior. Definition sentence adds a recency requirement: the prior must be one the offender is still serving, or whose later of release-from-confinement/supervision/sanction date falls within 3 years before the date the primary or any additional offense was committed. Carrier line on the worksheet face is 'PRIOR SERIOUS FELONY'.
rows.quote: Prior serious felony points: If the offender has a primary offense or any additional offense ranked in level 8, level 9, or level 10, and one or more prior serious felonies, a single assessment of thirty (30) points shall be added. For purposes of this section, a prior serious felony is an offense in the offender's prior record that is ranked in level 8, level 9, or level 10 under s. 921.0022 or s. 921.0023 and for which the offender is serving a sentence of confinement, supervision, or other sanction or for which the offender's date of release from confinement, supervision, or other sanction, whichever is later, is within 3 years before the date the primary offense or any additional offense was committed.

rows.trigger: Prior capital felony points. Not a flat figure: one or more prior capital felonies adds points equal to TWICE the points received for the primary offense and any additional offense, added to the subtotal. Definition sweeps in pleas of nolo contendere or guilty as well as findings of guilt, and out-of-state felonies that are capital there or would be capital if committed in Florida. Carrier line on the worksheet face is 'PRIOR CAPITAL FELONY'.
rows.quote: Prior capital felony points: If the offender has one or more prior capital felonies in the offender's criminal record, points shall be added to the subtotal sentence points of the offender equal to twice the number of points the offender receives for the primary offense and any additional offense. A prior capital felony in the offender's criminal record is a previous capital felony offense for which the offender has entered a plea of nolo contendere or guilty or has been found guilty; or a felony in another jurisdiction which is a capital felony in that jurisdiction, or would be a capital felony if the offense were committed in this state.

rows.trigger: Weapon possession points, TWO tiers in one paragraph, genuinely keyed to the thing possessed. Tier one: 18 points for possessing a firearm as defined in s. 790.001 while committing or attempting any felony OTHER THAN those enumerated in s. 775.087(2). Tier two: 25 points for possessing a semiautomatic firearm as defined in s. 775.087(3) or a machine gun as defined in s. 790.001 while committing or attempting any felony OTHER THAN those enumerated in s. 775.087(3). The second tier follows a semicolon and 'or' mid-paragraph and is easy to lose. Applies to attempts as well as completed felonies, and to mere possession without use. Carrier line on the worksheet face is 'FIREARM OR SEMIAUTOMATIC WEAPON'.
rows.quote: Possession of a firearm, semiautomatic firearm, or machine gun: If the offender is convicted of committing or attempting to commit any felony other than those enumerated in s. 775.087(2) while having in his or her possession: a firearm as defined in s. 790.001, an additional eighteen (18) sentence points are assessed; or if the offender is convicted of committing or attempting to commit any felony other than those enumerated in s. 775.087(3) while having in his or her possession a semiautomatic firearm as defined in s. 775.087(3) or a machine gun as defined in s. 790.001, an additional twenty-five (25) sentence points are assessed.

rows.trigger: Organizing heading that separates the additive point provisions above from the multiplicative provisions below. EIGHT multiplier paragraphs follow this line: aggravated animal cruelty (1.25x), drug trafficking (1.5x, discretionary), justice system personnel (2.5x / 2.0x / 1.5x), grand theft of a motor vehicle (1.5x), fleeing or eluding (1.5x), criminal gang (1.5x), domestic violence in the presence of a child (1.5x), adult-on-minor sex offense (2.0x). Every one of them multiplies the SUBTOTAL sentence points, not the total. Only seven have a checkbox on the (1)(a) worksheet face; fleeing or eluding does not.
rows.quote: Sentencing multipliers:

rows.trigger: Multiplier, aggravated animal cruelty, 1.25x on the subtotal. SCOPE CORRECTED to null: this multiplier turns on the primary offense being a violation of s. 828.12(2) plus a conduct element (knowing and intentional torture or torment that injured, mutilated, or killed the animal). It is not graded by any item taken, possessed, or valued. The s. 379.303 language defines what counts as an 'animal' and carves out agricultural animals and permitted captive wildlife, but that is a definitional exclusion, not an item-based grading tier. Lowest multiplier in the section.
rows.quote: Aggravated Animal Cruelty: If the primary offense is aggravated animal cruelty under s. 828.12(2), which included the knowing and intentional torture or torment of an animal that injured, mutilated, or killed the animal, the subtotal sentence points are multiplied by 1.25. As used in this paragraph, the term "animal" does not include an animal used for agricultural purposes or permitted as captive wildlife as authorized under s. 379.303.

rows.trigger: Multiplier, drug trafficking, 1.5x on the subtotal. Two limits that are easy to skip: the multiplier applies only to a level 7 or level 8 offense, and it is DISCRETIONARY ('at the discretion of the court'), unlike every other multiplier in this key, which are all mandatory in form. Second sentence adds a downward mechanism: the state attorney may move to reduce or suspend for substantial assistance under s. 893.135(4).
rows.quote: Drug trafficking: If the primary offense is drug trafficking under s. 893.135, the subtotal sentence points are multiplied, at the discretion of the court, for a level 7 or level 8 offense, by 1.5. The state attorney may move the sentencing court to reduce or suspend the sentence of a person convicted of a level 7 or level 8 offense, if the offender provides substantial assistance as described in s. 893.135(4).

rows.trigger: Multiplier, violent offenses against specified justice system personnel. THREE separate tiers packed into one paragraph, one per sentence: 2.5x for s. 775.0823(2), (3), or (4); 2.0x for s. 775.0823(5), (6), (7), (8), or (9); 1.5x for s. 784.07(3) or s. 775.0875(1) or s. 775.0823(10) or (11). The 2.5x tier is the largest multiplier anywhere in this section, larger than the 2.0x adult-on-minor multiplier. Stopping at the first sentence loses two thirds of the rule. Note also that no statutory-maximum cap is attached to any of these three tiers, unlike the gang and adult-on-minor multipliers.
rows.quote: Violent offenses committed against specified justice system personnel: If the primary offense is a violation of s. 775.0823(2), (3), or (4), the subtotal sentence points are multiplied by 2.5. If the primary offense is a violation of s. 775.0823(5), (6), (7), (8), or (9), the subtotal sentence points are multiplied by 2.0. If the primary offense is a violation of s. 784.07(3) or s. 775.0875(1), or s. 775.0823(10) or (11), the subtotal sentence points are multiplied by 1.5.

rows.trigger: Multiplier, grand theft of a motor vehicle, 1.5x on the subtotal. Conjunctive: the primary offense must be grand theft of the THIRD DEGREE involving a motor vehicle AND the prior record must contain THREE OR MORE third-degree grand thefts involving a motor vehicle. The degree label 'third degree' is imported from the theft statute; nothing here assigns it. No dollar threshold appears in this provision even though the underlying theft grading is value-based; the multiplier keys off the degree and the count of priors only.
rows.quote: Grand theft of a motor vehicle: If the primary offense is grand theft of the third degree involving a motor vehicle and in the offender's prior record, there are three or more grand thefts of the third degree involving a motor vehicle, the subtotal sentence points are multiplied by 1.5.

rows.trigger: Multiplier, fleeing or attempting to elude, 1.5x on the subtotal. Primary offense must be fleeing or attempting to elude a law enforcement officer, or aggravated fleeing or eluding, under s. 316.1935, plus ONE OR MORE prior s. 316.1935 violations in the record. Only one prior is required, in contrast to the three required by the motor vehicle theft multiplier immediately above. INDEPENDENT FINDING: this is the one multiplier in (1)(b) with NO corresponding checkbox on the (1)(a) worksheet face.
rows.quote: Fleeing or attempting to elude a law enforcement officer: If the primary offense is fleeing or attempting to elude a law enforcement officer or aggravated fleeing or eluding in violation of s. 316.1935, and in the offender's prior record, there is one or more violation of s. 316.1935, the subtotal sentence points are multiplied by 1.5.

rows.trigger: Multiplier, offense related to a criminal gang, 1.5x on the subtotal, where the offense was committed for the purpose of benefiting, promoting, or furthering a criminal gang as defined in s. 874.03. SECOND SENTENCE IS A CAP AND IS EASY TO MISS: if applying the multiplier would push the lowest permissible sentence above the chapter 775 statutory maximum for the primary offense, the court may NOT apply the multiplier and must impose the statutory maximum.
