This runs in the opposite direction from the override in subsection (2), which says a code sentence exceeding the statutory maximum must be imposed; the cap here is specific to this multiplier.
rows.quote: Offense related to a criminal gang: If the offender is convicted of the primary offense and committed that offense for the purpose of benefiting, promoting, or furthering the interests of a criminal gang as defined in s. 874.03, the subtotal sentence points are multiplied by 1.5. If applying the multiplier results in the lowest permissible sentence exceeding the statutory maximum sentence for the primary offense under chapter 775, the court may not apply the multiplier and must sentence the defendant to the statutory maximum sentence.

rows.trigger: Multiplier, domestic violence in the presence of a child, 1.5x on the subtotal. Requires the primary offense to be a crime of domestic violence as defined in s. 741.28, committed in the presence of a child UNDER 16 who is a family or household member as defined in s. 741.28(3) with the victim or perpetrator. NO statutory-maximum cap is attached to this multiplier, unlike the gang and adult-on-minor multipliers. Worksheet face carrier reads 'DOMESTIC VIOLENCE IN THE PRESENCE OF RELATED CHILD'.
rows.quote: Domestic violence in the presence of a child: If the offender is convicted of the primary offense and the primary offense is a crime of domestic violence, as defined in s. 741.28, which was committed in the presence of a child under 16 years of age who is a family or household member as defined in s. 741.28(3) with the victim or perpetrator, the subtotal sentence points are multiplied by 1.5.

rows.trigger: Multiplier, adult-on-minor sex offense, 2.0x on the subtotal, and the last multiplier in the key. Gateway conditions: offender 18 or older, victim under 18 at the time of the primary offense, and the primary offense committed on or after October 1, 2014. The predicate list is a semicolon-separated series with SIX branches, only the first of which carries the extra 'in the course of committing that violation' requirement: (i) s. 787.01(2) or s. 787.02(2) where the victim was a minor and the defendant committed a sexual battery under ch. 794 or a lewd act under s. 800.04 or s. 847.0135(5) against the minor; (ii) s. 787.01(3)(a)2. or 3.; (iii) s. 787.02(3)(a)2. or 3.; (iv) s. 794.011 excluding s. 794.011(10); (v) s. 800.04; (vi) s. 847.0135(5). Branches (ii) through (vi) carry no in-the-course-of element. Final sentence is the same statutory-maximum cap as the gang multiplier.
rows.quote: Adult-on-minor sex offense: If the offender was 18 years of age or older and the victim was younger than 18 years of age at the time the offender committed the primary offense, and if the primary offense was an offense committed on or after October 1, 2014, and is a violation of s. 787.01(2) or s. 787.02(2), if the violation involved a victim who was a minor and, in the course of committing that violation, the defendant committed a sexual battery under chapter 794 or a lewd act under s. 800.04 or s. 847.0135(5) against the minor; s. 787.01(3)(a)2. or 3.; s. 787.02(3)(a)2. or 3.; s. 794.011, excluding s. 794.011(10); s. 800.04; or s. 847.0135(5), the subtotal sentence points are multiplied by 2.0. If applying the multiplier results in the lowest permissible sentence exceeding the statutory maximum sentence for the primary offense under chapter 775, the court may not apply the multiplier and must sentence the defendant to the statutory maximum sentence.

rows.trigger: Total sentence points equal to or less than 44. Prescribes the sanction directly by point score, not by offense degree. Note the discretionary escape hatch in the same sentence: the court may still impose a prison sentence up to the statutory maximum notwithstanding the sub-44 score.
rows.quote: The lowest permissible sentence is the minimum sentence that may be imposed by the trial court, absent a valid reason for departure. The lowest permissible sentence is any nonstate prison sanction in which the total sentence points equals or is less than 44 points, unless the court determines within its discretion that a prison sentence, which may be up to the statutory maximums for the offenses committed, is appropriate.

rows.trigger: Total sentence points exceed 44. Prescribes a term directly by arithmetic formula: subtract 28 from the total points, then reduce the remainder by 25 percent; the result is the lowest permissible sentence expressed in prison months.
rows.quote: When the total sentence points exceeds 44 points, the lowest permissible sentence in prison months shall be calculated by subtracting 28 points from the total sentence points and decreasing the remaining total by 25 percent.

rows.trigger: Defines the top of the permissible range as the statutory maximum under s. 775.082 for the primary offense and any additional offenses before the court, and authorizes concurrent or consecutive sentences. The maximum is imported from s. 775.082, not assigned here. First sentence also limits the role of the point total: it exists only to fix the floor.
rows.quote: The total sentence points shall be calculated only as a means of determining the lowest permissible sentence. The permissible range for sentencing shall be the lowest permissible sentence up to and including the statutory maximum, as defined in s. 775.082, for the primary offense and any additional offenses before the court for sentencing. The sentencing court may impose such sentences concurrently or consecutively.

rows.trigger: Floor on any state prison sentence: it must exceed 1 year. Applies regardless of point score or offense degree. A one-sentence rule sitting between two larger provisions.
rows.quote: However, any sentence to state prison must exceed 1 year.

rows.trigger: OVERRIDE PROVISION, sitting mid-paragraph and easy to miss. When the scoresheet's lowest permissible sentence exceeds the s. 775.082 statutory maximum for the offense, the code sentence controls and must be imposed. The degree of the offense does not cap exposure in that situation. Contrast the multiplier-specific caps in the gang and adult-on-minor paragraphs of (1)(b), which resolve the same conflict the opposite way.
rows.quote: If the lowest permissible sentence under the code exceeds the statutory maximum sentence as provided in s. 775.082, the sentence required by the code must be imposed.

rows.trigger: Total sentence points greater than or equal to 363. Authorizes life imprisonment by point score alone, with no degree named and no lower bound tied to the offense's own grading. Second sentence strips discretionary early release for anyone so sentenced, except executive clemency or conditional medical release under s. 947.149. Last substantive rule in subsection (2).
rows.quote: If the total sentence points are greater than or equal to 363, the court may sentence the offender to life imprisonment. An offender sentenced to life imprisonment under this section is not eligible for any form of discretionary early release, except executive clemency or conditional medical release under s. 947.149.

rows.trigger: Procedural, read in full and recorded for completeness. One digitized scoresheet per defendant, except separate scoresheets when the felonies were committed under more than one version or revision of the guidelines or the code. State attorney prepares; defense counsel reviews for accuracy unless the judge directs otherwise; sentencing judge must approve and sign. No degree and no term assigned.
rows.quote: A single digitized scoresheet shall be prepared for each defendant to determine the permissible range for the sentence that the court may impose, except that if the defendant is before the court for sentencing for more than one felony and the felonies were committed under more than one version or revision of the guidelines or the code, separate digitized scoresheets must be prepared. The scoresheet or scoresheets must cover all the defendant's offenses pending before the court for sentencing. The state attorney shall prepare the digitized scoresheet or scoresheets, which must be presented to the defense counsel for review for accuracy in all cases unless the judge directs otherwise. The defendant's scoresheet or scoresheets must be approved and signed by the sentencing judge.

rows.trigger: Procedural, read in full. Department of Corrections, in consultation with OSCA, state attorneys, and public defenders, submits the revised digitized scoresheet to the Supreme Court by June 15 each year as necessary, and produces approved scoresheets by September 30. Scoresheets must have individual structured data cells per field, plus cells flagging any mandatory minimum imposed and any downward departure. No degree and no term assigned.
rows.quote: The Department of Corrections, in consultation with the Office of the State Courts Administrator, state attorneys, and public defenders, must develop and submit the revised digitized Criminal Punishment Code scoresheet to the Supreme Court for approval by June 15 of each year, as necessary. The digitized scoresheet shall have individual, structured data cells for each data field on the scoresheet. Upon the Supreme Court's approval of the revised digitized scoresheet, the Department of Corrections shall produce and provide the revised digitized scoresheets by September 30 of each year, as necessary. Digitized scoresheets must include individual data cells to indicate whether any prison sentence imposed includes a mandatory minimum sentence or the sentence imposed was a downward departure from the lowest permissible sentence under the Criminal Punishment Code.

rows.trigger: Procedural, read in full. DOC must make the digitized scoresheets available to those responsible for preparing them. No degree and no term assigned.
rows.quote: The Department of Corrections shall make available the digitized Criminal Punishment Code scoresheets to those persons charged with the responsibility for preparing scoresheets.

rows.trigger: Procedural, read in full. Clerk of the circuit court transmits a complete and accurate digitized copy of each sentencing scoresheet to DOC, electronically, no less than monthly by the first of each month, and may send them collectively. No degree and no term assigned.
rows.quote: The clerk of the circuit court shall transmit a complete and accurate digitized copy of the Criminal Punishment Code scoresheet used in each sentencing proceeding to the Department of Corrections. Scoresheets must be electronically transmitted no less frequently than monthly, by the first of each month, and may be sent collectively.

rows.trigger: Procedural, read in full, and the last operative subsection. A digitized sentencing scoresheet must be prepared for EVERY defendant sentenced for a felony offense, and it plus any attachments prepared under Fla. R. Crim. P. 3.701, 3.702, 3.703, or any other applicable rule, must accompany the uniform judgment and sentence form provided to DOC. No degree and no term assigned.
rows.quote: A digitized sentencing scoresheet must be prepared for every defendant who is sentenced for a felony offense. The individual offender's digitized Criminal Punishment Code scoresheet and any attachments thereto prepared pursuant to Rule 3.701, Rule 3.702, or Rule 3.703, Florida Rules of Criminal Procedure, or any other rule pertaining to the preparation and submission of felony sentencing scoresheets, must be included with the uniform judgment and sentence form provided to the Department of Corrections.

rows.trigger: History note, recorded rather than merely asserted as read. Not degree-assigning and not operative text. Twenty-four amendments from 1997 to 2025. Currency check: the two most recent are s. 3, ch. 2025-75 and s. 3, ch. 2025-102, which confirms this is the 2025 version and that the section was amended twice in the 2025 session. Anything relying on a pre-2025 copy of this worksheet is stale.

817.568.title: Criminal use of personal identification information
unread: s. 921.0022 offense severity ranking chart -- NOT OPENED AT ALL in this repair pass. The level values 4 ((2)(a)), 5 ((2)(b) rows), 8 ((6)), and 9 ((7)) are carried over unverified from the table I was repairing; treat them as unconfirmed. The only levels I can support from text I actually read are the level 2 rankings for reclassified misdemeanors, which appear in the express ranking sentences at the end of subsections (5) and (10) themselves.
s. 921.0023 (referenced in subsection (10) for ranking of reclassified offenses) -- not read.

s. 775.082, s. 775.083, s. 775.084 -- the actual terms of imprisonment, fines, and habitual-offender enhancements behind every 'punishable as provided in' clause. Not read. Every degree in this table converts to a term only through these sections.
Chapter 921 Criminal Punishment Code generally (referenced in subsections (3), (5), and (10)) -- not read.
s. 119.011 (definition of 'public record' that triggers the subsection (5) reclassification) -- not read.

s. 825.101 ('disabled adult'), s. 838.014 ('public servant'), s. 1.01 ('veteran' and, via s. 1.01(3), 'person'), s. 125.01045 ('first responder') -- the four definitions that set the reach of subsection (11). Not read.
s. 943.0412 and s. 775.089 (surcharge distribution under subsection (12) and restitution under subsection (15)) -- not read.
Chapter 944 incentive gain-time provisions referenced in subsection (5) -- not read.
s. 775.15 or whatever other general limitations provision supplies the period for subsections (8), (9), (10), and (11), which subsection (19) does not name -- not read.
s. 817.5685 and neighboring sections of ch. 817 -- not read; a related offense could carry different exposure for the same conduct.

Case law construing any provision, including any decision on whether the (2)(b) and (2)(c) count prongs may be charged without proof of pecuniary benefit, and the session laws in the History note (s. 1, ch. 99-335 through s. 5, ch. 2021-5) -- not read.

Scope note, not an unread source: I read every word of 817.568(1) through (19) and the History line as published for the 2025 statutes, and every quote in this table was string-verified against that fetch. Subsections (13), (14), (15), (16), (17), and (18), which the audit found missing from both the prior table and its unread list, are now recorded as rows.

rows.trigger: BASE OFFENSE WITH NO DOLLAR FLOOR AND NO VICTIM-COUNT FLOOR. min is null because value is not an element at all, not because the range starts at zero. Willful, unauthorized fraudulent use of another living person's personal identification information without consent. Critically, this paragraph is also violated by mere POSSESSION WITH INTENT to fraudulently use -- no use, no completed fraud, and no loss of any amount is required. A $0 case is a third degree felony.
rows.quote: Any person who willfully and without authorization fraudulently uses, or possesses with intent to fraudulently use, personal identification information concerning another person without first obtaining that person’s consent, commits the offense of fraudulent use of personal identification information, which is a felony of the third degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.trigger: ONE OF TWO INDEPENDENT PRONGS IN PARAGRAPH (2)(b). This row is the DOLLAR prong only: pecuniary benefit, value of services received, payment sought to be avoided, or amount of injury or fraud of $5,000 or more. max is null because the paragraph states NO upper dollar bound. A defendant who nets $500,000 from one victim still literally satisfies this prong; the $50,000 figure in (2)(c) is a floor for a higher paragraph, not a ceiling on this one, and any ceiling here would be fabricated. Unlike (2)(a), this paragraph requires actual fraudulent USE -- possession with intent does not reach it. See the separate (2)(b) COUNT PRONG row, which has no dollar element at all.
rows.quote: Any person who willfully and without authorization fraudulently uses personal identification information concerning a person without first obtaining that person’s consent commits a felony of the second degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084, if the pecuniary benefit, the value of the services received, the payment sought to be avoided, or the amount of the injury or fraud perpetrated is $5,000 or more or if the person fraudulently uses the personal identification information of 10 or more persons, but fewer than 20 persons, without their consent.

rows.trigger: THE PRONG THAT GETS MISSED. Paragraph (2)(b) is satisfied, wholly independently of any dollar amount, by fraudulent use of the personal identification information of 10 OR MORE BUT FEWER THAN 20 PERSONS. min and max are BOTH null and that is the point: 12 victims with ZERO pecuniary benefit is a SECOND DEGREE FELONY carrying a 3-year mandatory minimum. Anyone who evaluates (2)(b) against a $5,000 floor will read a $0 twelve-victim case as, at most, a (2)(a) third degree felony. That is wrong by two degrees and by three years of mandatory prison.
rows.quote: Any person who willfully and without authorization fraudulently uses personal identification information concerning a person without first obtaining that person’s consent commits a felony of the second degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084, if the pecuniary benefit, the value of the services received, the payment sought to be avoided, or the amount of the injury or fraud perpetrated is $5,000 or more or if the person fraudulently uses the personal identification information of 10 or more persons, but fewer than 20 persons, without their consent.

rows.trigger: TRAILING SENTENCE INSIDE PARAGRAPH (2)(b) THAT PRESCRIBES A TERM DIRECTLY WITHOUT NAMING A DEGREE. It attaches to EVERY conviction under (2)(b) -- the words are 'the offense described in this paragraph', which includes a conviction resting purely on the 10-to-19-victim count prong with no dollar loss. min and max are null for exactly that reason: a $0 conviction under this paragraph carries the 3-year mandatory minimum. Anyone who reads only the degree sentence of (2)(b) and stops will understate this exposure as an ordinary probationable second degree felony. Subsection (13) is the only route to relief from it.
rows.quote: Notwithstanding any other provision of law, the court shall sentence any person convicted of committing the offense described in this paragraph to a mandatory minimum sentence of 3 years’ imprisonment.

rows.trigger: DOLLAR prong of paragraph (2)(c): $50,000 or more, with NO UPPER BOUND. Not found in the s. 921.0022 ranking chart as recorded in the source table, so level is null rather than guessed. See the separate (2)(c) COUNT PRONG row, which reaches this same first degree felony with no dollar element whatsoever.
rows.quote: Any person who willfully and without authorization fraudulently uses personal identification information concerning a person without first obtaining that person’s consent commits a felony of the first degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084, if the pecuniary benefit, the value of the services received, the payment sought to be avoided, or the amount of the injury or fraud perpetrated is $50,000 or more or if the person fraudulently uses the personal identification information of 20 or more persons, but fewer than 30 persons, without their consent.

rows.trigger: INDEPENDENT COUNT PRONG WITH NO DOLLAR ELEMENT. Fraudulent use of the personal identification information of 20 OR MORE BUT FEWER THAN 30 PERSONS is a FIRST DEGREE FELONY at ANY dollar value, including zero, and carries the 5-year mandatory minimum in the next sentence. min and max are null. A guard that only reaches (2)(c) above $50,000 makes a 25-victim, $0 case invisible.
rows.quote: Any person who willfully and without authorization fraudulently uses personal identification information concerning a person without first obtaining that person’s consent commits a felony of the first degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084, if the pecuniary benefit, the value of the services received, the payment sought to be avoided, or the amount of the injury or fraud perpetrated is $50,000 or more or if the person fraudulently uses the personal identification information of 20 or more persons, but fewer than 30 persons, without their consent.

rows.trigger: Prescribes a term directly without naming a degree. It attaches to EVERY (2)(c) conviction, including one resting solely on the 20-to-29-victim count prong with no dollar loss, so min and max are null. Only subsection (13) can reduce or suspend it.
rows.quote: Notwithstanding any other provision of law, the court shall sentence any person convicted of committing the offense described in this paragraph to a mandatory minimum sentence of 5 years’ imprisonment.

rows.trigger: A SECOND, HIGHER THRESHOLD BURIED IN THE LAST SENTENCE OF PARAGRAPH (2)(c), numbered by nothing. $100,000 or more, with NO UPPER BOUND, raises the mandatory minimum from 5 years to 10 years. The degree remains first degree felony -- this sentence names no degree, it prescribes a term -- so a reader tracking only degrees records the $50,000 tier and stops. See the companion count-prong row: 30 or more persons triggers the same 10 years at any dollar value.
rows.quote: If the pecuniary benefit, the value of the services received, the payment sought to be avoided, or the amount of the injury or fraud perpetrated is $100,000 or more, or if the person fraudulently uses the personal identification information of 30 or more persons without their consent, notwithstanding any other provision of law, the court shall sentence any person convicted of committing the offense described in this paragraph to a mandatory minimum sentence of 10 years’ imprisonment.

rows.trigger: THE 10-YEAR MANDATORY MINIMUM IS ALSO TRIGGERED, WHOLLY INDEPENDENTLY OF MONEY, BY 30 OR MORE PERSONS. min and max are null. Thirty victims and $0 of proven loss is a first degree felony with a 10-year mandatory minimum. There is no upper bound on victim count either -- (2)(c) is the top of both ladders. This is the single easiest provision in the section to miss, because it sits in the third sentence of a paragraph whose first sentence already answered the degree question.
rows.quote: If the pecuniary benefit, the value of the services received, the payment sought to be avoided, or the amount of the injury or fraud perpetrated is $100,000 or more, or if the person fraudulently uses the personal identification information of 30 or more persons without their consent, notwithstanding any other provision of law, the court shall sentence any person convicted of committing the offense described in this paragraph to a mandatory minimum sentence of 10 years’ imprisonment.

rows.trigger: Assigns no degree but governs how the (2)(b) and (2)(c) mandatory minimums interact with the Criminal Punishment Code. Recorded because it defeats the natural assumption that a scoresheet or a statutory maximum caps the mandatory minimum: THE MANDATORY MINIMUM MUST BE IMPOSED EVEN IF IT EXCEEDS THE MAXIMUM otherwise authorized under s. 775.082, s. 775.084, or chapter 921. It also expressly preserves the court's power to go higher. Note it names only (2)(b) and (2)(c); it says nothing about the parallel (8)(b) and (8)(c) mandatory minimums.
rows.quote: Neither paragraph (2)(b) nor paragraph (2)(c) prevents a court from imposing a greater sentence of incarceration as authorized by law. If the minimum mandatory terms of imprisonment imposed under paragraph (2)(b) or paragraph (2)(c) exceed the maximum sentences authorized under s. 775.082, s. 775.084, or the Criminal Punishment Code under chapter 921, the mandatory minimum sentence must be imposed. If the mandatory minimum terms of imprisonment under paragraph (2)(b) or paragraph (2)(c) are less than the sentence that could be imposed under s. 775.082, s. 775.084, or the Criminal Punishment Code under chapter 921, the sentence imposed by the court must include the mandatory minimum term of imprisonment as required by paragraph (2)(b) or paragraph (2)(c).

rows.trigger: Harassment purpose, not fraud purpose. Value is irrelevant; min and max are null because no dollar amount is an element. Reaches POSSESSES, USES, OR ATTEMPTS TO USE -- an attempt alone completes the offense. 'Harass' is narrowed by the definition in (1)(c), which excludes accepted commercial purposes and constitutionally protected conduct such as organized protests. This is the only base offense in the section that is a misdemeanor, and subsections (5)(a) and (10)(a) can each convert it to a third degree felony.
rows.quote: Any person who willfully and without authorization possesses, uses, or attempts to use personal identification information concerning a person without first obtaining that person’s consent, and who does so for the purpose of harassing that person, commits the offense of harassment by use of personal identification information, which is a misdemeanor of the first degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082 or s. 775.083.

rows.trigger: RECLASSIFICATION, NOT A STANDALONE OFFENSE. Applies when ANY offense prohibited under this section was facilitated or furthered by use of a public record as defined in s. 119.011. Converts the (4) harassment first degree misdemeanor into a third degree felony. Level 2 is taken from the express ranking sentence at the end of subsection (5), which I read in the operative text, not from the s. 921.0022 chart.
rows.quote: If an offense prohibited under this section was facilitated or furthered by the use of a public record, as defined in s. 119.011, the offense is reclassified to the next higher degree as follows: ... (a) A misdemeanor of the first degree is reclassified as a felony of the third degree.

rows.trigger: Reclassification. Any third degree felony under this section -- (2)(a), (8)(a), or (9) -- becomes a second degree felony when facilitated or furthered by use of a public record. Level is null because the reclassified rank is defined as one level above the base offense's s. 921.0022 ranking, and the three possible base offenses do not share a single ranking.
rows.quote: (b) A felony of the third degree is reclassified as a felony of the second degree. ... For purposes of sentencing under chapter 921 and incentive gain-time eligibility under chapter 944, a felony offense that is reclassified under this subsection is ranked one level above the ranking under s. 921.0022 of the felony offense committed, and a misdemeanor offense that is reclassified under this subsection is ranked in level 2 of the offense severity ranking chart in s. 921.0022.

rows.trigger: Reclassification. Any second degree felony under this section -- (2)(b) on either prong, (6), (7), (8)(b) on either prong, or (11) -- becomes a first degree felony when facilitated or furthered by use of a public record. NOTE THE GAP: subsection (5) provides no reclassification for an offense that is already a first degree felony ((2)(c) or (8)(c)); the ladder in (5) stops at (c), unlike subsection (10), which continues to a life felony.
rows.quote: (c) A felony of the second degree is reclassified as a felony of the first degree.

rows.trigger: VICTIM-STATUS OFFENSE WITH NO DOLLAR ELEMENT AT ALL. min and max are null and that is critical: a single fraudulent use of the personal identification information of a person under 18, or of a person 60 or older, is a SECOND DEGREE FELONY regardless of amount -- a $1 case carries the same degree as a $5,000 case under (2)(b) and jumps four severity levels above the (2)(a) base. Level 8 is carried over from a prior reading of the s. 921.0022 chart and was NOT verified in this pass.
rows.quote: Any person who willfully and without authorization fraudulently uses personal identification information concerning an individual who is younger than 18 years of age or 60 years of age or older without first obtaining the consent of that individual or of his or her legal guardian commits a felony of the second degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.trigger: No dollar element. Aggravated by the defendant's custodial relationship to a victim under 18 or 60 or older: parent, legal guardian, or anyone otherwise exercising custodial authority. Note the mens rea here omits 'without authorization' and omits any lack-of-consent element -- it requires only willful and fraudulent use. Level 9 is carried over from a prior reading of the s. 921.0022 chart and was NOT verified in this pass.
rows.quote: Any person who is in the relationship of parent or legal guardian, or who otherwise exercises custodial authority over an individual who is younger than 18 years of age or 60 years of age or older, who willfully and fraudulently uses personal identification information of that individual commits a felony of the second degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.trigger: NO DOLLAR FLOOR. Parallel base offense for the personal identification information of a DECEASED INDIVIDUAL OR A DISSOLVED BUSINESS ENTITY -- note that (1)(d) defines 'individual' to exclude corporations and partnerships, so this subsection is the only route to entity victims. Reaches possession with intent to fraudulently use, so no completed use and no loss is required. No consent element, since there is no one to consent.
rows.quote: Any person who willfully and fraudulently uses, or possesses with intent to fraudulently use, personal identification information concerning a deceased individual or dissolved business entity commits the offense of fraudulent use or possession with intent to use personal identification information of a deceased individual or dissolved business entity, a felony of the third degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.trigger: DOLLAR prong only: $5,000 or more. max is null -- the paragraph states no upper bound, and the $50,000 figure in (8)(c) is a floor for a higher paragraph, not a ceiling here. Requires actual fraudulent use, not possession. See the separate (8)(b) COUNT PRONG row.
rows.quote: Any person who willfully and fraudulently uses personal identification information concerning a deceased individual or dissolved business entity commits a felony of the second degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084, if the pecuniary benefit, the value of the services received, the payment sought to be avoided, or the amount of injury or fraud perpetrated is $5,000 or more, or if the person fraudulently uses the personal identification information of 10 or more but fewer than 20 deceased individuals or dissolved business entities.

rows.trigger: INDEPENDENT COUNT PRONG, NO DOLLAR ELEMENT. Fraudulent use of the personal identification information of 10 OR MORE BUT FEWER THAN 20 DECEASED INDIVIDUALS OR DISSOLVED BUSINESS ENTITIES is a SECOND DEGREE FELONY at ANY value including zero, and carries the 3-year mandatory minimum in the next sentence. min and max are null. This is the deceased-victim twin of the (2)(b) count-prong trap.
rows.quote: Any person who willfully and fraudulently uses personal identification information concerning a deceased individual or dissolved business entity commits a felony of the second degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084, if the pecuniary benefit, the value of the services received, the payment sought to be avoided, or the amount of injury or fraud perpetrated is $5,000 or more, or if the person fraudulently uses the personal identification information of 10 or more but fewer than 20 deceased individuals or dissolved business entities.

rows.trigger: Trailing sentence prescribing a term without naming a degree: a 3-year MANDATORY MINIMUM on every (8)(b) conviction, including one resting solely on the 10-to-19-entity count prong with no dollar loss. Both bounds null for that reason. Note that subsection (3), which forces mandatory minimums past the Criminal Punishment Code maximum, names only (2)(b) and (2)(c) and does not mention this one.
rows.quote: Notwithstanding any other provision of law, the court shall sentence any person convicted of committing the offense described in this paragraph to a mandatory minimum sentence of 3 years’ imprisonment.

rows.trigger: DOLLAR prong only: $50,000 or more with NO UPPER BOUND. Named offense: aggravated fraudulent use of the personal identification information of multiple deceased individuals or dissolved business entities. See the separate (8)(c) COUNT PRONG row.
rows.quote: Any person who willfully and fraudulently uses personal identification information concerning a deceased individual or dissolved business entity commits the offense of aggravated fraudulent use of the personal identification information of multiple deceased individuals or dissolved business entities, a felony of the first degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084, if the pecuniary benefit, the value of the services received, the payment sought to be avoided, or the amount of injury or fraud perpetrated is $50,000 or more, or if the person fraudulently uses the personal identification information of 20 or more but fewer than 30 deceased individuals or dissolved business entities.

rows.trigger: INDEPENDENT COUNT PRONG, NO DOLLAR ELEMENT. 20 OR MORE BUT FEWER THAN 30 deceased individuals or dissolved business entities is a FIRST DEGREE FELONY at any value including zero, carrying the 5-year minimum mandatory in the next sentence. min and max are null.
rows.quote: Any person who willfully and fraudulently uses personal identification information concerning a deceased individual or dissolved business entity commits the offense of aggravated fraudulent use of the personal identification information of multiple deceased individuals or dissolved business entities, a felony of the first degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084, if the pecuniary benefit, the value of the services received, the payment sought to be avoided, or the amount of injury or fraud perpetrated is $50,000 or more, or if the person fraudulently uses the personal identification information of 20 or more but fewer than 30 deceased individuals or dissolved business entities.

rows.trigger: Prescribes a term without naming a degree: a 5-year minimum mandatory on every (8)(c) conviction, including a zero-dollar count-prong conviction, so both bounds are null. The statute says 'minimum mandatory' here where the parallel (2)(c) says 'mandatory minimum'; the wording differs and is recorded verbatim.
rows.quote: Notwithstanding any other provision of law, the court shall sentence any person convicted of the offense described in this paragraph to a minimum mandatory sentence of 5 years’ imprisonment.

rows.trigger: SECOND HIDDEN THRESHOLD IN THE LAST SENTENCE OF (8)(c), the deceased-victim twin of the (2)(c) trap. $100,000 or more, with NO UPPER BOUND, raises the mandatory minimum to 10 years. No degree is named; the degree remains first degree felony under (8)(c). Stopping at the $50,000 sentence of this paragraph understates exposure by five years of mandatory time.
rows.quote: If the pecuniary benefit, the value of the services received, the payment sought to be avoided, or the amount of the injury or fraud perpetrated is $100,000 or more, or if the person fraudulently uses the personal identification information of 30 or more deceased individuals or dissolved business entities, notwithstanding any other provision of law, the court shall sentence any person convicted of an offense described in this paragraph to a mandatory minimum sentence of 10 years’ imprisonment.

rows.trigger: The 10-year mandatory minimum is ALSO triggered, independently of money, by 30 OR MORE deceased individuals or dissolved business entities. min and max are null: thirty dissolved-entity identities and $0 of proven loss carries a 10-year mandatory minimum. No upper bound on count either.
rows.quote: If the pecuniary benefit, the value of the services received, the payment sought to be avoided, or the amount of the injury or fraud perpetrated is $100,000 or more, or if the person fraudulently uses the personal identification information of 30 or more deceased individuals or dissolved business entities, notwithstanding any other provision of law, the court shall sentence any person convicted of an offense described in this paragraph to a mandatory minimum sentence of 10 years’ imprisonment.

rows.trigger: NO DOLLAR ELEMENT AND NO REAL VICTIM REQUIRED. Reaches counterfeit or fictitious personal identification information concerning a FICTITIOUS PERSON as well as a real person, so synthetic identity conduct is a third degree felony even though no actual human is harmed. Reaches CREATES or USES or POSSESSES WITH INTENT TO USE. 'Counterfeit or fictitious personal identification information' is defined in (1)(g) by a reasonably-prudent-person standard. Requires intent to commit or facilitate a fraud on another person.
rows.quote: Any person who willfully and fraudulently creates or uses, or possesses with intent to fraudulently use, counterfeit or fictitious personal identification information concerning a fictitious person, or concerning a real person without first obtaining that real person’s consent, with intent to use such counterfeit or fictitious personal identification information for the purpose of committing or facilitating the commission of a fraud on another person, commits the offense of fraudulent creation or use, or possession with intent to fraudulently use, counterfeit or fictitious personal identification information, a felony of the third degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.trigger: RECLASSIFICATION, NOT A STANDALONE OFFENSE. Triggered when the defendant, for the purpose of obtaining or using personal identification information, misrepresents himself or herself as a law enforcement officer; an employee or representative of a bank, credit card company, credit counseling company, or credit reporting agency; or wrongfully represents that he or she is seeking to help the victim with a credit-history problem. Converts the (4) misdemeanor into a third degree felony. Level 2 is taken from the express ranking sentence at the end of subsection (10), which I read in the operative text.
rows.quote: Any person who commits an offense described in this section and for the purpose of obtaining or using personal identification information misrepresents himself or herself to be a law enforcement officer; an employee or representative of a bank, credit card company, credit counseling company, or credit reporting agency; or any person who wrongfully represents that he or she is seeking to assist the victim with a problem with the victim’s credit history shall have the offense reclassified as follows: ... (a) In the case of a misdemeanor, the offense is reclassified as a felony of the third degree.

rows.trigger: Reclassification of any third degree felony under this section to a second degree felony on the impersonation trigger. Level null: the statute ranks it one level above the base offense's s. 921.0022 or s. 921.0023 ranking, and the possible base offenses do not share one ranking.
rows.quote: (b) In the case of a felony of the third degree, the offense is reclassified as a felony of the second degree. ... For purposes of sentencing under chapter 921, a felony offense that is reclassified under this subsection is ranked one level above the ranking under s. 921.0022 or s. 921.0023 of the felony offense committed, and a misdemeanor offense that is reclassified under this subsection is ranked in level 2 of the offense severity ranking chart.

rows.trigger: Reclassification of any second degree felony under this section -- (2)(b) on either prong, (6), (7), (8)(b) on either prong, or (11) -- to a first degree felony on the impersonation trigger.
rows.quote: (c) In the case of a felony of the second degree, the offense is reclassified as a felony of the first degree.

rows.trigger: THE SINGLE HIGHEST EXPOSURE IN THIS SECTION AND THE LAST SUBPARAGRAPH OF THE SUBSECTION -- exactly the position where a reader who found the answer at (a), (b), or (c) stops. A first degree felony under this section, or a first degree felony punishable by life, becomes a LIFE FELONY when the impersonation trigger applies. So a (2)(c) or (8)(c) case in which the defendant posed as a bank representative or a police officer is not a 30-year first degree felony but a life felony. Because the (2)(c) and (8)(c) count prongs carry no dollar element, this life-felony exposure is reachable at $0 with 20 or more victims. Subsection (5) has no equivalent top rung; only (10) reaches this degree.
rows.quote: (d) In the case of a felony of the first degree or a felony of the first degree punishable by a term of imprisonment not exceeding life, the offense is reclassified as a life felony.

rows.trigger: NO DOLLAR ELEMENT WHATSOEVER -- a single unauthorized fraudulent use of one protected person's information is a second degree felony no matter how small the amount. The protected classes are broad and largely non-obvious: an individual 60 or older; a disabled adult as defined in s. 825.101; a public servant as defined in s. 838.014; a veteran as defined in s. 1.01; a first responder as defined in s. 125.01045; any individual employed by the State of Florida; and any individual employed by the Federal Government. The 60-or-older branch overlaps subsection (6). I did not read the four incorporated definitions, so the outer boundary of each class is unverified.
rows.quote: A person who willfully and without authorization fraudulently uses personal identification information concerning an individual who is 60 years of age or older; a disabled adult as defined in s. 825.101; a public servant as defined in s. 838.014; a veteran as defined in s. 1.01; a first responder as defined in s. 125.01045; an individual who is employed by the State of Florida; or an individual who is employed by the Federal Government without first obtaining the consent of that individual commits a felony of the second degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.trigger: Assigns no degree but imposes a monetary consequence on EVERY conviction under this section, including a withhold of adjudication and including a plea of nolo contendere: a mandatory $1,001 surcharge that THE COURT MAY NOT WAIVE, on top of any fine under s. 775.083 and any restitution under s. 775.089. Recorded because it attaches to every offense row above, including the (4) misdemeanor.
rows.quote: In addition to any sanction imposed when a person pleads guilty or nolo contendere to, or is found guilty of, regardless of adjudication, a violation of this section, the court shall impose a surcharge of $1,001. ... (d) The surcharge may not be waived by the court. In the event that the person has been ordered to pay restitution in accordance with s. 775.089, the surcharge shall be included in a judgment.

rows.trigger: SUBSTANTIAL ASSISTANCE. Assigns no degree but is the ONLY provision in this section capable of defeating the 3-, 5-, and 10-year mandatory minimums in (2)(b), (2)(c), (8)(b), and (8)(c), which subsection (3) otherwise makes unavoidable. The court may REDUCE OR SUSPEND the sentence of any person convicted of a violation of this section who provides substantial assistance in the identification, arrest, or conviction of accomplices, accessories, coconspirators, principals, or any other person engaged in fraudulent possession or use of personal identification information. Two structural limits worth noting: the motion is the PROSECUTOR'S to make, not the defendant's, and the judge MAY but need not grant it. The arresting agency gets a hearing in aggravation or mitigation, and on good cause the motion may be filed and heard in camera. Applies to every row in this table, at any dollar value and any victim count.
rows.quote: The prosecutor may move the sentencing court to reduce or suspend the sentence of any person who is convicted of a violation of this section and who provides substantial assistance in the identification, arrest, or conviction of any of that person’s accomplices, accessories, coconspirators, or principals or of any other person engaged in fraudulent possession or use of personal identification information. The arresting agency shall be given an opportunity to be heard in aggravation or mitigation in reference to any such motion. Upon good cause shown, the motion may be filed and heard in camera. The judge hearing the motion may reduce or suspend the sentence if the judge finds that the defendant rendered such substantial assistance.

rows.trigger: COMPLETE EXEMPTION FROM THE ENTIRE SECTION, not a defense to one subsection. Every offense row above is stated without this carve-out and must be read subject to it. Lawfully authorized investigative, protective, or intelligence activity of a law enforcement agency of this state or its political subdivisions, of ANY OTHER STATE or its political subdivisions, or of the FEDERAL GOVERNMENT or its political subdivisions is outside the section entirely. The exemption runs to the agency activity and requires that the activity be lawfully authorized.
rows.quote: This section does not prohibit any lawfully authorized investigative, protective, or intelligence activity of a law enforcement agency of this state or any of its political subdivisions, of any other state or its political subdivisions, or of the Federal Government or its political subdivisions.

rows.trigger: Assigns no degree but expands monetary exposure beyond the $1,001 surcharge in (12) and beyond ordinary out-of-pocket loss: restitution under s. 775.089 may include the victim's ATTORNEY'S FEES for clearing a credit history or credit rating and costs of civil or administrative proceedings to undo debts and liens created by the defendant. Because the restitution measure is not the same as the pecuniary-benefit element that sets the degree, a low-dollar or zero-dollar count-prong conviction can still carry substantial restitution. Paragraph (b) also authorizes orders correcting false public records.
rows.quote: (a) In sentencing a defendant convicted of an offense under this section, the court may order that the defendant make restitution under s. 775.089 to any victim of the offense. In addition to the victim’s out-of-pocket costs, restitution may include payment of any other costs, including attorney’s fees incurred by the victim in clearing the victim’s credit history or credit rating, or any costs incurred in connection with any civil or administrative proceeding to satisfy any debt, lien, or other obligation of the victim arising as the result of the actions of the defendant. (b) The sentencing court may issue such orders as are necessary to correct any public record that contains false information given in violation of this section.

rows.trigger: Assigns no degree. Recorded for completeness of the section rather than as a source of exposure: charging authority is not limited to the local state attorney, so the statewide prosecutor may bring a multi-circuit case. Relevant in practice to the multi-victim count prongs, which typically span circuits.
rows.quote: Prosecutions for violations of this section may be brought on behalf of the state by any state attorney or by the statewide prosecutor.

rows.trigger: Assigns no degree. Legislative finding that fixes, absent contrary evidence, the situs of consent or non-consent at the county where the victim generally resides. Recorded because it feeds the venue rule in (18); no degree, no dollar bounds.
rows.quote: The Legislature finds that, in the absence of evidence to the contrary, the location where a victim gives or fails to give consent to the use of personal identification information is the county where the victim generally resides.

rows.trigger: Assigns no degree. Venue in ANY county in which an element occurred, expressly including the county where the victim generally resides. Recorded for completeness; it does not change degree or dollar bounds.
rows.quote: Notwithstanding any other provision of law, venue for the prosecution and trial of violations of this section may be commenced and maintained in any county in which an element of the offense occurred, including the county where the victim generally resides.

rows.trigger: Assigns no degree. Statute of limitations, recorded because it is a limit on exposure rather than a source of it, and because its reach is partial in a way easily misread: the 3-year period with the discovery extension applies ONLY to prosecutions under subsection (2), subsection (6), or subsection (7). Subsections (8), (9), (10), and (11) are NOT named, so their limitation periods come from elsewhere in the law and are not established by this section. Ambiguity noted rather than resolved -- I did not read the general limitations statute.
rows.quote: A prosecution of an offense prohibited under subsection (2), subsection (6), or subsection (7) must be commenced within 3 years after the offense occurred. However, a prosecution may be commenced within 1 year after discovery of the offense by an aggrieved party, or by a person who has a legal duty to represent the aggrieved party and who is not a party to the offense, if such prosecution is commenced within 5 years after the violation occurred.

775.082.title: Penalties; applicability of sentencing structures; mandatory minimum sentences for certain reoffenders previously released from prison.

rows.trigger: NOT VALUE-TRIGGERED (no dollar, quantity, or weight element anywhere in s. 775.082; every null min/max in this table means 'value is not an element,' not 'range starts at zero'). Trigger is conviction of a capital felony, subject to the s. 921.141 penalty proceeding. Expressly subordinate to paragraph (1)(b) ('Except as provided in paragraph (b)'), which removes juvenile offenders from this rule entirely. Where death is not returned, the sentence is life WITHOUT parole eligibility.
rows.quote: Except as provided in paragraph (b), a person who has been convicted of a capital felony shall be punished by death if the proceeding held to determine sentence according to the procedure set forth in s. 921.141 results in a determination that such person shall be punished by death, otherwise such person shall be punished by life imprisonment and shall be ineligible for parole.

rows.trigger: NOT VALUE-TRIGGERED. Narrowed by (i) offense committed before the person attained 18 years of age, (ii) conviction under s. 782.04 of a capital felony or an offense reclassified as a capital felony, and (iii) the person actually killed, intended to kill, or attempted to kill the victim. SCOPE IS NULL, AND THAT IS A CORRECTION: the prior table tagged this row scope='prior'. There is NO prior-record, recidivist, or criminal-history element here. The narrowing facts are the defendant's age at the offense and his or her killing role. Tagging it 'prior' makes a MITIGATING juvenile-sentencing provision indistinguishable from an AGGRAVATING recidivist enhancement -- a sign flip for any consumer filtering on scope. Floor of 40 years if life is found inappropriate.
rows.quote: A person who actually killed, intended to kill, or attempted to kill the victim and who is convicted under s. 782.04 of a capital felony, or an offense that was reclassified as a capital felony, which was committed before the person attained 18 years of age shall be punished by a term of imprisonment for life if, after a sentencing hearing conducted by the court in accordance with s. 921.1401, the court finds that life imprisonment is an appropriate sentence. If the court finds that life imprisonment is not an appropriate sentence, such person shall be punished by a term of imprisonment of at least 40 years. A person sentenced pursuant to this subparagraph is entitled to a review of his or her sentence in accordance with s. 921.1402(2)(a).

rows.trigger: NOT VALUE-TRIGGERED. Same juvenile capital-felony track as (1)(b)1., but for a person who did NOT actually kill, intend to kill, or attempt to kill. Scope null (corrected from 'prior') for the same reason: age and killing role, not criminal history. Two differences from (1)(b)1. that are easy to miss: the statute says 'may be punished' rather than 'shall,' and NO minimum term is stated (contrast the 40-year floor in (1)(b)1.). Sentence review runs to s. 921.1402(2)(c), not (2)(a), and only where the term exceeds 15 years.
rows.quote: A person who did not actually kill, intend to kill, or attempt to kill the victim and who is convicted under s. 782.04 of a capital felony, or an offense that was reclassified as a capital felony, which was committed before the person attained 18 years of age may be punished by a term of imprisonment for life or by a term of years equal to life if, after a sentencing hearing conducted by the court in accordance with s. 921.1401, the court finds that life imprisonment is an appropriate sentence. A person who is sentenced to a term of imprisonment of more than 15 years is entitled to a review of his or her sentence in accordance with s. 921.1402(2)(c).

rows.trigger: NOT VALUE-TRIGGERED. ADDED ON REPAIR -- this subparagraph had no row and was not referenced anywhere in the prior table, not even in its unread list. It assigns no penalty and no degree, but it is the OPERATIVE ALLOCATOR between the (1)(b)1. and (1)(b)2. tracks: the court SHALL make a written finding on sentence-review eligibility under s. 921.1402(2)(a) or (c), based on whether the person actually killed, intended to kill, or attempted to kill. The final sentence is the non-obvious one: the court MAY find that MULTIPLE DEFENDANTS killed, intended to kill, or attempted to kill the same victim, so more than one codefendant can be routed into the harsher (1)(b)1. track for a single death. Scope null: a procedural mandate keyed to the juvenile capital track, not a value, item, place, or prior-record narrowing.
rows.quote: The court shall make a written finding as to whether a person is eligible for a sentence review hearing under s. 921.1402(2)(a) or (c). Such a finding shall be based upon whether the person actually killed, intended to kill, or attempted to kill the victim. The court may find that multiple defendants killed, intended to kill, or attempted to kill the victim.

rows.trigger: NOT VALUE-TRIGGERED. SPLIT ON REPAIR. The prior table folded both sentences of subsection (2) into one row labeled 'capital felony,' which is at best half right: 'capital felony' here describes the OFFENSE OF CONVICTION, not the resulting penalty class. The operative effect of this sentence is the opposite of a capital penalty -- if the death penalty for a capital felony is held unconstitutional by the Florida Supreme Court or the United States Supreme Court, a person previously sentenced to death is brought back before the court and RESENTENCED TO LIFE as provided in subsection (1). Contingent trigger; no offense conduct triggers it.
rows.quote: In the event the death penalty in a capital felony is held to be unconstitutional by the Florida Supreme Court or the United States Supreme Court, the court having jurisdiction over a person previously sentenced to death for a capital felony shall cause such person to be brought before the court, and the court shall sentence such person to life imprisonment as provided in subsection (1).

rows.trigger: NOT VALUE-TRIGGERED. A SEPARATE RULE WITH THE OPPOSITE VALENCE FROM THE FIRST SENTENCE, and the reason subsection (2) had to be split. The first sentence converts death to life when the death PENALTY is held unconstitutional. This sentence forecloses the parallel argument as to METHOD: a holding that a method of execution is unconstitutional does NOT reduce any death sentence. A reader who treats subsection (2) as a single 'unconstitutionality gets you life' provision gets this backwards. Assigns no degree; it is a limitation on relief.
rows.quote: No sentence of death shall be reduced as a result of a determination that a method of execution is held to be unconstitutional under the State Constitution or the Constitution of the United States.

rows.trigger: NOT VALUE-TRIGGERED. ADDED ON REPAIR. Unnumbered lead-in scoping everything in paragraphs (3)(a) through (3)(e). It reaches 'any other designated felony' -- every felony other than a capital felony handled by subsection (1) -- and it is PERMISSIVE on its face ('may be punished as follows'). The degree-specific figures that follow are ceilings, not mandates, except where another provision makes a term mandatory.
rows.quote: A person who has been convicted of any other designated felony may be punished as follows:

rows.trigger: NOT VALUE-TRIGGERED. Date-of-offense trigger: life felony committed BEFORE October 1, 1983. The only life-felony tier with an express minimum term (30 years) and no stated maximum other than life.
rows.quote: For a life felony committed before October 1, 1983, by a term of imprisonment for life or for a term of at least 30 years.

rows.trigger: NOT VALUE-TRIGGERED. Date-of-offense trigger: life felony committed on or after October 1, 1983 (and, by operation of subparagraph 3., before July 1, 1995). The only life-felony tier with a term-of-years CAP of 40 years.
rows.quote: For a life felony committed on or after October 1, 1983, by a term of imprisonment for life or by a term of imprisonment not exceeding 40 years.

rows.trigger: NOT VALUE-TRIGGERED. Date-of-offense trigger: life felony committed on or after July 1, 1995. Expressly subordinate to subparagraph 4. A term of years here may run up to life, so there is no numeric ceiling below life.
rows.quote: Except as provided in subparagraph 4., for a life felony committed on or after July 1, 1995, by a term of imprisonment for life or by imprisonment for a term of years not exceeding life imprisonment.

rows.trigger: NOT VALUE-TRIGGERED. SCOPE IS NULL, AND THAT IS A CORRECTION: the prior table tagged this row scope='item.' In this schema 'item' denotes the thing taken or involved (the property/cargo axis from 812.014). NOTHING is taken here and no item narrows this provision. The narrowing is the OFFENSE OF CONVICTION -- a life felony committed on or after September 1, 2005, which is a violation of s. 800.04(5)(b) (lewd or lascivious battery). Reusing the item axis for a statutory-cross-reference axis corrupts the field's meaning. Mandates either life or a split sentence with a 25-year prison floor followed by probation or community control for the person's natural life. Subordinate to sub-subparagraph b.
rows.quote: Except as provided in sub-subparagraph b., for a life felony committed on or after September 1, 2005, which is a violation of s. 800.04(5)(b), by: (I) A term of imprisonment for life; or (II) A split sentence that is a term of at least 25 years’ imprisonment and not exceeding life imprisonment, followed by probation or community control for the remainder of the person’s natural life, as provided in s. 948.012(4).

rows.trigger: NOT VALUE-TRIGGERED. SCOPE 'prior' IS CORRECT HERE AND THIS IS THE ONLY GENUINELY RECIDIVIST PROVISION IN SUBSECTION (3). Trigger: a life felony committed on or after July 1, 2008, which is the person's SECOND OR SUBSEQUENT violation of s. 800.04(5)(b). Mandatory life; the split-sentence option in 4.a. is unavailable. The prior table gave this identical tag to five age-based juvenile provisions with no criminal-history element, making them indistinguishable from this one; those tags have been removed so this row is now the only 'prior' in subsection (3).
rows.quote: For a life felony committed on or after July 1, 2008, which is a person’s second or subsequent violation of s. 800.04(5)(b), by a term of imprisonment for life.

rows.trigger: NOT VALUE-TRIGGERED. Scope null (corrected from 'prior'): the narrowing fact is age at the offense, not criminal history. Overrides subparagraphs 1.-4. Trigger: conviction under s. 782.04 of an offense RECLASSIFIED as a life felony, committed before the person attained 18 years of age, after a s. 921.1401 sentencing hearing. Permissive ('may be punished') and states NO minimum term. Sub-subparagraphs a., b., and c. now have their own rows -- the prior table stopped here.
rows.quote: Notwithstanding subparagraphs 1.-4., a person who is convicted under s. 782.04 of an offense that was reclassified as a life felony which was committed before the person attained 18 years of age may be punished by a term of imprisonment for life or by a term of years equal to life imprisonment if the judge conducts a sentencing hearing in accordance with s. 921.1401 and finds that life imprisonment or a term of years equal to life imprisonment is an appropriate sentence.

rows.trigger: NOT VALUE-TRIGGERED. ADDED ON REPAIR. Sentence-review entitlement on the (3)(a)5. juvenile life-felony track. Assigns no penalty and no degree; it confers a right. Threshold: the person actually killed, intended to kill, or attempted to kill AND is sentenced to MORE THAN 25 YEARS. Review runs to s. 921.1402(2)(b) -- a different subdivision from the (1)(b)1. track, which runs to 921.1402(2)(a).
rows.quote: A person who actually killed, intended to kill, or attempted to kill the victim and is sentenced to a term of imprisonment of more than 25 years is entitled to a review of his or her sentence in accordance with s. 921.1402(2)(b).

rows.trigger: NOT VALUE-TRIGGERED. ADDED ON REPAIR. The lower-threshold twin of 5.a.: a person who did NOT kill, intend to kill, or attempt to kill is entitled to review at MORE THAN 15 YEARS, ten years earlier than the killer track. Review runs to s. 921.1402(2)(c). A reader who stops at 5.a. records a 25-year review threshold and misses that a large part of this population reviews at 15.
rows.quote: A person who did not actually kill, intend to kill, or attempt to kill the victim and is sentenced to a term of imprisonment of more than 15 years is entitled to a review of his or her sentence in accordance with s. 921.1402(2)(c).

rows.trigger: NOT VALUE-TRIGGERED. ADDED ON REPAIR. THIS IS THE LAST SUB-SUBPARAGRAPH OF THE PARAGRAPH -- exactly the position a reader who found the answer at a. or b. never reaches. Mandatory written finding allocating between the 5.a. and 5.b. review tracks, and it carries the same MULTIPLE-DEFENDANTS clause as (1)(b)3.: the court may find that more than one defendant killed, intended to kill, or attempted to kill the same victim, routing several codefendants into the harsher 25-year track for a single death.
rows.quote: The court shall make a written finding as to whether a person is eligible for a sentence review hearing under s. 921.1402(2)(b) or (c). Such a finding shall be based upon whether the person actually killed, intended to kill, or attempted to kill the victim. The court may find that multiple defendants killed, intended to kill, or attempted to kill the victim.

rows.trigger: NOT VALUE-TRIGGERED. SCOPE IS NULL, A CORRECTION from 'item' for the same reason as 4.a.: no item is involved, the narrowing is the offense of conviction. A life felony committed on or after October 1, 2014, which is a violation of s. 787.06(3)(g) (human trafficking). MANDATORY LIFE with no term-of-years alternative and no split-sentence option -- harsher than 4.a., which at least permits a 25-year split sentence.
rows.quote: For a life felony committed on or after October 1, 2014, which is a violation of s. 787.06(3)(g), by a term of imprisonment for life.

rows.trigger: NOT VALUE-TRIGGERED. General first degree felony penalty. THE SECOND CLAUSE IS THE CRITICAL ONE: where another statute specifically so provides, a first degree felony is punishable by a term of years NOT EXCEEDING LIFE. Reading only the first clause understates exposure from 30 years to life for every 'first degree felony punishable by life' offense in the code.
rows.quote: For a felony of the first degree, by a term of imprisonment not exceeding 30 years or, when specifically provided by statute, by imprisonment for a term of years not exceeding life imprisonment.

rows.trigger: NOT VALUE-TRIGGERED. Scope null (corrected from 'prior'): narrowed by age at the offense, not by criminal history. Overrides subparagraph 1. Trigger: conviction under s. 782.04 of a first degree felony punishable by a term of years not exceeding life (or an offense reclassified as such), committed before the person attained 18 years of age, after a s. 921.1401 hearing. Sub-subparagraphs a., b., and c. now have their own rows.
rows.quote: Notwithstanding subparagraph 1., a person convicted under s. 782.04 of a first degree felony punishable by a term of years not exceeding life imprisonment, or an offense that was reclassified as a first degree felony punishable by a term of years not exceeding life, which was committed before the person attained 18 years of age may be punished by a term of years equal to life imprisonment if the judge conducts a sentencing hearing in accordance with s. 921.1401 and finds that a term of years equal to life imprisonment is an appropriate sentence.

rows.trigger: NOT VALUE-TRIGGERED. ADDED ON REPAIR. Review entitlement on the juvenile first-degree-punishable-by-life track: killed / intended to kill / attempted to kill AND sentenced to MORE THAN 25 YEARS, review under s. 921.1402(2)(b). Textually identical to (3)(a)5.a. but attaches to a different offense class, so both must exist as separate rows.
rows.quote: A person who actually killed, intended to kill, or attempted to kill the victim and is sentenced to a term of imprisonment of more than 25 years is entitled to a review of his or her sentence in accordance with s. 921.1402(2)(b).

rows.trigger: NOT VALUE-TRIGGERED. ADDED ON REPAIR. Review at MORE THAN 15 YEARS where the person did not kill, intend to kill, or attempt to kill. Review under s. 921.1402(2)(c).
rows.quote: A person who did not actually kill, intend to kill, or attempt to kill the victim and is sentenced to a term of imprisonment of more than 15 years is entitled to a review of his or her sentence in accordance with s. 921.1402(2)(c).

rows.trigger: NOT VALUE-TRIGGERED. ADDED ON REPAIR. Last sub-subparagraph of the paragraph. Mandatory written finding allocating between the 2.a. and 2.b. review tracks, including the multiple-defendants clause.
rows.quote: The court shall make a written finding as to whether a person is eligible for a sentence review hearing under s. 921.1402(2)(b) or (c). Such a finding shall be based upon whether the person actually killed, intended to kill, or attempted to kill the victim. The court may find that multiple defendants killed, intended to kill, or attempted to kill the victim.

rows.trigger: NOT VALUE-TRIGGERED. Scope null (corrected from 'prior'): narrowed by age at the offense, not criminal history. Catch-all overriding paragraphs (a) and (b) for any offense NOT included in s. 782.04 that is a life felony, or is punishable by life or by a term of years not exceeding life, or was reclassified as such, committed before the person attained 18 years of age. Degree is 'no degree assigned' because the provision deliberately spans multiple degrees rather than naming one. Sentence review under s. 921.1402(2)(d) where the term exceeds 20 YEARS -- a third distinct threshold, neither the 25 nor the 15 used elsewhere -- and unlike (3)(a)5. and (3)(b)2. this paragraph has NO written-finding subparagraph.
rows.quote: Notwithstanding paragraphs (a) and (b), a person convicted of an offense that is not included in s. 782.04 but that is an offense that is a life felony or is punishable by a term of imprisonment for life or by a term of years not exceeding life imprisonment, or an offense that was reclassified as a life felony or an offense punishable by a term of imprisonment for life or by a term of years not exceeding life imprisonment, which was committed before the person attained 18 years of age may be punished by a term of imprisonment for life or a term of years equal to life imprisonment if the judge conducts a sentencing hearing in accordance with s. 921.1401 and finds that life imprisonment or a term of years equal to life imprisonment is an appropriate sentence. A person who is sentenced to a term of imprisonment of more than 20 years is entitled to a review of his or her sentence in accordance with s. 921.1402(2)(d).

rows.trigger: NOT VALUE-TRIGGERED. Applies to any offense a substantive statute grades a second degree felony, whatever the trigger in that statute. THIS IS A CEILING, NOT A TERM. It is the exposure carried by F.S. 812.014(2)(b)2. (cargo in the stream of commerce) at ANY value including zero, and by every other degree-graded second degree felony with no value element. Compare (9)(a)3.c., where 15 years is a FLAT MANDATORY TERM rather than a maximum.
rows.quote: For a felony of the second degree, by a term of imprisonment not exceeding 15 years.

rows.trigger: NOT VALUE-TRIGGERED. Applies to any offense a substantive statute grades a third degree felony. A ceiling, not a term. Subject to the mandatory nonstate prison sanction in subsection (10) and, in the opposite direction, to the flat 5-year prison releasee reoffender term in (9)(a)3.d.
rows.quote: For a felony of the third degree, by a term of imprisonment not exceeding 5 years.

rows.trigger: NOT VALUE-TRIGGERED. ADDED ON REPAIR. Unnumbered lead-in scoping paragraphs (4)(a) and (4)(b). Reaches a person convicted of a 'designated misdemeanor' and is permissive ('may be sentenced as follows').
rows.quote: A person who has been convicted of a designated misdemeanor may be sentenced as follows:

rows.trigger: NOT VALUE-TRIGGERED. Applies to any offense graded a first degree misdemeanor. The term is a DEFINITE term, not an indeterminate one -- subsection (6) preserves indeterminate sentencing generally, but this paragraph forecloses it here.
rows.quote: For a misdemeanor of the first degree, by a definite term of imprisonment not exceeding 1 year;

rows.trigger: NOT VALUE-TRIGGERED. Applies to any offense graded a second degree misdemeanor. Source of the familiar '60-day misdemeanor' figure; the 60 days is correct ONLY where the substantive statute actually grades the conduct as a second degree misdemeanor. Also a definite term.
rows.quote: For a misdemeanor of the second degree, by a definite term of imprisonment not exceeding 60 days.

rows.trigger: NOT VALUE-TRIGGERED. DEGREE CORRECTED from 'no degree assigned.' The provision expressly names its own class -- noncriminal violation -- and states a real ceiling: NO imprisonment, and nothing more severe than a fine, forfeiture, or other civil penalty. Recording it as 'no degree assigned' understated that (5) identifies a class and caps it. The carve-out is genuine and open-ended: 'except as provided in chapter 316 or by ordinance of any city or county,' meaning a local ordinance can in terms exceed this ceiling. I did not read chapter 316 or any ordinance, so the outer reach of that exception is unverified.
rows.quote: Any person who has been convicted of a noncriminal violation may not be sentenced to a term of imprisonment nor to any other punishment more severe than a fine, forfeiture, or other civil penalty, except as provided in chapter 316 or by ordinance of any city or county.

rows.trigger: NOT VALUE-TRIGGERED. ADDED ON REPAIR. Savings clause preserving every Florida statute that lets a trial court impose an INDETERMINATE sentence within statutory minimum and maximum limits, EXCEPT as provided in subsection (1). Matters because the fixed ceilings in subsection (3) are not the whole picture: a separate statute may authorize an indeterminate structure, and only the capital-felony rules in (1) override it.
rows.quote: Nothing in this section shall be construed to alter the operation of any statute of this state authorizing a trial court, in its discretion, to impose a sentence of imprisonment for an indeterminate period within minimum and maximum limits as provided by law, except as provided in subsection (1).

rows.trigger: NOT VALUE-TRIGGERED. ADDED ON REPAIR. Preserves authority to decree FORFEITURE OF PROPERTY, suspend or cancel a LICENSE, REMOVE A PERSON FROM OFFICE, or impose any other CIVIL PENALTY, and expressly allows such a judgment or order to be INCLUDED IN THE SENTENCE. This is real exposure sitting outside every term-of-imprisonment row in this table; a consumer reading only degrees and terms will not see it.
rows.quote: This section does not deprive the court of any authority conferred by law to decree a forfeiture of property, suspend or cancel a license, remove a person from office, or impose any other civil penalty. Such a judgment or order may be included in the sentence.

rows.scope: all felonies except capital felonies (pre-10/1/1983 branch also excepts life felonies)
rows.trigger: NOT VALUE-TRIGGERED. ADDED ON REPAIR. Applicability of sentencing structures by offense date, and it CARVES OUT BY DEGREE on its face. The October 1, 1983 guidelines apply to ALL FELONIES EXCEPT CAPITAL FELONIES committed on or after 10/1/1983 and before 1/1/1994. Separately, they apply to felonies committed BEFORE 10/1/1983 except CAPITAL FELONIES AND LIFE FELONIES, and only when the defendant AFFIRMATIVELY ELECTS to be sentenced under them. That second branch is the only defendant-elective sentencing structure in the section and carries a broader degree carve-out than any other paragraph in subsection (8).
rows.quote: The sentencing guidelines that were effective October 1, 1983, and any revisions thereto, apply to all felonies, except capital felonies, committed on or after October 1, 1983, and before January 1, 1994, and to all felonies, except capital felonies and life felonies, committed before October 1, 1983, when the defendant affirmatively selects to be sentenced pursuant to such provisions.

rows.trigger: NOT VALUE-TRIGGERED. ADDED ON REPAIR. The 1994 sentencing guidelines apply to all felonies EXCEPT CAPITAL FELONIES committed on or after January 1, 1994, and before October 1, 1995. Degree carve-out on its face.
rows.quote: The 1994 sentencing guidelines, that were effective January 1, 1994, and any revisions thereto, apply to all felonies, except capital felonies, committed on or after January 1, 1994, and before October 1, 1995.

rows.trigger: NOT VALUE-TRIGGERED. ADDED ON REPAIR. The 1995 sentencing guidelines apply to all felonies EXCEPT CAPITAL FELONIES committed on or after October 1, 1995, and before October 1, 1998.
rows.quote: The 1995 sentencing guidelines that were effective October 1, 1995, and any revisions thereto, apply to all felonies, except capital felonies, committed on or after October 1, 1995, and before October 1, 1998.

rows.trigger: NOT VALUE-TRIGGERED. ADDED ON REPAIR, AND IT IS THE MISSING FOUNDATION OF THE ENTIRE `level` COLUMN. The Criminal Punishment Code applies to all felonies EXCEPT CAPITAL FELONIES committed on or after October 1, 1998. This is the provision that switches on the Code and, through it, the s. 921.0022 severity ranking chart and the s. 921.0023 default rankings -- the apparatus every `level` field in these tables depends on. The prior table left `level` null across all 24 of its rows while never citing the paragraph that governs whether ranking applies at all. Second sentence is its own rule: any REVISION to the Code applies to felonies committed on or after the revision's effective date, so the applicable version floats with the offense date.
rows.quote: The Criminal Punishment Code applies to all felonies, except capital felonies, committed on or after October 1, 1998. Any revision to the Criminal Punishment Code applies to sentencing for all felonies, except capital felonies, committed on or after the effective date of the revision.

rows.scope: all felonies except capital felonies, continuing dates of enterprise
rows.trigger: NOT VALUE-TRIGGERED. ADDED ON REPAIR, AND IT IS THE LAST PARAGRAPH OF SUBSECTION (8) -- the position a reader who found the applicable date range at (a) through (d) never reaches. CONTINUING-ENTERPRISE FELONIES (again excepting capital felonies) are sentenced under the guidelines or Criminal Punishment Code in effect ON THE BEGINNING DATE OF THE CRIMINAL ACTIVITY, not the ending date and not the date of any individual act. For a scheme spanning a structural change this can move the entire sentencing regime backward by years.
rows.quote: Felonies, except capital felonies, with continuing dates of enterprise shall be sentenced under the sentencing guidelines or the Criminal Punishment Code in effect on the beginning date of the criminal activity.

rows.trigger: NOT VALUE-TRIGGERED. ADDED ON REPAIR. Sixteen ENUMERATED NAMED OFFENSES that qualify a defendant as a prison releasee reoffender: treason, murder, manslaughter, sexual battery, carjacking, home-invasion robbery, robbery, arson, kidnapping, aggravated assault with a deadly weapon, aggravated battery, aggravated stalking, aircraft piracy, unlawful throwing/placing/discharging of a destructive device or bomb, armed burglary, and burglary of a dwelling or occupied structure. The list reaches ATTEMPTS as well as completed offenses ('commits, or attempts to commit'). This row covers ONLY the named-offense entries; sub-subparagraph o. and sub-subparagraph r. are structurally different and have their own rows. The quote is elided at o. and stops before r., and the ellipses mark that -- this is not the whole of subparagraph 1.
rows.quote: “Prison releasee reoffender” means any defendant who commits, or attempts to commit: a. Treason; b. Murder; c. Manslaughter; d. Sexual battery; e. Carjacking; f. Home-invasion robbery; g. Robbery; h. Arson; i. Kidnapping; j. Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon; k. Aggravated battery; l. Aggravated stalking; m. Aircraft piracy; n. Unlawful throwing, placing, or discharging of a destructive device or bomb; ... p. Armed burglary; q. Burglary of a dwelling or burglary of an occupied structure; or ...

rows.scope: any felony of any degree involving use or threat of physical force or violence
rows.trigger: NOT VALUE-TRIGGERED. THIS IS THE PROVISION THIS REPAIR EXISTS TO SURFACE, AND IT IS THE EXACT STRUCTURAL TRAP FROM F.S. 812.014(2)(b)2. AND F.S. 817.568(2)(b): a list whose neighboring entries are NAMED ITEMS and whose middle entry is SOMETHING ELSE ENTIRELY WITH NO FLOOR. Sub-subparagraphs a.-n. and p.-q. are sixteen named offenses. Sub-subparagraph o. is NOT an offense name at all -- it is an OPEN-ENDED CATEGORY: 'Any felony that involves the use or threat of physical force or violence against an individual.' There is NO enumerated floor and NO DEGREE FLOOR. It reaches a felony of ANY DEGREE, including a THIRD DEGREE felony, and it is satisfied by the mere THREAT of force with no force used, no weapon, and no injury. Consequence, stated plainly because the prior table concealed it: the prison releasee reoffender mandatory minimums in (9)(a)3. attach to ANY VIOLENT FELONY WHATSOEVER, unbounded, not merely to the sixteen named crimes. A defendant whose new offense is a garden-variety third degree felony involving a threat of force draws a FLAT 5 YEARS at 100 percent under (9)(a)3.d. and (9)(b). Degree is 'no degree assigned' because this sub-subparagraph assigns none -- but that null must be read as 'EVERY felony degree,' never as 'no exposure.'
