rows.quote: Any felony that involves the use or threat of physical force or violence against an individual;

rows.trigger: NOT VALUE-TRIGGERED. A THIRD STRUCTURALLY DIFFERENT KIND OF ENTRY in the same list, and the LAST sub-subparagraph -- the terminal position a reader who found an answer earlier never reaches. Neither a named offense nor a conduct category but a STATUTORY CROSS-REFERENCE LIST: ANY felony violation of s. 790.07 (weapons during a felony), s. 800.04 (lewd or lascivious offenses on a person under 16), s. 827.03 (child abuse), s. 827.071 (sexual performance by a child), or s. 847.0135(5) (lewd computer solicitation). 'Any felony violation' means every degree of felony under each cited section qualifies -- no degree floor and no violence element required. I did not read those five sections, so the full set of qualifying offenses they contain is unverified.

NOT VALUE-TRIGGERED. ADDED ON REPAIR. The unnumbered flush text following sub-subparagraph r. that supplies the TIMING ELEMENT for every entry a. through r.: the qualifying offense must be committed WITHIN 3 YEARS after release. Three release sources count, and the second and third are easy to miss: a state correctional facility (DOC or private vendor); A COUNTY DETENTION FACILITY following incarceration for an offense for which the sentence pronounced was a prison sentence; and a correctional institution of ANOTHER STATE, the District of Columbia, the United States, any U.S. possession or territory, OR ANY FOREIGN JURISDICTION, following incarceration for an offense punishable by more than 1 year IN THIS STATE. The out-of-state and foreign equivalence rule is measured by Florida's punishment for the conduct, not the sentencing jurisdiction's.
rows.quote: within 3 years after being released from a state correctional facility operated by the Department of Corrections or a private vendor, a county detention facility following incarceration for an offense for which the sentence pronounced was a prison sentence, or a correctional institution of another state, the District of Columbia, the United States, any possession or territory of the United States, or any foreign jurisdiction, following incarceration for an offense for which the sentence is punishable by more than 1 year in this state.

rows.trigger: NOT VALUE-TRIGGERED. ADDED ON REPAIR. A SECOND, FULLY INDEPENDENT PRISON RELEASEE REOFFENDER PATHWAY WITH NO RELEASE-DATE TRIGGER AND NO 3-YEAR WINDOW AT ALL. It reaches any defendant who commits or attempts to commit any offense listed in sub-subparagraphs (a)1.a.-r. WHILE SERVING A PRISON SENTENCE, or while on ESCAPE STATUS from a state correctional facility or from an out-of-state, federal, territorial, or foreign institution. Because it incorporates the whole a.-r. list, it carries the open-ended (9)(a)1.o. violent-felony catch-all with it. A consumer who models PRR purely as a 3-year post-release window misses this pathway entirely.
rows.quote: “Prison releasee reoffender” also means any defendant who commits or attempts to commit any offense listed in sub-subparagraphs (a)1.a.-r. while the defendant was serving a prison sentence or on escape status from a state correctional facility operated by the Department of Corrections or a private vendor or while the defendant was on escape status from a correctional institution of another state, the District of Columbia, the United States, any possession or territory of the United States, or any foreign jurisdiction, following incarceration for an offense for which the sentence is punishable by more than 1 year in this state.

rows.trigger: NOT VALUE-TRIGGERED. ADDED ON REPAIR, AND IT RESTORES TEXT THE PRIOR TABLE SILENTLY DROPPED. The prior row cited to sub-subparagraph a. but opened its quote mid-subparagraph-3 without an ellipsis, deleting the first sentence. That sentence is not filler: it establishes that PRR sentencing is ELECTIVE WITH THE STATE ATTORNEY ('the state attorney MAY seek'), which is the whole subject of the omitted (9)(d). The lead-in also sets the burden -- PREPONDERANCE OF THE EVIDENCE, not beyond a reasonable doubt -- and the consequence that the defendant is NOT ELIGIBLE for sentencing under the sentencing guidelines, before any of the four terms in a.-d. is reached.
rows.quote: If the state attorney determines that a defendant is a prison releasee reoffender as defined in subparagraph 1., the state attorney may seek to have the court sentence the defendant as a prison releasee reoffender. Upon proof from the state attorney that establishes by a preponderance of the evidence that a defendant is a prison releasee reoffender as defined in this section, such defendant is not eligible for sentencing under the sentencing guidelines and must be sentenced as follows:

rows.trigger: NOT VALUE-TRIGGERED. QUOTE CORRECTED: this row now quotes only sub-subparagraph a., verbatim; the silently dropped lead-in has its own row above. Prison releasee reoffender term for 'a felony punishable by life' -- the statute names no DEGREE here, only a punishment class, so degree is 'no degree assigned' rather than a guess. MANDATORY LIFE. The predicate is any offense in (9)(a)1.a.-r., WHICH INCLUDES THE OPEN-ENDED VIOLENT-FELONY CATEGORY AT (9)(a)1.o. AND THE CROSS-REFERENCE LIST AT r. -- not a closed list of sixteen named crimes. Under (9)(b), release only by expiration of sentence. Under (9)(c), a court may go higher. Under (9)(d)1., the state attorney may decline for extenuating circumstances.
rows.quote: For a felony punishable by life, by a term of imprisonment for life;

rows.trigger: NOT VALUE-TRIGGERED. Prison releasee reoffender: a FLAT MANDATORY 30 YEARS, not a maximum -- contrast (3)(b)1., where 30 years is a ceiling. The predicate is any offense in (9)(a)1.a.-r., INCLUDING the open-ended 'any felony that involves the use or threat of physical force or violence' at (9)(a)1.o. and any felony violation of the five sections listed at r. Under (9)(b) the full 30 years must be served at 100 percent with no parole, control release, or any form of early release. Under (9)(c) the court may impose MORE, including under s. 775.084.
rows.quote: For a felony of the first degree, by a term of imprisonment of 30 years;

rows.trigger: NOT VALUE-TRIGGERED. Prison releasee reoffender: a FLAT MANDATORY 15 YEARS, not a maximum. Compare (3)(d), where 15 years is the CEILING for the same degree -- so a PRR second degree felony is sentenced at the statutory maximum with no discretion below it. The predicate includes the unbounded (9)(a)1.o. violent-felony category and the r. cross-references, not just the sixteen named offenses. Served at 100 percent under (9)(b); may be exceeded under (9)(c).
rows.quote: For a felony of the second degree, by a term of imprisonment of 15 years; and

rows.trigger: NOT VALUE-TRIGGERED. TRIGGER CORRECTED -- THE PRIOR VERSION DESCRIBED THE PREDICATE AS 'one of the qualifying offenses listed in (9)(a)1.a.-r.,' WHICH READS AS A CLOSED ENUMERATION AND CONCEALED THE OPEN CATEGORY. Prison releasee reoffender: a FLAT MANDATORY 5 YEARS, which is also the statutory maximum for the degree under (3)(e), so there is no room below it. THE PREDICATE IS NOT A CLOSED LIST. Via (9)(a)1.o., ANY FELONY THAT INVOLVES THE USE OR THREAT OF PHYSICAL FORCE OR VIOLENCE AGAINST AN INDIVIDUAL qualifies, at any degree. So a defendant whose new offense is an ordinary THIRD DEGREE felony involving nothing more than a THREAT of force, committed within 3 years of release under (9)(a)1. or while serving a sentence or on escape status under (9)(a)2., draws a flat, non-negotiable 5 years served at 100 PERCENT under (9)(b), with no parole, control release, or any form of early release -- and the court may impose MORE under (9)(c). Also reachable via (9)(a)1.r. through any felony violation of ss. 790.07, 800.04, 827.03, 827.071, or 847.0135(5).
rows.quote: For a felony of the third degree, by a term of imprisonment of 5 years.

rows.trigger: NOT VALUE-TRIGGERED. ADDED ON REPAIR AS ITS OWN ROW, AND IT IS WHAT CONVERTS ALL FOUR (9)(a)3. TERMS FROM NOMINAL SENTENCES INTO TRUE MANDATORY MINIMUMS. A person sentenced under paragraph (a) is RELEASED ONLY BY EXPIRATION OF SENTENCE, is NOT eligible for parole, control release, or ANY FORM of early release, and MUST SERVE 100 PERCENT of the court-imposed sentence. It applies to every tier -- life, 30, 15, and 5 years -- not just one. The prior table mentioned it only as an aside inside the trigger prose of the 30-year row and nowhere for the other three.
rows.quote: A person sentenced under paragraph (a) shall be released only by expiration of sentence and shall not be eligible for parole, control release, or any form of early release. Any person sentenced under paragraph (a) must serve 100 percent of the court-imposed sentence.

rows.trigger: NOT VALUE-TRIGGERED. ADDED ON REPAIR. The PRR terms in (9)(a)3. are FLOORS, NOT CEILINGS. Nothing in subsection (9) prevents a court from imposing a GREATER sentence of incarceration as authorized by law, expressly including under s. 775.084 (habitual felony offender, habitual violent felony offender, three-time violent felony offender, violent career criminal) or ANY OTHER provision of law. Applies to all four tiers; the prior table mentioned it only in passing in the third-degree row.
rows.quote: Nothing in this subsection shall prevent a court from imposing a greater sentence of incarceration as authorized by law, pursuant to s. 775.084 or any other provision of law.

rows.trigger: NOT VALUE-TRIGGERED. ADDED ON REPAIR. THE DISCRETION VALVE ON AN OTHERWISE MANDATORY SCHEME, and the only thing in subsection (9) that can keep a qualifying defendant off the PRR track. Legislative intent that qualifying offenders be punished to the fullest extent of the law UNLESS THE STATE ATTORNEY DETERMINES THAT EXTENUATING CIRCUMSTANCES EXIST which preclude just prosecution -- expressly INCLUDING WHETHER THE VICTIM RECOMMENDS that the offender not be sentenced as a prison releasee reoffender. Read with the (9)(a)3. lead-in ('the state attorney may seek'), PRR is prosecutorially elective, not automatic. A table that records the four terms as absolute and omits this understates the reader's options.
rows.quote: It is the intent of the Legislature that offenders previously released from prison or a county detention facility following incarceration for an offense for which the sentence pronounced was a prison sentence who meet the criteria in paragraph (a) be punished to the fullest extent of the law and as provided in this subsection, unless the state attorney determines that extenuating circumstances exist which preclude the just prosecution of the offender, including whether the victim recommends that the offender not be sentenced as provided in this subsection.

rows.trigger: NOT VALUE-TRIGGERED. ADDED ON REPAIR, AND IT IS THE LAST SUBPARAGRAPH OF THE LAST PARAGRAPH OF SUBSECTION (9). Accountability mechanism for the (9)(d)1. valve: for EVERY case in which the offender meets the paragraph (a) criteria and does NOT receive the mandatory minimum, the state attorney MUST explain the sentencing deviation IN WRITING and place the explanation in the case file maintained by the state attorney. Creates a documented record of every PRR declination.
rows.quote: For every case in which the offender meets the criteria in paragraph (a) and does not receive the mandatory minimum prison sentence, the state attorney must explain the sentencing deviation in writing and place such explanation in the case file maintained by the state attorney.

rows.trigger: NOT VALUE-TRIGGERED. MANDATORY NONSTATE PRISON SANCTION, and it cuts DOWNWARD -- the only mitigating mandate in the section. Requires ALL of: offense committed on or after July 1, 2009; it is a third degree felony; it is NOT a forcible felony as defined in s. 776.08; it is NOT any third degree felony violation under chapter 810 (burglary and trespass); and total sentence points under s. 921.0024 are 22 OR FEWER. Escape hatch: the court may still impose state prison on WRITTEN FINDINGS that a nonstate prison sanction could present a danger to the public. Note the tension with (9)(a)3.d.: a PRR-qualified third degree felon is ineligible for guidelines sentencing altogether and faces a flat 5 years, and the s. 776.08 forcible-felony exclusion here will often be triggered by the same conduct that satisfies (9)(a)1.o.
rows.quote: If a defendant is sentenced for an offense committed on or after July 1, 2009, which is a third degree felony but not a forcible felony as defined in s. 776.08, and excluding any third degree felony violation under chapter 810, and if the total sentence points pursuant to s. 921.0024 are 22 points or fewer, the court must sentence the offender to a nonstate prison sanction. However, if the court makes written findings that a nonstate prison sanction could present a danger to the public, the court may sentence the offender to a state correctional facility pursuant to this section.

rows.trigger: NOT VALUE-TRIGGERED. ADDED ON REPAIR, AND IT IS THE FINAL SUBSECTION OF THE SECTION. Incorporation-by-reference rule: the purpose of s. 775.082 is uniform punishment, and to that end A REFERENCE TO THIS SECTION CONSTITUTES A GENERAL REFERENCE under the doctrine of incorporation by reference. Operationally this governs every substantive statute in the Florida code that says 'punishable as provided in s. 775.082': those statutes absorb LATER AMENDMENTS to this section automatically rather than freezing the version in force when the substantive statute was enacted. It is the reason a degree label in any other statute converts to the terms in THIS table as currently amended.
rows.quote: The purpose of this section is to provide uniform punishment for those crimes made punishable under this section and, to this end, a reference to this section constitutes a general reference under the doctrine of incorporation by reference.

unread: SCOPE OF THIS FIELD, STATED FIRST BECAUSE THE PRIOR VERSION INVERTED IT: `unread` is for parts of s. 775.082 itself that this table does not cover. The prior table filled it with fifteen entries about OTHER statutes while asserting that nothing in this section was skipped -- a cross-reference bibliography dressed as a coverage disclosure, which is exactly what drives a false whole-section pass through a build guard. In-section items are listed first below; external references not read are listed after them and are labeled EXTERNAL.

IN-SECTION COVERAGE: I re-fetched https://www.flsenate.gov/Laws/Statutes/2025/775.082 and read subsections (1) through (11) start to finish, and every operative provision now has a row -- including the ones that had none before: (1)(b)3.; the second sentence of (2); the (3) and (4) lead-ins; (3)(a)5.a.-c.; (3)(b)2.a.-c.; (6); (7); (8)(a)-(e); (9)(a)1. and its sub-subparagraphs a.-r.; the flush 3-year-window text closing (9)(a)1.; (9)(a)2.; the (9)(a)3. lead-in; (9)(b); (9)(c); (9)(d)1.-2.; and (11). 52 rows against the prior 24. I do NOT claim any provision is fully understood -- see the residual ambiguities immediately below.

RESIDUAL IN-SECTION AMBIGUITY -- 775.082(9)(a)1.o. The phrase 'any felony that involves the use or threat of physical force or violence against an individual' is undefined within this section and carries no degree limit. Its outer boundary is set by case law I did not read. The row records that it is unbounded; it does NOT resolve which specific felonies courts have held to fall inside it, so a consumer cannot use this table to determine whether a particular third degree felony qualifies.

RESIDUAL IN-SECTION AMBIGUITY -- 775.082(5). The exception 'except as provided in chapter 316 or by ordinance of any city or county' is open-ended on its face and appears to permit a local ordinance to exceed the noncriminal-violation ceiling. I did not read chapter 316 or any ordinance, so how far that exception reaches is unresolved.

RESIDUAL IN-SECTION AMBIGUITY -- 775.082(3)(c) has no written-finding subparagraph parallel to (1)(b)3., (3)(a)5.c., and (3)(b)2.c., and uses a 20-year review threshold found nowhere else in the section. Whether that omission is deliberate is not resolvable from this text.

RESIDUAL IN-SECTION AMBIGUITY -- 775.082(9)(a)3.a. states a term for 'a felony punishable by life' without naming a degree, so the degree field is null. Which offenses fall in that class is fixed by other statutes via (3)(b)1.'s 'when specifically provided by statute' clause, not by this section.
History note (s. 3, ch. 71-136 through s. 30, ch. 2019-167) -- read as a citation list only. I did not pull any session law, so I cannot independently confirm the 2025 text against the enacting acts.

The prior table's unread list named only s. 921.0022 and therefore misidentified which statute governs `level` for unranked offenses. Correcting the identification here; neither statute was read.

fs 741.2901.title: Domestic violence cases; prosecutors; legislative intent; investigation; duty of circuits; first appearance.

rows.trigger: Arrest for an act of domestic violence. Mandatory pretrial custody until first appearance; this is a custody/bail directive, NOT a degree of offense, mandatory minimum sentence, or penalty enhancement. No value trigger and no lower bound of any kind.
rows.quote: When a defendant is arrested for an act of domestic violence, the defendant shall be held in custody until brought before the court for admittance to bail in accordance with chapter 903. In determining bail, the court shall consider the safety of the victim, the victim's children, and any other person who may be in danger if the defendant is released.

unread: None within F.S. 741.2901 -- the section consists of exactly three subsections, (1), (2), and (3), plus the History note, and all were read start to finish. The section contains no paragraphs or subparagraphs (no (a)/(b), no 1./2.) at any level.

Cross-referenced statutes not fetched or read: s. 741.28 (definition of 'domestic violence'), which supplies the operative definition used in subsections (2) and (3); chapter 903 (bail), which supplies the admittance-to-bail procedure referenced in subsection (3). Any degree of offense, mandatory minimum, or enhancement for domestic violence conduct lives outside this section (e.g. s. 741.283, s. 741.31, s. 784.03, s. 921.0022) and was not read.
Session-law text of s. 4, ch. 91-210; s. 3, ch. 94-134; s. 3, ch. 94-135; s. 3, ch. 95-195 (History note) not read.

rows.trigger: Definitional only. Defines "domestic violence" for ss. 741.28-741.31; assigns no degree of offense, no mandatory minimum, and no enhancement. Enumerates predicate offenses (assault, aggravated assault, battery, aggravated battery, sexual assault, sexual battery, stalking, aggravated stalking, kidnapping, false imprisonment) AND a residual catch-all covering ANY criminal offense resulting in physical injury or death, with no limit on offense degree and no lower bound of any kind; the enumerated list does not cap the definition.
rows.quote: “Domestic violence” means any assault, aggravated assault, battery, aggravated battery, sexual assault, sexual battery, stalking, aggravated stalking, kidnapping, false imprisonment, or any criminal offense resulting in physical injury or death of one family or household member by another family or household member.

rows.trigger: Definitional only. Defines the relationship element ("family or household member") that the (2) definition depends on; assigns no degree, no mandatory minimum, no enhancement. Includes a cohabitation requirement with an express exception for persons who have a child in common.
rows.quote: “Family or household member” means spouses, former spouses, persons related by blood or marriage, persons who are presently residing together as if a family or who have resided together in the past as if a family, and persons who are parents of a child in common regardless of whether they have been married. With the exception of persons who have a child in common, the family or household members must be currently residing or have in the past resided together in the same single dwelling unit.

rows.trigger: Definitional only; identifies the agency. No degree, mandatory minimum, or enhancement.
rows.quote: “Department” means the Florida Department of Law Enforcement.

rows.trigger: Definitional only; identifies who qualifies as a law enforcement officer for ss. 741.28-741.31. No degree, mandatory minimum, or enhancement.
rows.quote: “Law enforcement officer” means any person who is elected, appointed, or employed by any municipality or the state or any political subdivision thereof who meets the minimum qualifications established in s. 943.13 and is certified as a law enforcement officer under s. 943.1395.

fs-784.08.title: Assault or battery on persons 65 years of age or older; reclassification of offenses; minimum sentence.

rows.trigger: Conviction of aggravated assault or aggravated battery upon a person 65 years of age or older. NO dollar or quantity threshold of any kind: min is null because value is not the trigger. Imposes a 3-year mandatory minimum term of imprisonment, a fine of not more than $10,000, mandatory restitution to the victim, and up to 500 hours of community service; it assigns no degree of offense itself (the degree comes from the reclassification in subsection (2)).
rows.quote: A person who is convicted of an aggravated assault or aggravated battery upon a person 65 years of age or older shall be sentenced to a minimum term of imprisonment of 3 years and fined not more than $10,000 and shall also be ordered by the sentencing judge to make restitution to the victim of such offense and to perform up to 500 hours of community service work. Restitution and community service work shall be in addition to any fine or sentence which may be imposed and shall not be in lieu thereof.

rows.trigger: Flush/introductory language of the reclassification subsection. Applies whenever a person is CHARGED with assault, aggravated assault, battery, or aggravated battery upon a person 65 years of age or older. fs-847.0135.title: Computer pornography; prohibited computer usage; traveling to meet minor; penalties

rows.trigger: Computer pornography: knowingly compiling, entering, transmitting, making, printing, publishing, reproducing, causing or allowing to be entered or transmitted, or buying, selling, receiving, exchanging, or disseminating any notice, statement, or advertisement of a minor's identifying information for purposes of facilitating, encouraging, offering, or soliciting sexual conduct of or with any minor or the visual depiction of such conduct. No quantity or dollar trigger; any single instance qualifies. Undercover operative or law enforcement involvement is not a defense.
rows.quote: any notice, statement, or advertisement of any minor's name, telephone number, place of residence, physical characteristics, or other descriptive or identifying information for purposes of facilitating, encouraging, offering, or soliciting sexual conduct of or with any minor, or the visual depiction of such conduct, commits a felony of the third degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.trigger: Knowingly using a computer online service, Internet service, local bulletin board service, or any other device capable of electronic data storage or transmission to (a) seduce, solicit, lure, or entice, or attempt to, a child or a person believed to be a child to commit an illegal act described in chapter 794, 800, or 827 or otherwise engage in unlawful sexual conduct; or (b) to solicit, lure, or entice, or attempt to, a parent, legal guardian, or custodian (or person believed to be one) to consent to the child's participation. No value trigger; no lower bound of any kind. Each separate use may be charged as a separate offense.
rows.quote: commits a felony of the third degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084. ... Each separate use of a computer online service, Internet service, local bulletin board service, or any other device capable of electronic data storage or transmission wherein an offense described in this section is committed may be charged as a separate offense.

rows.trigger: Enhancement within subsection (3): the offender misrepresents his or her age while violating subsection (3). No value or quantity trigger; applies to any violation of (3) accompanied by age misrepresentation.
rows.quote: Any person who, in violating this subsection, misrepresents his or her age, commits a felony of the second degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.trigger: Traveling to meet a minor: traveling any distance within, to, or from this state by any means, attempting to do so, or causing another to do so or attempt to do so, for the purpose of engaging in an illegal act described in chapter 794, 800, or 827 or other unlawful sexual conduct with a child or person believed to be a child, after using a computer online or Internet service or other electronic data storage or transmission device to (a) seduce, solicit, lure, or entice, or attempt to, the child or believed child; or (b) to solicit, lure, or entice, or attempt to, a parent, legal guardian, or custodian, or believed parent, legal guardian, or custodian, to consent to the child's participation. No distance minimum -- 'any distance' -- and no value trigger.
rows.quote: Any person who travels any distance either within this state, to this state, or from this state by any means, who attempts to do so, or who causes another to do so or to attempt to do so for the purpose of engaging in any illegal act described in chapter 794, chapter 800, or chapter 827, or to otherwise engage in other unlawful sexual conduct with a child or with another person believed by the person to be a child after using a computer online service, Internet service, local bulletin board service, or any other device capable of electronic data storage or transmission to: ... commits a felony of the second degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.trigger: Definitional provision only; assigns no degree. Committed live over a computer online, Internet, or local bulletin board service where the offender knows, should know, or has reason to believe the transmission is viewed by a victim less than 16 years of age. Undercover operative or law enforcement involvement is not a defense. Degree is supplied by (5)(b) and (5)(c) based on offender age.

rows.quote: A person who violates subparagraphs (a)1.-6. commits a misdemeanor of the first degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082 or s. 775.083, except that, upon a second or subsequent violation, the person commits a felony of the third degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.quote: A person who violates paragraph (a) commits a felony of the third degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.quote: Notwithstanding paragraph (c), if a prescribing practitioner has violated paragraph (a) and received $1,000 or more in payment for writing one or more prescriptions or, in the case of a prescription written for a controlled substance described in s. 893.135, has written one or more prescriptions for a quantity of a controlled substance which, individually or in the aggregate, meets the threshold for the offense of trafficking in a controlled substance under s. 893.135, the violation is reclassified as a felony of the second degree and ranked in level 4 of the Criminal Punishment Code.

rows.trigger: Violation of ANY provision of chapter 893 that results in serious injury to a state or local law enforcement officer, firefighter, emergency medical technician, paramedic, employee of a public utility or electric utility, animal control officer, volunteer firefighter engaged by state or local government, federal law enforcement officer, or any other local, state, or federal government employee injured during the course and scope of employment. rows.trigger: Same class of protected persons as the first sentence of subsection (10), where the injury sustained results in death or great bodily harm. NO quantity or value threshold.

fs-827.071.title: Sexual performance by a child; child pornography; penalties.

rows.trigger: Use of a child in a sexual performance: knowingly employing, authorizing, or inducing a child (any person younger than 18 under (1)(a)) to engage in a sexual performance, OR a parent, legal guardian, or custodian consenting to the child's participation. NO quantity or value trigger and NO lower bound of any kind -- a single performance, and a single child, suffices. Degree is fixed at second degree regardless of the child's age below 18, the number of performances, or the number of children.
rows.quote: A person is guilty of the use of a child in a sexual performance if, knowing the character and content thereof, he or she employs, authorizes, or induces a child to engage in a sexual performance or, being a parent, legal guardian, or custodian of such child, consents to the participation by such child in a sexual performance. A person who violates this subsection commits a felony of the second degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.trigger: Promoting a sexual performance by a child: knowingly producing, directing, or promoting any performance which includes sexual conduct by a child. "Promote" is defined broadly at (1)(h) to include procure, manufacture, issue, sell, give, provide, lend, mail, deliver, transfer, transmit, transmute, publish, distribute, circulate, disseminate, present, exhibit, send, post, share, advertise, or offering or agreeing to do the same. NO quantity or value trigger and NO lower bound -- a single act of producing, directing, or promoting suffices.
rows.quote: A person is guilty of promoting a sexual performance by a child when, knowing the character and content thereof, he or she produces, directs, or promotes any performance which includes sexual conduct by a child. A person who violates this subsection commits a felony of the second degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.trigger: Possession with intent to promote material that in whole or in part includes child pornography. WARNING -- the "three or more copies" figure in this subsection is NOT a degree threshold and NOT a lower bound on liability: it is only prima facie evidence of intent to promote. The offense has NO LOWER BOUND. Possession of a single item with intent to promote is a second degree felony; the three-copy figure merely supplies an evidentiary presumption of the intent element.
rows.quote: It is unlawful for any person to possess with the intent to promote any photograph, motion picture, exhibition, show, representation, or other presentation which, in whole or in part, includes child pornography. The possession of three or more copies of such photograph, motion picture, representation, or presentation is prima facie evidence of an intent to promote. A person who violates this subsection commits a felony of the second degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.trigger: Knowingly soliciting, possessing, controlling, or intentionally viewing material known to include child pornography, in whole or in part. NO LOWER BOUND on quantity -- each single photograph, motion picture, exhibition, show, image, data, computer depiction, representation, or presentation is a SEPARATE third degree felony, and where one item depicts more than one child, each child in each item is a SEPARATE offense. The only quantity-like qualification is definitional and applies solely to the "intentionally view" modality: (1)(f) states that proof of intentional viewing requires establishing more than a single image over any period of time; that definitional limit does not attach to the solicit, possess, or control modalities. Ranking-chart cite is "827.071(5)" without paragraph designation.
rows.quote: It is unlawful for any person to knowingly solicit, possess, control, or intentionally view a photograph, motion picture, exhibition, show, representation, image, data, computer depiction, or other presentation which, in whole or in part, he or she knows to include child pornography. The solicitation, possession, control, or intentional viewing of each such photograph, motion picture, exhibition, show, image, data, computer depiction, representation, or presentation is a separate offense. If such photograph, motion picture, exhibition, show, representation, image, data, computer depiction, or other presentation includes child pornography depicting more than one child, then each such child in each such photograph, motion picture, exhibition, show, representation, image, data, computer depiction, or other presentation that is knowingly solicited, possessed, controlled, or intentionally viewed is a separate offense. A person who violates this paragraph commits a felony of the third degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.trigger: Exemption, not an offense. Removes (5)(a) liability entirely for material solicited, possessed, controlled, or intentionally viewed as part of a law enforcement investigation. Recorded because it is the second subparagraph of paragraph (5) and would be missed by anyone who stopped at (5)(a).
rows.quote: Paragraph (a) does not apply to any material solicited, possessed, controlled, or intentionally viewed as part of a law enforcement investigation.

rows.trigger: Non-preclusion clause. Assigns no degree and creates no enhancement, but expressly preserves prosecution under other state laws carrying GREATER penalties than this section, so the degrees in (2) through (5) are not a ceiling on exposure for the same conduct.
rows.quote: Prosecution of a person for an offense under this section does not preclude prosecution of that person in this state for a violation of any other law of this state, including a law providing for greater penalties than prescribed in this section or any other crime punishing the sexual performance or the sexual exploitation of children.

fs-775.21.title: The Florida Sexual Predators Act.

rows.trigger: Out-of-state-designated sexual predator/sexually violent predator residing in Florida; no degree assigned in this section -- penalty is imported wholesale by cross-reference to s. 943.0435 or s. 944.607. NO value or quantity trigger.
rows.quote: A person who meets the criteria of this section is subject to the requirements and penalty provisions of s. 943.0435 or s. 944.607 until the person provides the department with an order issued by the court that designated the person as a sexual predator, as a sexually violent predator, or any other sexual offender designation in the state or jurisdiction in which the order was issued which states that such designation has been removed

rows.trigger: Predator reported intent to vacate a permanent, temporary, or transient residence under subparagraph 2., then remained there and failed to report in person within 48 hours after the stated vacate date. NO value or quantity trigger; no lower bound of any kind.
rows.quote: A sexual predator who makes a report as required under subparagraph 2. but fails to make a report as required under this subparagraph commits a felony of the second degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.trigger: Transient-residence predator fails to report in person to the sheriff every 30 days as required by sub-subparagraph 2.b.; degree not stated here, penalty assigned by cross-reference to subsection (10). NO value or quantity trigger.
rows.quote: The failure of a sexual predator who maintains a transient residence to report in person to the sheriff’s office every 30 days as required by sub-subparagraph 2.b. is punishable as provided in subsection (10).

rows.trigger: Failure to report intended out-of-state/out-of-country residence or travel (48 hours before leaving the state; 21 days before international travel); degree not stated here, penalty assigned by cross-reference to subsection (10). NO value or quantity trigger.
rows.quote: The failure of a sexual predator to provide his or her intended place of residence or intended travel is punishable as provided in subsection (10).

rows.trigger: Predator reported intent to establish residence in another state/jurisdiction or to travel to another country, then remained in Florida without reporting in person to the sheriff within 48 hours. NO value or quantity trigger; no lower bound of any kind.
rows.quote: A sexual predator who reports his or her intent to establish a permanent, temporary, or transient residence in another state, a jurisdiction other than the State of Florida, or intent to travel to another country, but who remains in this state without reporting to the sheriff in the manner required by this paragraph, commits a felony of the second degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.trigger: Catch-all registration violation: failure to register; failure to maintain/acquire/renew a driver license or ID card; failure to provide location or change-of-name information, e-mail addresses, Internet identifiers, telephone numbers, employment changes, higher-education status changes, or vehicle changes; failure to report vacating a permanent residence; failure to reregister; failure to answer address-verification correspondence within 3 weeks; knowingly providing false registration information; OR 'otherwise fails, by act or omission, to comply with the requirements of this section.' NO value or quantity trigger and NO lower bound -- any single act or omission suffices, and each instance is a separate offense.
rows.quote: Except as otherwise specifically provided, a sexual predator who fails to register; who fails, after registration, to maintain, acquire, or renew a driver license or an identification card; who fails to provide required location information or change-of-name information; who fails to provide electronic mail addresses, Internet identifiers, and each Internet identifier’s corresponding website homepage or application software name; who fails to provide all home telephone numbers and cellular telephone numbers; who fails to report any changes to employment information, including the addition of new employment, termination of existing employment, and changes to the occupation, business name, employment address, and telephone number of previously reported employment; who fails to report any changes in status at an institution of higher education; who fails to report any changes to vehicles owned, including the addition of new vehicles and changes to the make, model, color, vehicle identification number (VIN), and license tag numbers of previously reported vehicles; who fails to make a required report in connection with vacating a permanent residence; who fails to reregister as required; who fails to respond to any address verification correspondence from the department or from county or local law enforcement agencies within 3 weeks after the date of the correspondence; who knowingly provides false registration information by act or omission; or who otherwise fails, by act or omission, to comply with the requirements of this section commits a felony of the third degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084. Each instance of a failure to register or report changes to the required information specified in this paragraph constitutes a separate offense.

rows.trigger: Predator with a qualifying enumerated conviction (s. 787.01, 787.02, or 787.025(2)(c) where victim is a minor; 794.011 excluding 794.011(10); 794.05; former 796.03; former 796.035; 800.04; 827.071; 847.0133; 847.0135(5); 847.0145; 985.701(1); or similar law of another jurisdiction where the victim was a minor) works, for compensation OR as a volunteer, at any business, school, child care facility, park, playground, or other place where children regularly congregate. NO value or quantity trigger.
rows.quote: A sexual predator who has been convicted of or found to have committed, or has pled nolo contendere or guilty to, regardless of adjudication, any violation, or attempted violation, of s. 787.01, s. 787.02, or s. 787.025(2)(c), where the victim is a minor; s. 794.011, excluding s. 794.011(10); s. 794.05; former s. 796.03; former s. 796.035; s. 800.04; s. 827.071; s. 847.0133; s. 847.0135(5); s. 847.0145; or s. 985.701(1); or a violation of a similar law of another jurisdiction when the victim of the offense was a minor, and who works, whether for compensation or as a volunteer, at any business, school, child care facility, park, playground, or other place where children regularly congregate, commits a felony of the third degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.trigger: Umbrella clause for the mandatory minimum community-control tiers in subparagraphs 1.-3. Applies to ANY felony violation of s. 775.21 EXCLUDING paragraph (g), committed on or after July 1, 2018, and only where the court does not impose a prison sentence. Assigns no degree itself; it is a mandatory-minimum enhancement. NO value trigger.
rows.quote: For a felony violation of this section, excluding paragraph (g), committed on or after July 1, 2018, if the court does not impose a prison sentence, the court shall impose a mandatory minimum term of community control, as defined in s. 948.001, as follows:

rows.trigger: First offense (no prior s. 775.21 felony offense). Mandatory minimum 6 months community control with electronic monitoring, imposed only when the court does not impose a prison sentence for a felony violation of this section other than paragraph (g). Quantity encoded is the offense count, not a dollar value.
rows.quote: For a first offense, a mandatory minimum term of 6 months with electronic monitoring.

rows.trigger: Second offense. Mandatory minimum 1 year community control with electronic monitoring, imposed only when the court does not impose a prison sentence for a felony violation of this section other than paragraph (g). Quantity encoded is the offense count, not a dollar value.
rows.quote: For a second offense, a mandatory minimum term of 1 year with electronic monitoring.

rows.trigger: Third or subsequent offense -- open-ended upper end, no maximum. Mandatory minimum 2 years community control with electronic monitoring, imposed only when the court does not impose a prison sentence for a felony violation of this section other than paragraph (g). Quantity encoded is the offense count, not a dollar value.
rows.quote: For a third or subsequent offense, a mandatory minimum term of 2 years with electronic monitoring.

rows.trigger: ANY person (not limited to predators or offenders) who misuses public records information about a sexual predator or sexual offender to secure a payment from that predator/offender; OR knowingly distributes or publishes false information about such a person misrepresented as public records information; OR materially alters public records information with intent to misrepresent it. NO value or quantity trigger; no lower bound -- no minimum payment amount or number of publications required.
rows.quote: Any person who misuses public records information relating to a sexual predator, as defined in this section, or a sexual offender, as defined in s. 943.0435 or s. 944.607, to secure a payment from such a predator or offender; who knowingly distributes or publishes false information relating to such a predator or offender which the person misrepresents as being public records information; or who materially alters public records information with the intent to misrepresent the information, including documents, summaries of public records information provided by law enforcement agencies, or public records information displayed by law enforcement agencies on websites or provided through other means of communication, commits a misdemeanor of the first degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082 or s. 775.083.

rows.trigger: ANY person with reason to believe a predator is not complying, acting with intent to assist the predator in eluding law enforcement, who does ANY of four alternative acts: 1. withholds information from or fails to notify law enforcement about the noncompliance and the predator's whereabouts; 2. harbors or attempts to harbor, or assists another in harboring; 3. conceals or attempts to conceal, or assists another in concealing; or 4. provides information the person knows to be false. Mere omission (subparagraph 1.) suffices. Does NOT apply if the predator is incarcerated in or in the custody of a state correctional facility, contractor-operated correctional facility, local jail, or federal correctional facility. This paragraph is expressly excluded from the (10)(c) mandatory minimums. NO value or quantity trigger; no lower bound.
rows.quote: Any person who has reason to believe that a sexual predator is not complying, or has not complied, with the requirements of this section and who, with the intent to assist the sexual predator in eluding a law enforcement agency that is seeking to find the sexual predator to question the sexual predator about, or to arrest the sexual predator for, his or her noncompliance with the requirements of this section:1. Withholds information from, or does not notify, the law enforcement agency about the sexual predator’s noncompliance with the requirements of this section, and, if known, the whereabouts of the sexual predator; 2. Harbors, or attempts to harbor, or assists another person in harboring or attempting to harbor, the sexual predator; 3. Conceals or attempts to conceal, or assists another person in concealing or attempting to conceal, the sexual predator; or 4. Provides information to the law enforcement agency regarding the sexual predator which the person knows to be false information, commits a felony of the third degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084. This paragraph does not apply if the sexual predator is incarcerated in or is in the custody of a state correctional facility, a contractor-operated correctional facility, a local jail, or a federal correctional facility.

fs-817.568.title: Criminal use of personal identification information
unread: None of s. 817.568 was left unread. All nineteen subsections (1) through (19), every lettered paragraph, every numbered subparagraph, and both undesignated closing (flush-left) paragraphs following (5)(c) and (10)(d) were read start to finish from the verbatim flsenate.gov text.

rows.trigger: Willful, unauthorized fraudulent USE, or POSSESSION WITH INTENT to fraudulently use, another living person's personal identification information without consent. NO LOWER BOUND: no dollar amount and no victim count is required. This is the base offense.
rows.quote: Any person who willfully and without authorization fraudulently uses, or possesses with intent to fraudulently use, personal identification information concerning another person without first obtaining that person's consent, commits the offense of fraudulent use of personal identification information, which is a felony of the third degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.trigger: VALUE BRANCH. Fraudulent use (use only, not mere possession) where pecuniary benefit, value of services received, payment sought to be avoided, or amount of injury or fraud is $5,000 or more. max is null because this paragraph states NO upper dollar limit of its own; $50,000 or more is separately covered by (2)(c).
rows.quote: Any person who willfully and without authorization fraudulently uses personal identification information concerning a person without first obtaining that person's consent commits a felony of the second degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084, if the pecuniary benefit, the value of the services received, the payment sought to be avoided, or the amount of the injury or fraud perpetrated is $5,000 or more

rows.trigger: VICTIM-COUNT BRANCH, disjunctive with the value branch ('or'). 10 or more but fewer than 20 victims. NO DOLLAR LOWER BOUND WHATSOEVER: this branch is second degree at ANY dollar value, including zero. min/max here are a PERSON COUNT, not dollars. This is the exact trap the audit was built to catch.
rows.quote: or if the person fraudulently uses the personal identification information of 10 or more persons, but fewer than 20 persons, without their consent.

rows.trigger: MANDATORY MINIMUM of 3 years' imprisonment, attaching to ANY conviction under (2)(b), whether reached by the $5,000 value branch or the 10-to-19 victim-count branch. Non-discretionary and overrides other law.
rows.quote: Notwithstanding any other provision of law, the court shall sentence any person convicted of committing the offense described in this paragraph to a mandatory minimum sentence of 3 years' imprisonment.

rows.trigger: VALUE BRANCH. Fraudulent use where pecuniary benefit, value of services received, payment sought to be avoided, or amount of injury or fraud is $50,000 or more. max is null because the paragraph states no upper dollar limit; $100,000 or more stays a first degree felony but adds a longer mandatory minimum within this same paragraph.
rows.quote: Any person who willfully and without authorization fraudulently uses personal identification information concerning a person without first obtaining that person's consent commits a felony of the first degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084, if the pecuniary benefit, the value of the services received, the payment sought to be avoided, or the amount of the injury or fraud perpetrated is $50,000 or more

rows.trigger: VICTIM-COUNT BRANCH, disjunctive with the value branch. 20 or more but fewer than 30 victims. NO DOLLAR LOWER BOUND: first degree felony at ANY dollar value. min/max are a PERSON COUNT, not dollars.
rows.quote: or if the person fraudulently uses the personal identification information of 20 or more persons, but fewer than 30 persons, without their consent.

rows.trigger: MANDATORY MINIMUM of 5 years' imprisonment for any conviction under (2)(c), reached by either the $50,000 value branch or the 20-to-29 victim-count branch.
rows.quote: Notwithstanding any other provision of law, the court shall sentence any person convicted of committing the offense described in this paragraph to a mandatory minimum sentence of 5 years' imprisonment.

rows.trigger: ESCALATED MANDATORY MINIMUM of 10 years' imprisonment, VALUE BRANCH, $100,000 or more. Degree remains first degree felony under (2)(c); this sentence raises only the mandatory minimum, it assigns no new degree.
rows.quote: If the pecuniary benefit, the value of the services received, the payment sought to be avoided, or the amount of the injury or fraud perpetrated is $100,000 or more, or if the person fraudulently uses the personal identification information of 30 or more persons without their consent, notwithstanding any other provision of law, the court shall sentence any person convicted of committing the offense described in this paragraph to a mandatory minimum sentence of 10 years' imprisonment.

rows.trigger: ESCALATED MANDATORY MINIMUM of 10 years' imprisonment, VICTIM-COUNT BRANCH, 30 or more persons, with NO DOLLAR LOWER BOUND and NO UPPER COUNT LIMIT. min/max are a PERSON COUNT. TEXTUAL NOTE, RECORDED NOT INFERRED: the degree-assigning clause of (2)(c) covers '20 or more persons, but fewer than 30 persons', so 30-or-more is expressly named only in this mandatory-minimum sentence, which reaches back to 'the offense described in this paragraph'.
rows.quote: or if the person fraudulently uses the personal identification information of 30 or more persons without their consent, notwithstanding any other provision of law, the court shall sentence any person convicted of committing the offense described in this paragraph to a mandatory minimum sentence of 10 years' imprisonment.

rows.trigger: Operating rule for the (2)(b) and (2)(c) mandatory minimums. The mandatory minimum must be imposed even where it exceeds the maximum otherwise authorized by s. 775.082, s. 775.084, or the Criminal Punishment Code, and must be included in the sentence where it is less than what could otherwise be imposed. A greater sentence is still permitted.
rows.quote: Neither paragraph (2)(b) nor paragraph (2)(c) prevents a court from imposing a greater sentence of incarceration as authorized by law. If the minimum mandatory terms of imprisonment imposed under paragraph (2)(b) or paragraph (2)(c) exceed the maximum sentences authorized under s. 775.082, s. 775.084, or the Criminal Punishment Code under chapter 921, the mandatory minimum sentence must be imposed. If the mandatory minimum terms of imprisonment under paragraph (2)(b) or paragraph (2)(c) are less than the sentence that could be imposed under s. 775.082, s. 775.084, or the Criminal Punishment Code under chapter 921, the sentence imposed by the court must include the mandatory minimum term of imprisonment as required by paragraph (2)(b) or paragraph (2)(c).

rows.trigger: Harassment by use of personal identification information. Possession, use, or ATTEMPTED use without consent for the purpose of harassing that person. NO LOWER BOUND: no dollar amount and no victim count. Note this offense is punishable under s. 775.082 or s. 775.083 only, with no reference to s. 775.084.
rows.quote: Any person who willfully and without authorization possesses, uses, or attempts to use personal identification information concerning a person without first obtaining that person's consent, and who does so for the purpose of harassing that person, commits the offense of harassment by use of personal identification information, which is a misdemeanor of the first degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082 or s. 775.083.

rows.trigger: RECLASSIFICATION UP ONE DEGREE where the offense was facilitated or furthered by the use of a public record as defined in s. 119.011. A first degree misdemeanor under this section becomes a third degree felony. NO LOWER BOUND: no dollar amount and no victim count.
rows.quote: If an offense prohibited under this section was facilitated or furthered by the use of a public record, as defined in s. 119.011, the offense is reclassified to the next higher degree as follows:(a) A misdemeanor of the first degree is reclassified as a felony of the third degree.

rows.trigger: RECLASSIFICATION for public-record facilitation. A third degree felony under this section becomes a second degree felony. NO LOWER BOUND.
rows.quote: (b) A felony of the third degree is reclassified as a felony of the second degree.

rows.trigger: RECLASSIFICATION for public-record facilitation. A second degree felony under this section becomes a first degree felony. NO LOWER BOUND. NOTE, RECORDED NOT INFERRED: subsection (5) stops at (c) and provides NO reclassification for a first degree felony, unlike subsection (10) which adds a (d) reaching life felony.
rows.quote: (c) A felony of the second degree is reclassified as a felony of the first degree.

rows.trigger: SENTENCING-LEVEL ENHANCEMENT accompanying the public-record reclassification. A reclassified felony is ranked one level above its s. 921.0022 ranking, and a reclassified misdemeanor is ranked in level 2. Expressly applies to incentive gain-time eligibility under chapter 944 as well as sentencing under chapter 921. level field left null because the s. 921.0022 chart itself was not opened.
rows.quote: For purposes of sentencing under chapter 921 and incentive gain-time eligibility under chapter 944, a felony offense that is reclassified under this subsection is ranked one level above the ranking under s. 921.0022 of the felony offense committed, and a misdemeanor offense that is reclassified under this subsection is ranked in level 2 of the offense severity ranking chart in s. 921.0022.

rows.trigger: Victim is an individual younger than 18 years of age, OR 60 years of age or older, and neither that individual nor his or her legal guardian consented. NO LOWER BOUND: no dollar amount and no victim count. A single victim in either age class is enough. 'Individual' is defined in (1)(d) as a single human being, excluding entities.
rows.quote: Any person who willfully and without authorization fraudulently uses personal identification information concerning an individual who is younger than 18 years of age or 60 years of age or older without first obtaining the consent of that individual or of his or her legal guardian commits a felony of the second degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.trigger: Offender is the parent or legal guardian of, or otherwise exercises custodial authority over, an individual younger than 18 or 60 or older, and fraudulently uses that individual's personal identification information. NO LOWER BOUND: no dollar amount and no victim count. Note the absence of any 'without authorization' or consent element in this subsection, unlike (6).
rows.quote: Any person who is in the relationship of parent or legal guardian, or who otherwise exercises custodial authority over an individual who is younger than 18 years of age or 60 years of age or older, who willfully and fraudulently uses personal identification information of that individual commits a felony of the second degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.trigger: Base offense for a DECEASED INDIVIDUAL or DISSOLVED BUSINESS ENTITY. Covers use OR possession with intent to fraudulently use. NO LOWER BOUND: no dollar amount and no count.
rows.quote: Any person who willfully and fraudulently uses, or possesses with intent to fraudulently use, personal identification information concerning a deceased individual or dissolved business entity commits the offense of fraudulent use or possession with intent to use personal identification information of a deceased individual or dissolved business entity, a felony of the third degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.trigger: DECEASED / DISSOLVED ENTITY, VALUE BRANCH. Pecuniary benefit, value of services received, payment sought to be avoided, or amount of injury or fraud is $5,000 or more. max null because the paragraph states no upper dollar limit; $50,000 or more is separately covered by (8)(c).
rows.quote: Any person who willfully and fraudulently uses personal identification information concerning a deceased individual or dissolved business entity commits a felony of the second degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084, if the pecuniary benefit, the value of the services received, the payment sought to be avoided, or the amount of injury or fraud perpetrated is $5,000 or more

rows.trigger: DECEASED / DISSOLVED ENTITY, COUNT BRANCH, disjunctive with the value branch. 10 or more but fewer than 20 deceased individuals or dissolved business entities. NO DOLLAR LOWER BOUND: second degree at ANY dollar value. min/max are a COUNT, not dollars.
rows.quote: or if the person fraudulently uses the personal identification information of 10 or more but fewer than 20 deceased individuals or dissolved business entities.

rows.trigger: MANDATORY MINIMUM of 3 years' imprisonment for any conviction under (8)(b), by either branch.
rows.quote: Notwithstanding any other provision of law, the court shall sentence any person convicted of committing the offense described in this paragraph to a mandatory minimum sentence of 3 years' imprisonment.

rows.trigger: Aggravated fraudulent use of the personal identification information of multiple deceased individuals or dissolved business entities, VALUE BRANCH, $50,000 or more. max null because no upper dollar limit is stated in the paragraph.
rows.quote: Any person who willfully and fraudulently uses personal identification information concerning a deceased individual or dissolved business entity commits the offense of aggravated fraudulent use of the personal identification information of multiple deceased individuals or dissolved business entities, a felony of the first degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084, if the pecuniary benefit, the value of the services received, the payment sought to be avoided, or the amount of injury or fraud perpetrated is $50,000 or more

rows.trigger: DECEASED / DISSOLVED ENTITY, COUNT BRANCH, disjunctive with the value branch. 20 or more but fewer than 30 deceased individuals or dissolved business entities. NO DOLLAR LOWER BOUND: first degree at ANY dollar value. min/max are a COUNT, not dollars.
rows.quote: or if the person fraudulently uses the personal identification information of 20 or more but fewer than 30 deceased individuals or dissolved business entities.

rows.trigger: MANDATORY MINIMUM of 5 years' imprisonment for any conviction under (8)(c), by either branch. Statute phrases this one as 'minimum mandatory' rather than 'mandatory minimum'.
rows.quote: Notwithstanding any other provision of law, the court shall sentence any person convicted of the offense described in this paragraph to a minimum mandatory sentence of 5 years' imprisonment.

rows.trigger: ESCALATED MANDATORY MINIMUM of 10 years' imprisonment. Two disjunctive triggers in one sentence: value of $100,000 or more (min recorded here), OR 30 or more deceased individuals or dissolved business entities with NO DOLLAR LOWER BOUND and no upper count limit. Degree stays first degree felony. TEXTUAL NOTE, RECORDED NOT INFERRED: the degree-assigning clause of (8)(c) reaches only '20 or more but fewer than 30', so 30-or-more appears expressly only in this mandatory-minimum sentence.
rows.quote: If the pecuniary benefit, the value of the services received, the payment sought to be avoided, or the amount of the injury or fraud perpetrated is $100,000 or more, or if the person fraudulently uses the personal identification information of 30 or more deceased individuals or dissolved business entities, notwithstanding any other provision of law, the court shall sentence any person convicted of an offense described in this paragraph to a mandatory minimum sentence of 10 years' imprisonment.

rows.trigger: COUNTERFEIT OR FICTITIOUS personal identification information, as defined in (1)(g). Creating, using, or possessing with intent to fraudulently use such information concerning a FICTITIOUS person, or concerning a real person without consent, with intent to commit or facilitate a fraud on another person. NO LOWER BOUND: no dollar amount and no victim count, and no tiered ladder exists in this subsection at all.
rows.quote: Any person who willfully and fraudulently creates or uses, or possesses with intent to fraudulently use, counterfeit or fictitious personal identification information concerning a fictitious person, or concerning a real person without first obtaining that real person's consent, with intent to use such counterfeit or fictitious personal identification information for the purpose of committing or facilitating the commission of a fraud on another person, commits the offense of fraudulent creation or use, or possession with intent to fraudulently use, counterfeit or fictitious personal identification information, a felony of the third degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.trigger: RECLASSIFICATION UP ONE DEGREE where, for the purpose of obtaining or using personal identification information, the offender misrepresents himself or herself as a law enforcement officer, or as an employee or representative of a bank, credit card company, credit counseling company, or credit reporting agency, or wrongfully represents that he or she is seeking to assist the victim with a credit history problem. A misdemeanor becomes a third degree felony. NO LOWER BOUND.
rows.quote: Any person who commits an offense described in this section and for the purpose of obtaining or using personal identification information misrepresents himself or herself to be a law enforcement officer; an employee or representative of a bank, credit card company, credit counseling company, or credit reporting agency; or any person who wrongfully represents that he or she is seeking to assist the victim with a problem with the victim's credit history shall have the offense reclassified as follows:(a) In the case of a misdemeanor, the offense is reclassified as a felony of the third degree.

rows.trigger: RECLASSIFICATION for impersonation. A third degree felony becomes a second degree felony. NO LOWER BOUND.
rows.quote: (b) In the case of a felony of the third degree, the offense is reclassified as a felony of the second degree.

rows.trigger: RECLASSIFICATION for impersonation. A second degree felony becomes a first degree felony. NO LOWER BOUND.
rows.quote: (c) In the case of a felony of the second degree, the offense is reclassified as a felony of the first degree.

rows.trigger: RECLASSIFICATION for impersonation, TOP OF THE LADDER. A first degree felony, or a first degree felony punishable by a term of imprisonment not exceeding life, becomes a LIFE FELONY. NO LOWER BOUND: no dollar amount and no victim count. This is the highest degree anywhere in s. 817.568 and exists only in subsection (10); subsection (5) has no counterpart.
rows.quote: (d) In the case of a felony of the first degree or a felony of the first degree punishable by a term of imprisonment not exceeding life, the offense is reclassified as a life felony.

rows.trigger: SENTENCING-LEVEL ENHANCEMENT accompanying the impersonation reclassification. A reclassified felony is ranked one level above its ranking under s. 921.0022 OR s. 921.0023, and a reclassified misdemeanor is ranked in level 2. Differs from the (5) closing paragraph in citing s. 921.0023 as well and in omitting any chapter 944 gain-time reference. level field left null because neither ranking chart was opened.
rows.quote: For purposes of sentencing under chapter 921, a felony offense that is reclassified under this subsection is ranked one level above the ranking under s. 921.0022 or s. 921.0023 of the felony offense committed, and a misdemeanor offense that is reclassified under this subsection is ranked in level 2 of the offense severity ranking chart.

rows.trigger: PROTECTED-VICTIM CLASSES, seven of them, disjunctive: an individual 60 or older; a disabled adult as defined in s. 825.101; a public servant as defined in s. 838.014; a veteran as defined in s. 1.01; a first responder as defined in s. 125.01045; an individual employed by the State of Florida; or an individual employed by the Federal Government. NO LOWER BOUND: no dollar amount and no victim count. A single victim in any one class is enough. This subsection overlaps (6) as to 60-and-older victims.
rows.quote: A person who willfully and without authorization fraudulently uses personal identification information concerning an individual who is 60 years of age or older; a disabled adult as defined in s. 825.101; a public servant as defined in s. 838.014; a veteran as defined in s. 1.01; a first responder as defined in s. 125.01045; an individual who is employed by the State of Florida; or an individual who is employed by the Federal Government without first obtaining the consent of that individual commits a felony of the second degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.trigger: MANDATORY, NON-WAIVABLE MONETARY PENALTY. A $1,001 surcharge is imposed on ANY violation of this section, in addition to any other sanction, on a plea of guilty or nolo contendere or a finding of guilt regardless of adjudication. Applies to every subsection, including the (4) first degree misdemeanor. Distribution is set out in (12)(a) through (12)(c); (12)(d) makes it non-waivable and requires inclusion in a restitution judgment. NO LOWER BOUND.
rows.quote: In addition to any sanction imposed when a person pleads guilty or nolo contendere to, or is found guilty of, regardless of adjudication, a violation of this section, the court shall impose a surcharge of $1,001. ... (d) The surcharge may not be waived by the court. In the event that the person has been ordered to pay restitution in accordance with s. 775.089, the surcharge shall be included in a judgment.

rows.trigger: SUBSTANTIAL ASSISTANCE. The only downward mechanism in the section, recorded because it is the sole textual route around the (2)(b), (2)(c), (8)(b), and (8)(c) mandatory minimums. Requires a prosecutor's motion; the judge MAY reduce or suspend. NO LOWER BOUND.
rows.quote: The prosecutor may move the sentencing court to reduce or suspend the sentence of any person who is convicted of a violation of this section and who provides substantial assistance in the identification, arrest, or conviction of any of that person's accomplices, accessories, coconspirators, or principals or of any other person engaged in fraudulent possession or use of personal identification information. ... The judge hearing the motion may reduce or suspend the sentence if the judge finds that the defendant rendered such substantial assistance.

usc-18-1956.title: 18 U.S.C. §1956 - Laundering of monetary instruments
