rows.trigger: NO LOWER BOUND. Federal statute assigns no felony degree. Conducting or attempting a financial transaction knowing the property represents proceeds of some form of unlawful activity, where the transaction in fact involves proceeds of specified unlawful activity, PLUS any one of the four alternative mental states in (A)(i), (A)(ii), (B)(i), or (B)(ii). There is no dollar threshold of any kind: the $500,000 figure is a FINE CAP, not a value trigger. Any amount, however small, is covered.
rows.quote: Whoever, knowing that the property involved in a financial transaction represents the proceeds of some form of unlawful activity, conducts or attempts to conduct such a financial transaction which in fact involves the proceeds of specified unlawful activity- ... shall be sentenced to a fine of not more than $500,000 or twice the value of the property involved in the transaction, whichever is greater, or imprisonment for not more than twenty years, or both. For purposes of this paragraph, a financial transaction shall be considered to be one involving the proceeds of specified unlawful activity if it is part of a set of parallel or dependent transactions, any one of which involves the proceeds of specified unlawful activity, and all of which are part of a single plan or arrangement.

rows.trigger: NO LOWER BOUND. Alternative mental state 1 of 4 under (a)(1): intent to promote the carrying on of specified unlawful activity. Carries the flush penalty of (a)(1) (fine up to the greater of $500,000 or twice the value of the property, imprisonment up to 20 years, or both). No value element.
rows.quote: (A)(i) with the intent to promote the carrying on of specified unlawful activity; or

rows.trigger: NO LOWER BOUND. Alternative mental state 2 of 4 under (a)(1): intent to engage in tax evasion or false-return conduct. Carries the same flush penalty of (a)(1). No value element.
rows.quote: (ii) with intent to engage in conduct constituting a violation of section 7201 or 7206 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986; or

rows.trigger: NO LOWER BOUND. Alternative mental state 3 of 4 under (a)(1), reached through the (B) chapeau 'knowing that the transaction is designed in whole or in part-': concealment. Carries the same flush penalty of (a)(1). No value element.
rows.quote: (B) knowing that the transaction is designed in whole or in part- (i) to conceal or disguise the nature, the location, the source, the ownership, or the control of the proceeds of specified unlawful activity; or

rows.trigger: NO LOWER BOUND. Alternative mental state 4 of 4 under (a)(1): avoiding a transaction reporting requirement. Carries the same flush penalty of (a)(1). No value element, and note this reaches structuring-type intent with no dollar floor stated in this section.
rows.quote: (ii) to avoid a transaction reporting requirement under State or Federal law,

rows.trigger: NO LOWER BOUND. International transportation, transmission, or transfer of a monetary instrument or funds into or out of the United States, plus a mental state under (A) or (B). No dollar threshold: the $500,000 figure is a FINE CAP, not a trigger. Any amount is covered.
rows.quote: Whoever transports, transmits, or transfers, or attempts to transport, transmit, or transfer a monetary instrument or funds from a place in the United States to or through a place outside the United States or to a place in the United States from or through a place outside the United States- ... shall be sentenced to a fine of not more than $500,000 or twice the value of the monetary instrument or funds involved in the transportation, transmission, or transfer, whichever is greater, or imprisonment for not more than twenty years, or both. For the purpose of the offense described in subparagraph (B), the defendant's knowledge may be established by proof that a law enforcement officer represented the matter specified in subparagraph (B) as true, and the defendant's subsequent statements or actions indicate that the defendant believed such representations to be true.

rows.trigger: NO LOWER BOUND. Alternative mental state under (a)(2): intent to promote specified unlawful activity. Note this subparagraph does NOT require knowledge that the funds are criminal proceeds, unlike (B). Carries the flush penalty of (a)(2).
rows.quote: (A) with the intent to promote the carrying on of specified unlawful activity; or

rows.trigger: NO LOWER BOUND. Alternative mental state under (a)(2) via the (B) chapeau: knowledge of criminal proceeds plus concealment design. Carries the flush penalty of (a)(2). Government's proof of knowledge may be by law enforcement representation (sting) under the flush language.
rows.quote: (B) knowing that the monetary instrument or funds involved in the transportation, transmission, or transfer represent the proceeds of some form of unlawful activity and knowing that such transportation, transmission, or transfer is designed in whole or in part- (i) to conceal or disguise the nature, the location, the source, the ownership, or the control of the proceeds of specified unlawful activity; or

rows.trigger: NO LOWER BOUND. Alternative mental state under (a)(2) via the (B) chapeau: knowledge of criminal proceeds plus design to avoid a reporting requirement. Carries the flush penalty of (a)(2). No value element.
rows.quote: (ii) to avoid a transaction reporting requirement under State or Federal law,

rows.trigger: NO LOWER BOUND. Sting / undercover offense: the property need only be REPRESENTED to be proceeds of specified unlawful activity, or property used to conduct or facilitate specified unlawful activity. Actual criminal proceeds are not required. No dollar threshold at all. Penalty is a fine under this title (no $500,000 cap language) and up to 20 years.
rows.quote: Whoever, with the intent- ... conducts or attempts to conduct a financial transaction involving property represented to be the proceeds of specified unlawful activity, or property used to conduct or facilitate specified unlawful activity, shall be fined under this title or imprisoned for not more than 20 years, or both. For purposes of this paragraph and paragraph (2), the term "represented" means any representation made by a law enforcement officer or by another person at the direction of, or with the approval of, a Federal official authorized to investigate or prosecute violations of this section.

rows.trigger: NO LOWER BOUND. Alternative intent 1 of 3 under (a)(3): promotion. Carries the flush penalty of (a)(3).
rows.quote: (A) to promote the carrying on of specified unlawful activity;

rows.trigger: NO LOWER BOUND. Alternative intent 2 of 3 under (a)(3): concealment of property BELIEVED to be proceeds. Carries the flush penalty of (a)(3).
rows.quote: (B) to conceal or disguise the nature, location, source, ownership, or control of property believed to be the proceeds of specified unlawful activity; or

rows.trigger: NO LOWER BOUND. Alternative intent 3 of 3 under (a)(3): avoiding a transaction reporting requirement. Carries the flush penalty of (a)(3).
rows.quote: (C) to avoid a transaction reporting requirement under State or Federal law,

rows.trigger: NO LOWER BOUND. CIVIL penalty, not a criminal degree, and it is cumulative with the criminal penalties. Reaches conduct described in (a)(1), (a)(3), (a)(2), OR section 1957. The penalty is the GREATER of the two figures in (A) and (B), so $10,000 operates as a FLOOR on the penalty amount, not as a threshold the conduct must meet.
rows.quote: (1) In general.-Whoever conducts or attempts to conduct a transaction described in subsection (a)(1) or (a)(3), or section 1957, or a transportation, transmission, or transfer described in subsection (a)(2), is liable to the United States for a civil penalty of not more than the greater of- (A) the value of the property, funds, or monetary instruments involved in the transaction; or (B) $10,000.

rows.trigger: First of two alternative civil penalty measures under (b)(1); the court applies whichever of (A) and (B) is greater. Value-based measure, uncapped upward and with no minimum.
rows.quote: (A) the value of the property, funds, or monetary instruments involved in the transaction; or

rows.trigger: Second of two alternative civil penalty measures under (b)(1): a flat $10,000. This is the amount of the penalty when it exceeds the value of the property; it is NOT a value threshold for liability.

NO LOWER BOUND. Conspiracy to commit any §1956 or §1957 offense carries the SAME penalty as the completed object offense. No overt act requirement stated, no reduction from the substantive penalty, no value element.
rows.quote: (h) Any person who conspires to commit any offense defined in this section or section 1957 shall be subject to the same penalties as those prescribed for the offense the commission of which was the object of the conspiracy.

rows.trigger: JURISDICTIONAL threshold, not a penalty tier and not a degree trigger. Extraterritorial jurisdiction requires BOTH (f)(1) (conduct by a U.S. citizen, or conduct occurring in part in the U.S. by a non-citizen) AND (f)(2) value exceeding $10,000. The statute says 'exceeding $10,000', so the stated figure is exclusive; the recorded min of 10000 is the exclusive floor, not an inclusive one. This threshold applies ONLY to the extraterritorial jurisdiction question and does NOT limit domestic prosecutions under (a), which have no dollar floor.
rows.quote: (f) There is extraterritorial jurisdiction over the conduct prohibited by this section if- (1) the conduct is by a United States citizen or, in the case of a non-United States citizen, the conduct occurs in part in the United States; and (2) the transaction or series of related transactions involves funds or monetary instruments of a value exceeding $10,000.

rows.trigger: PREDICATE-QUALIFYING value threshold inside the definition of 'specified unlawful activity'. Only this one clause within the very long (c)(7)(D) list carries a dollar floor: a felony violation of section 15 of the Food and Nutrition Act of 2008 qualifies as a predicate only if the benefits involved are worth not less than $5,000. Every other offense listed in (c)(7)(D) qualifies as a predicate at ANY value. Do not read this $5,000 figure as a general threshold for §1956.
rows.quote: any felony violation of section 15 of the Food and Nutrition Act of 2008 (relating to supplemental nutrition assistance program benefits fraud) involving a quantity of benefits having a value of not less than $5,000

rows.trigger: PREDICATE-QUALIFYING value threshold inside the definition of 'specified unlawful activity'. Endangered Species Act, African Elephant Conservation Act, and Rhinoceros and Tiger Conservation Act violations qualify as predicates only if the fish, wildlife, products, items, or substances involved in the violation AND the relevant conduct total more than $10,000. Statute says 'more than $10,000', so the recorded min of 10000 is an exclusive floor.
rows.quote: (G) any act that is a criminal violation of subparagraph (A), (B), (C), (D), (E), or (F) of paragraph (1) of section 9(a) of the Endangered Species Act of 1973 (16 U.S.C. 1538(a)(1)), section 2203 of the African Elephant Conservation Act (16 U.S.C. 4223), or section 7(a) of the Rhinoceros and Tiger Conservation Act of 1994 (16 U.S.C. 5305a(a)), if the endangered or threatened species of fish or wildlife, products, items, or substances involved in the violation and relevant conduct, as applicable, have a total value of more than $10,000;

rows.trigger: NO LOWER BOUND. Definitional provision that widens liability rather than narrowing it: the defendant need not know WHICH form of unlawful activity produced the property, and the underlying activity need not be one of the offenses enumerated in (c)(7). Any felony under State, Federal, or foreign law satisfies the knowledge element. Recorded because it materially controls whether the (a) penalties attach.
rows.quote: (1) the term "knowing that the property involved in a financial transaction represents the proceeds of some form of unlawful activity" means that the person knew the property involved in the transaction represented proceeds from some form, though not necessarily which form, of activity that constitutes a felony under State, Federal, or foreign law, regardless of whether or not such activity is specified in paragraph (7);

rows.trigger: PUNISHMENT LIMIT, not a degree or enhancement. Applies ONLY where the specified unlawful activity is a foreign offense defined in (c)(7)(B): a 7-year limitations period, notwithstanding the general period in section 3282. No value element.
rows.quote: (j) Seven-year Limitation.-Notwithstanding section 3282, no person shall be prosecuted, tried, or punished for a violation of this section or section 1957 if the specified unlawful activity constituting the violation is the activity defined in subsection (c)(7)(B) of this section, unless the indictment is found or the information is instituted not later than 7 years after the date on which the offense was committed.

rows.trigger: Non-preemption / cumulative-punishment clause. No degree, no minimum, no enhancement of its own, but it expressly preserves additional criminal penalties and civil remedies under other law, so §1956 penalties are not exclusive.
rows.quote: (d) Nothing in this section shall supersede any provision of Federal, State, or other law imposing criminal penalties or affording civil remedies in addition to those provided for in this section.

usc-18-924.title: Penalties (federal firearms offenses, Chapter 44)

rows.trigger: NO VALUE THRESHOLD. Catch-all for the four enumerated acts in (A) false statement in required records or license/exemption/relief application; (B) knowing violation of 922(a)(4),(f),(k),(q); (C) knowing import in violation of 922(l); (D) willful violation of any other provision of the chapter. Federal statute assigns no Florida-style degree.

rows.trigger: Cocaine base. Values in GRAMS. No express upper bound in the text; max recorded as the (A)(iii) threshold.
rows.quote: (iii) 28 grams or more of a mixture or substance described in clause (ii) which contains cocaine base;

rows.trigger: Phencyclidine (PCP). TWO alternative thresholds in GRAMS: 10 grams of PCP itself, OR 100 grams of a mixture containing a detectable amount of PCP. min/max recorded on the pure-PCP figures; mixture range is 100 to 1,000 grams.
rows.quote: (iv) 10 grams or more of phencyclidine (PCP) or 100 grams or more of a mixture or substance containing a detectable amount of phencyclidine (PCP);

rows.trigger: LSD. Values in GRAMS. No express upper bound in the text; max recorded as the (A)(v) threshold.
rows.quote: (v) 1 gram or more of a mixture or substance containing a detectable amount of lysergic acid diethylamide (LSD);

rows.trigger: Fentanyl. TWO alternative thresholds in GRAMS: 40 grams of a fentanyl mixture, OR 10 grams of any analogue or a fentanyl-related substance. min/max recorded on the analogue/fentanyl-related figures (10 to 100 grams); the fentanyl-mixture range is 40 to 400 grams.
rows.quote: (vi) 40 grams or more of a mixture or substance containing a detectable amount of N-phenyl-N- [ 1- ( 2-phenylethyl ) -4-piperidinyl ] propanamide or 10 grams or more of a mixture or substance containing a detectable amount of any analogue of N-phenyl-N-[1-(2-phenylethyl)-4-piperidinyl] propanamide or a fentanyl-related substance;

rows.trigger: Marihuana. Weight in GRAMS (100 kilograms). SECOND, INDEPENDENT trigger with no weight element: 100 or more marihuana plants regardless of weight (plant range 100 to 1,000).
rows.quote: (vii) 100 kilograms or more of a mixture or substance containing a detectable amount of marihuana, or 100 or more marihuana plants regardless of weight; or

rows.trigger: Methamphetamine. TWO alternative thresholds in GRAMS: 5 grams pure, OR 50 grams of a mixture. min/max recorded on the pure figures; mixture range is 50 to 500 grams.
rows.quote: (viii) 5 grams or more of methamphetamine, its salts, isomers, and salts of its isomers or 50 grams or more of a mixture or substance containing a detectable amount of methamphetamine, its salts, isomers, or salts of its isomers;

rows.trigger: Death or serious bodily injury results from use of the substance; mandatory minimum rises from 5 years to 20 years and the maximum rises from 40 years to life.
rows.quote: and if death or serious bodily injury results from the use of such substance shall be not less than 20 years or more than life, a fine not to exceed the greater of that authorized in accordance with the provisions of title 18 or $5,000,000 if the defendant is an individual or $25,000,000 if the defendant is other than an individual, or both.

rows.trigger: One prior final conviction for a serious drug felony or serious violent felony; mandatory minimum 10 years, maximum life, and mandatory LIFE if death or serious bodily injury results.
rows.quote: If any person commits such a violation after a prior conviction for a serious drug felony or serious violent felony has become final, such person shall be sentenced to a term of imprisonment which may not be less than 10 years and not more than life imprisonment and if death or serious bodily injury results from the use of such substance shall be sentenced to life imprisonment, a fine not to exceed the greater of twice that authorized in accordance with the provisions of title 18 or $8,000,000 if the defendant is an individual or $50,000,000 if the defendant is other than an individual, or both.

rows.trigger: Mandatory minimum supervised release: at least 4 years with no prior conviction, at least 8 years with such a prior conviction.
rows.quote: Notwithstanding section 3583 of title 18, any sentence imposed under this subparagraph shall, in the absence of such a prior conviction, include a term of supervised release of at least 4 years in addition to such term of imprisonment and shall, if there was such a prior conviction, include a term of supervised release of at least 8 years in addition to such term of imprisonment.

rows.trigger: No probation, no suspended sentence, no parole for anyone sentenced under this subparagraph.
rows.quote: Notwithstanding any other provision of law, the court shall not place on probation or suspend the sentence of any person sentenced under this subparagraph. No person sentenced under this subparagraph shall be eligible for parole during the term of imprisonment imposed therein.

rows.trigger: NO LOWER BOUND. Any schedule I or II controlled substance in ANY quantity that is not covered by subparagraphs (A), (B), or (D); also gamma hydroxybutyric acid (including when scheduled as an approved drug product) and 1 gram of flunitrazepam. Maximum 20 years, no mandatory minimum in the base case.
rows.quote: (C) In the case of a controlled substance in schedule I or II, gamma hydroxybutyric acid (including when scheduled as an approved drug product for purposes of section 3(a)(1)(B) of the Hillory J. Farias and Samantha Reid Date-Rape Drug Prohibition Act of 2000), or 1 gram of flunitrazepam, except as provided in subparagraphs (A), (B), and (D), such person shall be sentenced to a term of imprisonment of not more than 20 years

rows.trigger: Death or serious bodily injury results from use of the substance. This converts a no-minimum, 20-year-max offense into a 20-year MANDATORY MINIMUM with a maximum of life, with NO LOWER BOUND on quantity.
rows.quote: and if death or serious bodily injury results from the use of such substance shall be sentenced to a term of imprisonment of not less than twenty years or more than life, a fine not to exceed the greater of that authorized in accordance with the provisions of title 18 or $1,000,000 if the defendant is an individual or $5,000,000 if the defendant is other than an individual, or both.

rows.trigger: Prior final conviction for a felony drug offense (note: a different and broader predicate than the "serious drug felony or serious violent felony" used in (A) and (B)); maximum rises to 30 years, and to mandatory LIFE if death or serious bodily injury results.
rows.quote: If any person commits such a violation after a prior conviction for a felony drug offense has become final, such person shall be sentenced to a term of imprisonment of not more than 30 years and if death or serious bodily injury results from the use of such substance shall be sentenced to life imprisonment, a fine not to exceed the greater of twice that authorized in accordance with the provisions of title 18 or $2,000,000 if the defendant is an individual or $10,000,000 if the defendant is other than an individual, or both.

rows.trigger: Mandatory minimum supervised release: at least 3 years with no prior conviction, at least 6 years with such a prior conviction.
rows.quote: Notwithstanding section 3583 of title 18, any sentence imposing a term of imprisonment under this paragraph shall, in the absence of such a prior conviction, impose a term of supervised release of at least 3 years in addition to such term of imprisonment and shall, if there was such a prior conviction, impose a term of supervised release of at least 6 years in addition to such term of imprisonment.

rows.trigger: Probation/suspension and parole are barred only for the death-or-serious-bodily-injury mandatory-minimum branch of this subparagraph, not for the whole subparagraph.
rows.quote: Notwithstanding any other provision of law, the court shall not place on probation or suspend the sentence of any person sentenced under the provisions of this subparagraph which provide for a mandatory term of imprisonment if death or serious bodily injury results, nor shall a person so sentenced be eligible for parole during the term of such a sentence.

rows.trigger: NO LOWER BOUND. Marihuana under 50 kilograms (max recorded in GRAMS), hashish under 10 kilograms, or hashish oil under one kilogram. Carve-out: does NOT apply where there are 50 or more marihuana plants regardless of weight. Also expressly subject to paragraphs (4) and (5). Maximum 5 years, no mandatory minimum.
rows.quote: (D) In the case of less than 50 kilograms of marihuana, except in the case of 50 or more marihuana plants regardless of weight, 10 kilograms of hashish, or one kilogram of hashish oil, such person shall, except as provided in paragraphs (4) and (5) of this subsection, be sentenced to a term of imprisonment of not more than 5 years, a fine not to exceed the greater of that authorized in accordance with the provisions of title 18 or $250,000 if the defendant is an individual or $1,000,000 if the defendant is other than an individual, or both.

rows.trigger: Prior final conviction for a felony drug offense; maximum doubles from 5 to 10 years.
rows.quote: If any person commits such a violation after a prior conviction for a felony drug offense has become final, such person shall be sentenced to a term of imprisonment of not more than 10 years, a fine not to exceed the greater of twice that authorized in accordance with the provisions of title 18 or $500,000 if the defendant is an individual or $2,000,000 if the defendant is other than an individual, or both.

rows.trigger: Mandatory minimum supervised release: at least 2 years with no prior conviction, at least 4 years with such a prior conviction.
rows.quote: Notwithstanding section 3583 of title 18, any sentence imposing a term of imprisonment under this paragraph shall, in the absence of such a prior conviction, impose a term of supervised release of at least 2 years in addition to such term of imprisonment and shall, if there was such a prior conviction, impose a term of supervised release of at least 4 years in addition to such term of imprisonment.

rows.trigger: NO LOWER BOUND. Any schedule III controlled substance in any quantity, except as provided in subparagraphs (C) and (D). Maximum 10 years; 15 years if death or serious bodily injury results (a victim-based enhancement with no quantity trigger).
rows.quote: (E)(i) Except as provided in subparagraphs (C) and (D), in the case of any controlled substance in schedule III, such person shall be sentenced to a term of imprisonment of not more than 10 years and if death or serious bodily injury results from the use of such substance shall be sentenced to a term of imprisonment of not more than 15 years, a fine not to exceed the greater of that authorized in accordance with the provisions of title 18 or $500,000 if the defendant is an individual or $2,500,000 if the defendant is other than an individual, or both.

rows.trigger: Prior final conviction for a felony drug offense; schedule III maximum rises to 20 years, or 30 years if death or serious bodily injury results.
rows.quote: (ii) If any person commits such a violation after a prior conviction for a felony drug offense has become final, such person shall be sentenced to a term of imprisonment of not more than 20 years and if death or serious bodily injury results from the use of such substance shall be sentenced to a term of imprisonment of not more than 30 years, a fine not to exceed the greater of twice that authorized in accordance with the provisions of title 18 or $1,000,000 if the defendant is an individual or $5,000,000 if the defendant is other than an individual, or both.

rows.trigger: Mandatory minimum supervised release: at least 2 years with no prior conviction, at least 4 years with such a prior conviction.
rows.quote: (iii) Any sentence imposing a term of imprisonment under this subparagraph shall, in the absence of such a prior conviction, impose a term of supervised release of at least 2 years in addition to such term of imprisonment and shall, if there was such a prior conviction, impose a term of supervised release of at least 4 years in addition to such term of imprisonment.

rows.trigger: NO LOWER BOUND. Any schedule IV controlled substance in any quantity. Maximum 5 years; 10 years after a prior final felony drug offense conviction; mandatory supervised release of at least 1 year (2 years with a prior).
rows.quote: (2) In the case of a controlled substance in schedule IV, such person shall be sentenced to a term of imprisonment of not more than 5 years, a fine not to exceed the greater of that authorized in accordance with the provisions of title 18 or $250,000 if the defendant is an individual or $1,000,000 if the defendant is other than an individual, or both. If any person commits such a violation after a prior conviction for a felony drug offense has become final, such person shall be sentenced to a term of imprisonment of not more than 10 years, a fine not to exceed the greater of twice that authorized in accordance with the provisions of title 18 or $500,000 if the defendant is an individual or $2,000,000 if the defendant is other than an individual, or both. Any sentence imposing a term of imprisonment under this paragraph shall, in the absence of such a prior conviction, impose a term of supervised release of at least one year in addition to such term of imprisonment and shall, if there was such a prior conviction, impose a term of supervised release of at least 2 years in addition to such term of imprisonment.

rows.trigger: NO LOWER BOUND. Any schedule V controlled substance in any quantity. Maximum one year; 4 years after a prior final felony drug offense conviction. Supervised release here is permissive ("may") and only with a prior, unlike every other tier.
rows.quote: (3) In the case of a controlled substance in schedule V, such person shall be sentenced to a term of imprisonment of not more than one year, a fine not to exceed the greater of that authorized in accordance with the provisions of title 18 or $100,000 if the defendant is an individual or $250,000 if the defendant is other than an individual, or both. If any person commits such a violation after a prior conviction for a felony drug offense has become final, such person shall be sentenced to a term of imprisonment of not more than 4 years, a fine not to exceed the greater of twice that authorized in accordance with the provisions of title 18 or $200,000 if the defendant is an individual or $500,000 if the defendant is other than an individual, or both. Any sentence imposing a term of imprisonment under this paragraph may, if there was a prior conviction, impose a term of supervised release of not more than 1 year, in addition to such term of imprisonment.

rows.trigger: Mitigating provision, not an enhancement: distributing a small amount of marihuana for no remuneration. "Small amount" is undefined and has NO numeric bound in either direction. Displaces paragraph (1)(D) and routes the offender to simple-possession treatment under §844 and 18 U.S.C. §3607.
rows.quote: (4) Notwithstanding paragraph (1)(D) of this subsection, any person who violates subsection (a) of this section by distributing a small amount of marihuana for no remuneration shall be treated as provided in section 844 of this title and section 3607 of title 18.

rows.trigger: Cultivating or manufacturing a controlled substance on Federal property. NO LOWER BOUND on quantity. Imprisonment as otherwise provided in subsection (b); the enhancement is to the fine ceiling, which becomes the greatest of the four listed amounts.
rows.quote: (5) Any person who violates subsection (a) of this section by cultivating or manufacturing a controlled substance on Federal property shall be imprisoned as provided in this subsection and shall be fined any amount not to exceed— (A) the amount authorized in accordance with this section; (B) the amount authorized in accordance with the provisions of title 18; (C) $500,000 if the defendant is an individual; or (D) $1,000,000 if the defendant is other than an individual; or both.

rows.trigger: Violating subsection (a) OR ATTEMPTING to do so while knowingly or intentionally using a poison, chemical, or other hazardous substance on Federal land, where the use does any ONE of three things: (A) creates a serious hazard to humans, wildlife, or domestic animals, (B) degrades or harms the environment or natural resources, or (C) pollutes an aquifer, spring, stream, river, or body of water. NO LOWER BOUND on quantity. Separate five-year maximum.
rows.quote: (6) Any person who violates subsection (a), or attempts to do so, and knowingly or intentionally uses a poison, chemical, or other hazardous substance on Federal land, and, by such use— (A) creates a serious hazard to humans, wildlife, or domestic animals, (B) degrades or harms the environment or natural resources, or (C) pollutes an aquifer, spring, stream, river, or body of water, shall be fined in accordance with title 18 or imprisoned not more than five years, or both.

rows.trigger: Distributing a controlled substance or controlled substance analogue to an individual without that individual's knowledge, with intent to commit a crime of violence (as defined in 18 U.S.C. §16, including rape) against that individual. NO LOWER BOUND on quantity and no schedule limitation. Maximum 20 years.
rows.quote: (A) In general.—Whoever, with intent to commit a crime of violence, as defined in section 16 of title 18 (including rape), against an individual, violates subsection (a) by distributing a controlled substance or controlled substance analogue to that individual without that individual's knowledge, shall be imprisoned not more than 20 years and fined in accordance with title 18.

rows.trigger: Definitional only; assigns no penalty. Defines the "without that individual's knowledge" element of (b)(7)(A).
rows.quote: (B) Definition.—For purposes of this paragraph, the term "without that individual's knowledge" means that the individual is unaware that a substance with the ability to alter that individual's ability to appraise conduct or to decline participation in or communicate unwillingness to participate in conduct is administered to the individual.

rows.trigger: Possessing a listed chemical with intent to manufacture a controlled substance. NO LOWER BOUND on quantity. Maximum 20 years if a list I chemical; otherwise 10 years.
rows.quote: (1) possesses a listed chemical with intent to manufacture a controlled substance except as authorized by this subchapter; ... shall be fined in accordance with title 18 or imprisoned not more than 20 years in the case of a violation of paragraph (1) or (2) involving a list I chemical or not more than 10 years in the case of a violation of this subsection other than a violation of paragraph (1) or (2) involving a list I chemical, or both.

rows.trigger: Possessing OR distributing a listed chemical knowing, or having reasonable cause to believe, it will be used to manufacture a controlled substance. NO LOWER BOUND on quantity. Maximum 20 years if a list I chemical; otherwise 10 years.
rows.quote: (2) possesses or distributes a listed chemical knowing, or having reasonable cause to believe, that the listed chemical will be used to manufacture a controlled substance except as authorized by this subchapter; or

rows.trigger: Structuring: receiving or distributing a reportable amount of any listed chemical in units small enough to avoid §830 recordkeeping/reporting, with intent to cause evasion. This paragraph never carries the 20-year list I penalty — it is always capped at 10 years, because the 20-year clause reaches only paragraphs (1) and (2).
rows.quote: (3) with the intent of causing the evasion of the recordkeeping or reporting requirements of section 830 of this title, or the regulations issued under that section, receives or distributes a reportable amount of any listed chemical in units small enough so that the making of records or filing of reports under that section is not required;

rows.trigger: Assembling, maintaining, placing, or causing to be placed a boobytrap on Federal property where a controlled substance is being manufactured, distributed, or dispensed. Maximum 10 years.
rows.quote: (1) Any person who assembles, maintains, places, or causes to be placed a boobytrap on Federal property where a controlled substance is being manufactured, distributed, or dispensed shall be sentenced to a term of imprisonment for not more than 10 years or fined under title 18, or both.

rows.trigger: One or more prior convictions for an offense punishable under subsection (d); maximum doubles to 20 years. Note the predicate is not required to be "final," unlike the (b) enhancements.
rows.quote: (2) If any person commits such a violation after 1 or more prior convictions for an offense punishable under this subsection, such person shall be sentenced to a term of imprisonment of not more than 20 years or fined under title 18, or both.

rows.trigger: Definitional only; assigns no penalty. Defines "boobytrap."
rows.quote: (3) For the purposes of this subsection, the term "boobytrap" means any concealed or camouflaged device designed to cause bodily injury when triggered by any action of any unsuspecting person making contact with the device. Such term includes guns, ammunition, or explosive devices attached to trip wires or other triggering mechanisms, sharpened stakes, and lines or wires with hooks attached.

rows.trigger: Additional, cumulative penalty (not a substitute): a person convicted of ANY felony violation of §841 relating to receipt, distribution, manufacture, exportation, or importation of a listed chemical may be enjoined from listed-chemical transactions for up to ten years.
rows.quote: In addition to any other applicable penalty, any person convicted of a felony violation of this section relating to the receipt, distribution, manufacture, exportation, or importation of a listed chemical may be enjoined from engaging in any transaction involving a listed chemical for not more than ten years.

rows.trigger: Knowingly distributing a listed chemical in violation of the subchapter, other than a §830 recordkeeping/reporting violation, and except to the extent §842(a)(12), (13), or (14) applies. NO LOWER BOUND on quantity. Maximum 5 years.
rows.quote: (1) Whoever knowingly distributes a listed chemical in violation of this subchapter (other than in violation of a recordkeeping or reporting requirement of section 830 of this title) shall, except to the extent that paragraph (12), (13), or (14) of section 842(a) of this title applies, be fined under title 18 or imprisoned not more than 5 years, or both.

rows.trigger: Possessing any listed chemical knowing §830 recordkeeping/reporting requirements have not been adhered to and failing to take immediate remedial steps after acquiring that knowledge. NO LOWER BOUND on quantity. Maximum one year.
rows.quote: (2) Whoever possesses any listed chemical, with knowledge that the recordkeeping or reporting requirements of section 830 of this title have not been adhered to, if, after such knowledge is acquired, such person does not take immediate steps to remedy the violation shall be fined under title 18 or imprisoned not more than one year, or both.

rows.trigger: Knowingly using the Internet to distribute a date rape drug knowing or with reasonable cause to believe EITHER (A) the drug would be used in the commission of criminal sexual conduct, OR (B) the person is not an authorized purchaser. Subparagraph (B) requires no sexual-conduct element at all — mere distribution to a non-authorized purchaser carries the same 20-year maximum. NO LOWER BOUND on quantity.
rows.quote: (1) Whoever knowingly uses the Internet to distribute a date rape drug to any person, knowing or with reasonable cause to believe that— (A) the drug would be used in the commission of criminal sexual conduct; or (B) the person is not an authorized purchaser; shall be fined under this subchapter or imprisoned not more than 20 years, or both.

rows.trigger: Definitional only; assigns no penalty. Defines "date rape drug" (GHB and its analogues including GBL and 1,4-butanediol; ketamine; flunitrazepam; and any substance the Attorney General designates by rulemaking) and "authorized purchaser."
rows.quote: (2) As used in this subsection: (A) The term "date rape drug" means— (i) gamma hydroxybutyric acid (GHB) or any controlled substance analogue of GHB, including gamma butyrolactone (GBL) or 1,4–butanediol; (ii) ketamine; (iii) flunitrazepam; or (iv) any substance which the Attorney General designates, pursuant to the rulemaking procedures prescribed by section 553 of title 5, to be used in committing rape or sexual assault.

rows.trigger: Rulemaking authority only; assigns no penalty. Records/reports required by these regulations become records or reports required under the chapter, which can expose a person to §842 liability.
rows.quote: (3) The Attorney General is authorized to promulgate regulations for record-keeping and reporting by persons handling 1,4–butanediol in order to implement and enforce the provisions of this section. Any record or report required by such regulations shall be considered a record or report required under this chapter.

rows.trigger: Prohibited-act provision: delivering, distributing, or dispensing a controlled substance by means of the Internet, or aiding or abetting such activity. Penalty comes from (h)(4).
rows.quote: (1) In general — It shall be unlawful for any person to knowingly or intentionally— (A) deliver, distribute, or dispense a controlled substance by means of the Internet, except as authorized by this subchapter; or (B) aid or abet (as such terms are used in section 2 of title 18) any activity described in subparagraph (A) that is not authorized by this subchapter.

rows.trigger: Non-exhaustive examples of conduct violating (h)(1) ("include, but are not limited to"); assigns no separate penalty. Includes unregistered online pharmacies, prescriptions written for Internet dispensation in violation of §829(e), acting as an intermediary bringing buyer and seller together, filling a prescription based solely on an online medical questionnaire, and false statements in §831 notifications or declarations.
rows.quote: (2) Examples — Examples of activities that violate paragraph (1) include, but are not limited to, knowingly or intentionally— (A) delivering, distributing, or dispensing a controlled substance by means of the Internet by an online pharmacy that is not validly registered with a modification authorizing such activity as required by section 823(g) of this title (unless exempt from such registration);

rows.trigger: Exemption provision; assigns no penalty. Excludes nonpractitioner delivery within registration, mere advocacy or pricing information posted online, and pure telecommunications/Internet access/hosting conduct — but subparagraph (B) withdraws the telecommunications and hosting exceptions from anyone acting in concert with a violator.
rows.quote: (B) The exceptions under subclauses (I) and (II) of subparagraph (A)(iii) shall not apply to a person acting in concert with a person who violates paragraph (1).

rows.trigger: Any knowing or intentional violation of subsection (h) is sentenced under the full subsection (b) ladder, including its mandatory minimums, rather than under a separate cap.
rows.quote: (4) Knowing or intentional violation — Any person who knowingly or intentionally violates this subsection shall be sentenced in accordance with subsection (b).

rows.quote: For purposes of determining which felony offenses are specifically listed in the offense severity ranking chart and which severity level has been assigned to each of these offenses, the numerical statutory references in the left column of the chart and the felony degree designations in the middle column of the chart are controlling; the language in the right column of the chart is provided solely for descriptive purposes. Reclassification of the degree of the felony through the application of s. 775.0845, s. 775.085, s. 775.0861, s. 775.0862, s. 775.0863, s. 775.087, s. 775.0875, s. 794.023, or any other law that provides an enhanced penalty for a felony offense, to any offense listed in the offense severity ranking chart in this section shall not cause the offense to become unlisted and is not subject to the provisions of s. 921.0023.

wrong: degree field carries non-degree values on two rows, contradicting the table's own section-level rule. Row '775.083(1) (introductory text, first clause -- capital felony exclusion)' sets degree = 'capital felony -- EXCLUDED from this section's fine authorization'; row '(second sentence -- noncriminal violation fine authority)' sets degree = 'noncriminal violation'. The table's own section-level row states 's. 775.083 assigns NO degree of offense anywhere ... Never cite this section as the source of an offense degree', and every other row correctly reads 'no degree assigned'. A consumer filtering by degree pulls two rows that assign nothing, and 'noncriminal violation' is not a degree of offense at all. Disclosed-but-wrong is still wrong in a typed field.

degree field is applied inconsistently in the opposite direction too: paragraphs (a) through (e) are the rows that actually name degrees in their operative text (life felony, felony of the first or second degree, felony of the third degree, misdemeanor of the first degree, misdemeanor of the second degree) yet all five read 'no degree assigned', while the two rows whose text assigns nothing are the only ones populated. Whichever convention is intended, the table cannot be using both.

cite field contains six fabricated subdivision identifiers that do not exist in the statute and are not citable: '775.083(1) (introductory text preceding paragraph (a))', '775.083(1) (introductory text, first clause -- capital felony exclusion)', '775.083(1) (introductory text, second clause -- fine in lieu of punishment)', '775.083(1) (introductory text, second sentence -- noncriminal violation fine authority)', '775.083(1) (introductory text, third sentence -- shall not exceed connector)', '775.083(2) (final sentences -- disposition and use restriction)'. Florida's subsection (1) has no clause-level or sentence-level subdivisions. Any consumer doing exact-match or dedupe on cite gets unaddressable rows.

Overlapping quotes inflate the row count and double-count text. The single first sentence of subsection (1) is quoted in three separate rows (the lead-in row quotes it whole; the capital-felony row quotes its first clause; the in-lieu-of row quotes its second clause). Independently, the last three sentences of subsection (2) are quoted twice, once inside the full '775.083(2)' row whose trigger asserts 'The quote below is now the COMPLETE subsection', and again in full in the '775.083(2) (final sentences)' row. Seventeen rows describe fourteen provisions.

scope = 'applies on top of the (a)-(e) ladder; no upper bound' on 775.083(1)(f) misstates the provision. (f) is 'double the pecuniary gain derived from the offense by the offender or double the pecuniary loss suffered by the victim' -- a bound that is computable and finite in every case, not absent. Only (g), 'Any higher amount specifically authorized by statute', is genuinely open-ended within this section. Both rows carry the identical scope string, erasing the difference between a multiplier cap and no cap.

Capital-felony consequence gap. The table asserts across two rows that a capital felony is 'outside s. 775.083(1) fine authorization entirely' and 'EXCLUDED from this section's fine authorization', but never records that subsection (2) court costs still attach to a capital felony conviction. Subsection (2) assesses costs on 'a felony' with no capital carve-out and is not governed by the subsection (1) lead-in, so the $50 felony cost applies. A reader of the capital-felony row concludes 775.083 does nothing to a capital felony; it does.

Quote truncated without ellipsis on the capital-felony row: 'A person who has been convicted of an offense other than a capital felony may be sentenced to pay a fine in addition to any punishment described in s. 775.082' stops mid-sentence at a semicolon, dropping the in-lieu-of clause. Verbatim as far as it goes, but this is the exact defect the table's own subsection (2) trigger faults the prior table for -- 'cut it mid-sentence at $20 for any other offense with no ellipsis'.

775.083.notes:
Coverage verdict is independent of the correctness verdict and I set it myself. I walked the statute from my own fetch before opening the table, and every operative unit has a row: the three lead-in sentences, (a) through (g), the closing flush text of subsection (1), subsection (2) including all four sentences, subsection (3), and subsection (4). Nothing is missing, so missing[] is empty. The only unrowed text is the History note, which assigns no degree, minimum, or enhancement and needs no row. Completeness is whole-section and that is not a courtesy -- I confirmed it against two independent sources.

The builder's structural claim also holds up under check. I verified from the raw HTML that s. 775.083 has no numbered subparagraph tier and no sub-subparagraph tier; (a) through (g) is the deepest level. The 812.014(2)(b)2 / 775.082(9)(a)1.o / 817.568(2)(b) failure mode -- a later subparagraph with no lower bound hiding under a paragraph opened for something else -- is structurally impossible in this section. Both no-lower-bound provisions, (1)(f) and (1)(g), are rowed and flagged as overrides on the (a)-(e) ladder, and the builder's self-correction identifying the unenumerated lead-in text as this section's real trap is sound. That trap is genuinely cleared.

Quote spot-check: I checked six, not three, against the leg.state.fl.us raw text. (1)(f), the full lead-in, the closing flush text of (1), the complete subsection (2), the (2) tail fragment, and (3) are all verbatim, including the curly quotation marks around "convicted" and "conviction". No paraphrase is presented as quotation anywhere in the table. The only quote defect is the unmarked truncation noted above.

The unread field is substantially honest -- every external citation it disclaims is genuinely external, the claim that no subparagraph tier exists is true, and the refusal to guess levels because 921.0022 was not consulted is exactly right and is why no level field can be faulted. Its defect is purpose drift rather than dishonesty: the first entry is a 200-word coverage argument litigating the prior table's failures, not a disclosure of what went unread, and it makes a verification claim ('independently re-fetched a second time from the raw HTML') that no consumer can check. I did that re-fetch myself and it confirms the text, so the claim is true, but the field should not be carrying advocacy.

Why FAIL despite whole-section coverage. No dollar cap is mis-mapped to a degree, no no-lower-bound provision is hidden, no level is guessed, and no quote is fabricated. The failures are field integrity and two substantive imprecisions: the degree field is populated in exactly the two places the table's own rule forbids and left empty in the five places that actually name degrees; the cite field carries six invented subdivisions that are not citable and break exact-match consumers; (f) and (g) are given identical 'no upper bound' scope when only (g) is unbounded; and the capital-felony rows leave a reader believing the section is inert as to capital felonies when subsection (2) costs still attach. Fixing these is field-level editing, not re-reading -- the reading underneath is sound.

2. NO-LOWER-BOUND: the classic trap pattern does not exist in this section -- there is no dollar tier, no drug-weight threshold, and no value element anywhere, so there is no 'first subparagraph is a tier, later subparagraphs are something else' structure to miss. I checked every analog and the table caught all of them: (1)(a) has THREE independent routes to capital felony sharing one flush clause and all three have rows (this is precisely the 812.014(2)(b)2 failure mode and it was avoided); subsection (4) is an EXCLUSION list where any unlisted felony qualifies with no floor of any kind, and the row states this explicitly; (6)(b)1. has an a./b. disjunct joined by 'and' to subparagraph 2., and the row flags that neither alone suffices. REVERSE-BOUND FINDING (the one thing worth escalating): (2) and (3) both carry 'imprisonment for a term of years not exceeding life,' an enhancement above the ordinary first-degree-felony ceiling. It appears ONLY in free-text trigger prose. The typed degree field reads 'first degree felony' and min/max are null, so a downstream consumer reading typed fields alone would infer a 30-year cap. There is no field in this schema for it and the degree recorded is what the statute says, so this is a schema limitation the builder disclosed rather than a wrong value -- but it is the same class of hazard this audit exists to surface, inverted.

3. DEGREES: all seven verified against operative words. (1)(a)1./2./3. capital felony via the flush clause closing (1)(a) -- correct, and correctly attributed to the flush language rather than to any single subparagraph. (2) first degree felony. (3) first degree felony. (4) second degree felony. (5)(b) second degree felony. No errors.

The left offense column contains EXACTLY four 782.04 entries: '782.04(4) | 2nd' under LEVEL 8; '782.04(1) | 1st | Attempt, conspire, or solicit to commit premeditated murder' and '782.04(3) | 1st,PBL | Accomplice to murder...' under LEVEL 9; '782.04(2) | 1st,PBL | Unlawful killing of human; act is homicide, unpremeditated' under LEVEL 10. '782.04' also appears in the right-hand DESCRIPTION column of the 782.051(1) and 782.051(2) entries, which are attempted-felony-murder rankings, not 782.04 rankings -- the builder identified this correctly and did not mine it for a level. The level assignment is still correct because the chart keys on the statutory cite, not the description, but the row presents the line as clean confirmation without noting the mismatch.

The age elements (18-or-older in (1)(a)3., under-18 in (5)(b)) are offense elements, not scope qualifiers, and were correctly left out of scope.

6. QUOTES: I spot-checked FOURTEEN fragments, not three, by normalizing whitespace and citation spacing and testing each as a substring of my own extraction. All fourteen matched verbatim: (2), (1)(b), (5)(a)1., (5)(b), (6)(a), (6)(b) in full, the (4) head, (4)(l), the (3) tail, the (1)(a)3. head, and the complete enumerated lists for (1)(a)2., (1)(a)3.a.-j., (3)(a)-(r), and (4)(a)-(s). The two ellipses (in the (1)(a)1. and (1)(a)2. quotes, both eliding intervening subparagraphs to reach the flush clause) are marked with '. . .' and disclosed in the trigger. 775.084.notes:
Verification performed: fetched https://www.flsenate.gov/Laws/Statutes/2025/775.084 by curl, stripped tags locally, read all 587 text lines start to finish, and enumerated every provision that assigns a term, a mandatory minimum, or an enhancement before opening the table. My independent penalty list is (4)(a)1.-3., (4)(b)1.-3., (4)(c)1.a.-d., (4)(d)1.-3. = thirteen rows, plus the modifiers (4)(c)2., (4)(e)-(4)(k)3., and the cross-cutting predicate rules (1)(e), (2), (5). Quote spot-check, three as instructed, all verbatim against source lines: (4)(d)2. matches line 483 exactly; (4)(c)1.c. matches line 473 exactly including the trailing '; or'; (1)(e) matches line 395 exactly. I extended the check to (2), (5), (6), (4)(e), (4)(i), (4)(k)1., (3)(d)1. -- all verbatim. No paraphrase-as-quotation found anywhere. The only quote defect is the unmarked truncation at (3)(a)6. and (3)(c)5.

Degrees checked against operative words: 'no degree assigned' is correct on every row. s. 775.084 grades no offense; it prescribes terms for felonies already graded elsewhere, and (4)(a)/(b)/(d) reference degree only as the input variable selecting which term applies. No wrong degrees.

Ceiling-vs-floor structure verified row by row and is correct throughout: (4)(a) ceilings only; (4)(b) ceilings plus release-ineligibility periods; (4)(c)1. floors; (4)(d)2. and (4)(d)3. genuinely dual-bound. The 'felony punishable by life' vs 'life felony' asymmetry at (4)(c)1.a. is real and correctly preserved rather than resolved.

One contested reading I am flagging but not scoring as an error: the (4)(c)2. row asserts that 'Nothing in this subsection' reaches all of subsection (4), so a court may exceed the (4)(a) 30/10 and (4)(b) 30/10 ceilings. The literal hierarchy reading is defensible and the table shows its work, but it is presented with more confidence than a disputed placement-vs-text question warrants, and it materially expands stated exposure on six rows. A downstream consumer should treat it as an open question, not a settled one.

Verdict is FAIL on correctness, not coverage. The table is unusually thorough -- it caught the (4)(k)1. drop-the-first-subparagraph trap that the prompt describes, and it caught it in the right place. It then reproduced the same failure at (1)(d)1.a., where the first item in the list is an incorporated any-degree catch-all and the later items are bounded named statutes. It read the subparagraphs that answered its question and let the one that did not answer it pass through as an unopened cross-reference.

missing: (1)(b) firearm paragraph, SECOND tier (25 points for a semiautomatic firearm as defined in s. 775.087(3) or a machine gun as defined in s. 790.001, for any felony other than those enumerated in s. 775.087(3)): no dedicated row. Substance IS present and quoted inside the shared 18-point row, so this is a granularity defect, not an omission. Flagged because it is exactly the shape of the failure this audit exists to catch: one paragraph, first tier is one item, later tier is a different item with a different carve-out cross-reference, and a consumer keying on a row cannot retrieve 25 without re-parsing prose.

(1)(b) justice-system-personnel multiplier, SECOND tier (2.0x for s. 775.0823(5),(6),(7),(8),(9)) and THIRD tier (1.5x for s. 784.07(3), s. 775.0875(1), s. 775.0823(10) or (11)): no dedicated rows. (1)(b)2. paragraph intro (the 'violent felony offender of special concern as defined in s. 948.06' gateway) has no row of its own; it is folded into the 2.a. row's quote. Content present, contiguous, and verbatim, so this one is defensible.

NO PROVISION OF THE SECTION IS ABSENT. I walked (1)(a) worksheet line by line against the flsenate.gov HTML grid, (1)(b) paragraph by paragraph, every sentence of (2), and (3) through (7) plus History. Every operative rule has coverage.
wrong: SCOPE MISUSE, (1)(b)1. row (12 points, community sanction violation including a new felony conviction): scope is 'prior'. This provision has ZERO criminal-history element. Its operative words are 'a new felony conviction BEFORE THE SENTENCING COURT' -- that is the present case, not prior record. 'prior' is a wrong value in a typed field.

SCOPE MISUSE, (1)(b) community sanction violation default row (6 points): scope is 'prior'. The trigger is 'when a community sanction violation is before the court for sentencing.' Again the matter before the court, not criminal history. Wrong value.

SCOPE MISUSE, (1)(b) legal status row (4 points): scope is 'prior'. Legal status is the offender's supervision/escape status EXISTING AT THE TIME the offense was committed, not prior record. The statute itself refutes the label: the (1)(a) worksheet places LEGAL STATUS in the subtotal block as a line item DISTINCT from TOTAL PRIOR RECORD SCORE. If the drafters had meant prior record they would have scored it in the Prior Record table.

SCOPE MISUSE (weaker but same family), (1)(b)2.a. and 2.b. rows: scope 'prior'. The s. 948.06 violent-felony-offender-of-special-concern status has a criminal-history component, but the assessed event in both is the CURRENT violation of felony probation or community control before the court. 'prior' at best half-describes these.

FALSE FACTUAL ASSERTION, Prior Record table row: 'Values are lower across the board than the Additional Offenses table at the same level.' Not true across the board. The M (misdemeanor) row is 0.2 in BOTH tables -- equal, not lower. Levels 10 through 1 are lower; M is not. The row states a rule that its own quoted data contradicts.

PARAPHRASE PRESENTED AS QUOTATION, all four worksheet point-table rows (Primary Offense, Additional Offenses, Victim Injury, Prior Record). The source HTML cells read '10 | 116 | =' -- the '=' is the operator introducing the empty Total cell. The quote field renders this as '10 = 116', which asserts an equality relation that does not exist in the statute and inverts what the '=' character is doing. The trailing 'Total ____' and 'x ___' fill markers are also invented characters. The unread field discloses this as a 'LAYOUT CAVEAT,' but a disclosed fabrication in a quote field is still a fabrication -- quote fields must be verbatim or the row must carry no quote.

INTERNAL CONTRADICTION, subtotal block row: 'Eight named line items feeding the SUBTOTAL line' and then lists SUBTOTAL itself as the eighth. Only SEVEN items feed the subtotal (TOTAL OFFENSE SCORE, TOTAL PRIOR RECORD SCORE, LEGAL STATUS, COMMUNITY SANCTION VIOLATION, PRIOR SERIOUS FELONY, PRIOR CAPITAL FELONY, FIREARM OR SEMIAUTOMATIC WEAPON). SUBTOTAL is the sum, not an addend.

NULLED FLOOR, (2) row 'any sentence to state prison must exceed 1 year': min is null. This is an unconditional statutory floor on every state prison sentence under the code, independent of point score and independent of degree. If the min field is meant to carry a mandatory floor, null understates a hard rule the row's own trigger correctly describes as a floor.
unread: The claim 'Every level field in this table is therefore null rather than guessed' is verified true. No row guesses a s. 921.0022 level. The level 8/9/10 and level 7/8 figures that appear in trigger text are quoted from 921.0024 itself, not imported from the ranking chart.

ONE OBJECTION to the unread field's use: the LAYOUT CAVEAT entry is doing double duty as a disclosure AND as an excuse for non-verbatim quote fields. Disclosure in unread does not convert a reconstruction into a quotation. The caveat belongs there; the reconstructions do not belong in quote fields.

WHAT THE TABLE GOT RIGHT, stated so the FAIL is not misread as a broken table. Coverage is genuinely whole-section; I could not find a single provision with no row. The table's two self-declared "INDEPENDENT FINDINGS" both hold up under my own count: (1)(b) does contain eight multiplier paragraphs while the (1)(a) face carries only seven checkboxes, and fleeing/eluding under s. 316.1935 is indeed the one with no box.

VERDICT REASONING. Completeness is whole-section on substance. Verdict is FAIL on correctness: five rows carry a wrong scope value (three of them clearly wrong, two half-wrong), one row asserts a comparative rule its own data contradicts, four rows put reconstructions in quote fields, and one row miscounts its own list. None of these misstate a degree or a point value, so the damage is to typed-field reliability rather than to the legal substance -- but per the rubric a table that covers everything and still misstates typed fields is whole-section and FAIL.

wrong: 316.193(6)(c) -- OVERSTATED MANDATORY-MINIMUM REACH. The trigger asserts the 30-day mandatory minimum 'reaches the (2)(b)2. non-felony third conviction as well as the (2)(b)1. and (2)(b)3. felonies.' The first half is wrong on the face of the text. (6)(c) applies to a third-or-subsequent conviction 'for an offense that occurs within a period of 10 years after the date of a prior conviction.' (2)(b)2 applies to a third violation 'for an offense that occurs more than 10 years after the date of a prior conviction.' These are complementary conditions on the identical fact, keyed to the identical 10-year window, pointing in opposite directions. A defendant in the (2)(b)2 class is by definition outside (6)(c)'s window. The only way to force an overlap is to read 'a prior conviction' as a different prior in each provision, which requires two priors of different vintages -- but on that reading the third offense is within 10 years of the recent prior, which puts the defendant in (2)(b)1 (felony) rather than (2)(b)2. Under either reading the claimed overlap is empty. The row tells a reader that a 30-day mandatory jail floor attaches to a class of defendants it does not reach.

SCOPE FIELD -- 'prior' applied inconsistently to structurally identical rows. 'First conviction' tiers carry scope 'prior' at (2)(a)1.a., (2)(a)2.a., and (6)(a), but scope null at (4)(a)1. and (4)(b)1. Worse, the inconsistency runs INSIDE a single paragraph: (4)(a)1. is null while (4)(a)2. and (4)(a)3. are 'prior', and (4)(b)1. is null while (4)(b)2. is 'prior' -- same conviction-count axis, opposite typing, adjacent subparagraphs. A consumer filtering scope=='prior' to collect the criminal-history-keyed tiers silently drops the first-conviction tiers of the entire 0.15-or-higher / minor-passenger enhancement.

SCOPE FIELD -- off-vocabulary values. The typed vocabulary reserves 'prior' for criminal history and 'item' for the thing taken or involved. Six rows instead load party identity into the field: (6)(e) and (6)(f) 'non-defendant vehicle owner', (6)(g) "vehicle owner's family", (6)(l) 'vehicle owner or lienholder of record', (9) 'arrestee (pre-conviction)', (13) and (13)(a) and (13)(b) 'immobilization agencies...', (13)(c) 'immobilization agencies and the persons they assign to immobilize vehicles; NOT the DUI defendant'. Three incompatible semantics now share one field. The (13)(c) row's own trigger advertises this as a repair ('SCOPE FIELD CORRECTED ON REPAIR') -- but disclosure does not make an off-vocabulary value a typed one, and it defeats the sole mechanical use of the field.

316.193(2)(a)2.a. and (2)(a)2.b. -- assert the contents of a statute the table states it did not read. The triggers claim 'A 6-month maximum corresponds to a second degree misdemeanor under s. 775.082' and 'A 9-month maximum matches no standard misdemeanor term in s. 775.082.' The unread field says 'F.S. 775.082, 775.083, 775.084 -- not read.' The second claim is the load-bearing one (it is an assertion about the ABSENCE of a term in an unread source, which cannot be made without reading it) and it is what licenses leaving the 9-month tier ungraded. Both rows hedge that they do not infer a degree, but both state 775.082's contents as fact.

316.193(6)(m) -- enumeration silently excludes every felony term. The statute lets a defendant serve 'all or any portion of a term of imprisonment to which the defendant has been sentenced pursuant to this section' in residential treatment, with no carve-out. The trigger enumerates '(2)(a)2., (2)(b)2., (4)(b), and the mandatory minimums in (6)(b) and (6)(c)' -- omitting the imprisonment imposed under (2)(b)1., (2)(b)3., (3)(c)2., and all three DUI manslaughter grades, including the 4-year mandatory minimum in the subsection (3) flush language. Whether a DUI manslaughter minimum can be served in residential treatment is the highest-stakes question this paragraph raises, and the row's list reads as excluding it.
unread: F.S. 921.0024 -- not read by me either. Level-to-points conversion unverified; I verified only ordinal chart placement.

F.S. 775.082, 775.083, 775.084 -- not read by me. Every degree in the table resolves through these; the actual years and fines behind each degree remain unverified, which is exactly why the (2)(a)2. rows' assertions about 775.082 are unsupported.
F.S. 316.1933 ('serious bodily injury'), 775.021(5) ('unborn child'), 316.062 (render-aid duty) -- not read. These supply elements, not grades, so they do not affect any degree in the table.

F.S. 327.35(3)(a)3.c., 782.071, 782.072 -- not read. These are the qualifying priors that elevate DUI manslaughter under (3)(c)3.c. I did incidentally confirm from the 921.0022 LEVEL 8/9 blocks that 327.35(3)(a)3.c.(I) and (II) exist as vessel-BUI analogues, which is consistent with the editor's renumbering note.

Case law -- not consulted. fs-316-193-2025.notes:
METHOD. I could not use the URL supplied in the task: https://uscode.house.gov/... is the federal US Code repository and cannot host a Florida statute. I fetched it anyway and it returned 'Document not Found'. I sourced the text from flsenate.gov/Laws/Statutes/2025/316.193, stripped the markup, and worked from the resulting 88-line body, then fetched 921.0022 separately for the levels.

COMPLETENESS IS GENUINE. I walked (1) through (14) in order against my own extraction. Every subsection, paragraph, subparagraph, sub-subparagraph, and all four unnumbered flush paragraphs (closing (2)(a), closing (3), sitting between (4)(b)2. and (4)(c), and closing (6)) have a row. A regex sweep for degree-assigning language returns exactly 9 hits -- 8 degree assignments plus the 'commits DUI manslaughter' lead-in -- and all 8 have rows with degrees matching the operative words. A sweep for time floors returns 11, all accounted for. I found no orphan provision, so 'whole-section' stands. The builder also caught the trap this audit exists to find: (2)(b)3.'s 'regardless of when any prior conviction occurred' is flagged as having no lower bound, the (2)(a) numbering trap (1=fines, 2=jail, 3=interlock) is flagged, (4)(a)3.'s floor-with-no-ceiling is flagged, (6)(i) is correctly identified as a fifth dismissal ground that the (6)(a)-(c) cross-references omit, and (13)(c) is correctly surfaced as a separate offense buried in a procedural subsection.

LEVELS INDEPENDENTLY RE-DERIVED, ALL SIX CORRECT. From my own extraction of the 921.0022 chart, the LEVEL block boundaries sit at lines 210/253/297/377/449/516/586/748/843/925. The 316.193 entries fall at 303 (LEVEL 3 block, '(2)(b) | 3rd | Felony DUI, 3rd conviction'), 520 (LEVEL 6, '(2)(b) | 3rd | Felony DUI, 4th or subsequent conviction'), 590 (LEVEL 7, '(3)(c)2. | 3rd | DUI resulting in serious bodily injury'), 751 (LEVEL 8, '(3)(c)3.a. | 2nd | DUI manslaughter'), 846 and 848 (LEVEL 9, '(3)(c)3.b.' and '(3)(c)3.c.'). Every level in the table is verifiable and correct. The unread field's '12 hits' claim is exactly reproducible -- and worth crediting, because 6 of those 12 are s. 316.1935 (fleeing or eluding), a different offense that shares the '316.193' substring. The builder read past the near-miss rather than importing it.

QUOTES. Spot-checked six, not three: (2)(b)3., the subsection (3) flush language, (6)(a), (3)(c)1., (13)(a), and (5). All verbatim against source, including the full (6)(a) paragraph the trigger says was restored. No paraphrase presented as quotation. One cosmetic artifact: the (3)(c)3.c. quote carries the stray footnote marker from the source HTML ('under this subparagraph, 1s. 327.35(3)(a)3.c.'), unbracketed inside quotation marks -- the trigger discloses the underlying editor's note, so this is a transcription nit, not a fidelity failure.

MIN/MAX CONVENTION IS SOUND. The table nulls min/max on every row and justifies it in the (1) row: nothing in 316.193 is graded by a dollar amount. I confirmed this -- every dollar figure in the section is a fine or a remittance threshold, never a grading trigger. The convention is correct and disclosed. One consequence to flag for downstream consumers rather than as an error: the section's only genuinely uncapped numeric provision, (4)(a)3.'s '$4,000 with no stated ceiling', therefore survives in prose only.

WHY FAIL DESPITE FULL COVERAGE. Coverage and correctness are separate axes and this table splits them. The (6)(c) row misstates the reach of a 30-day mandatory jail minimum, extending it to a class of defendants the statute's own 10-year window excludes -- an error that no degree check, level check, or quote check would surface, because the degree, level, and quote on that row are all fine. Combined with the scope-field typing defects, verdict is FAIL on correctness while completeness stands at whole-section.

missing: 817.568(1) -- the entire definitions subsection has NO row anywhere in the table, while purely procedural subsections (16), (17), and (18) each got one. Its paragraphs are load-bearing on the reach of the offense rows and several are cited inside triggers without ever being recorded: (1)(a) 'Access device'; (1)(b) 'Authorization'; (1)(c) 'Harass' (narrows subsection (4) and is the only thing that keeps (4) off protected speech); (1)(d) 'Individual' (excludes firms, corporations, partnerships -- controls the reach of (6), (7), (8), and (11)); (1)(e) 'Person' = s. 1.01(3) (INCLUDES corporations -- controls the reach of (2)(a), (2)(b), (2)(c), and (9)); (1)(f) 'Personal identification information' with subparagraphs 1. through 6., the object element of every single offense in the section; (1)(g) 'Counterfeit or fictitious personal identification information' (the reasonably-prudent-person standard that makes (9) chargeable).

817.568(12)(a), (12)(b), and (12)(c) -- the three surcharge-distribution paragraphs. The (12) row jumps from the first sentence straight to (d) with an ellipsis and never records that the $1,001 breaks into $500 / $250 / $250 / $1, and never records (c), the clerk's service charge. Minor for exposure, but the table elsewhere claims to record every paragraph.

No row and no note anywhere on whether subsection (5) and subsection (10) STACK. Both are reclassification subsections keyed to different facts (public record vs. impersonation), and neither says it is exclusive of the other. A (2)(a) third degree felony furthered by a public record AND committed while posing as a bank representative is reachable as a FIRST degree felony on a stacking reading -- a degree no row in this table reaches for a (2)(a) case. The table's (10)(d) row affirmatively asserts 'THE SINGLE HIGHEST EXPOSURE IN THIS SECTION' without ever confronting the stacking question. Unresolved ambiguity should have been recorded as ambiguity, not papered over.
wrong: 817.568(6), level 8 -- LEVEL IS OVERBROAD AND NOT VERIFIABLE FOR HALF THE PROVISION. I opened s. 921.0022. The only entry is Level 8, 817.568(6), 2nd degree, described as 'Fraudulent use of personal identification information of an individual under the age of 18.' The chart description stops at the under-18 branch. Subsection (6) also reaches an individual '60 years of age or older,' a branch added by later amendment that the ranking chart was never updated to cover. The table assigns level 8 to the WHOLE of (6), including the 60-or-older branch, which is not in the chart and would instead fall to the s. 921.0023 default for an unranked second degree felony. A 60-or-older (6) case scored at level 8 off this table is scored at a rank the chart does not support.

817.568(7), level 9 -- SAME DEFECT, SAME CAUSE. The s. 921.0022 Level 9 entry for 817.568(7) reads 'Fraudulent use of personal identification information of an individual under the age of 18 by his or her parent, legal guardian, or person exercising custodial authority.' Under 18 only. Subsection (7) equally reaches custodial use against an individual 60 years of age or older, and that branch has no chart entry. Level 9 is correct for the minor-victim branch and unsupported for the elder-victim branch. The row states level 9 flat, with no branch split and no caveat.

817.568(8)(a) trigger -- AFFIRMATIVELY FALSE STATEMENT ABOUT THE SCOPE OF THE SECTION. The trigger says: 'note that (1)(d) defines individual to exclude corporations and partnerships, so this subsection is the only route to entity victims.' That is wrong. (2)(a), (2)(b), (2)(c), and (9) are all written in terms of 'person,' and (1)(e) defines 'person' by reference to s. 1.01(3), which I fetched: 'The word person includes individuals, children, firms, associations, joint adventures, partnerships, estates, trusts, business trusts, syndicates, fiduciaries, corporations, and all other groups or combinations.' Subsection (2) therefore already reaches corporate and partnership victims. (8) is the only route to DISSOLVED entities and to deceased individuals -- not to entity victims generally. The error understates (2) and it is a direct consequence of subsection (1) having no row: the table cited (1)(d) and never opened (1)(e).

817.568(2)(b) and (2)(c) count-prong rows, scope 'victim count' -- THE COUNT PRONGS ARE UNDERSTATED FOR THE SAME REASON. Both prongs count 'persons,' not 'individuals.' Because (1)(e) pulls in s. 1.01(3), corporations, partnerships, trusts, and estates each count toward the 10 / 20 / 30 thresholds. The rows describe these throughout as 'victims' and 'persons' in the human sense ('12 victims,' 'a 25-victim, $0 case,' 'thirty victims'), which invites a reader to stop counting at natural persons and fall short of a threshold that is in fact satisfied. Compare the table's own (6), (7), and (11) rows, which correctly turn on 'individual' and do exclude entities -- the distinction is real and the table inverted it.

817.568(5)(b) quote -- STITCHED QUOTATION THAT MISATTRIBUTES A FLUSH-LEFT SENTENCE TO ONE PARAGRAPH. The quote string is '(b) A felony of the third degree is reclassified as a felony of the second degree. ... For purposes of sentencing under chapter 921 and incentive gain-time eligibility under chapter 944, ...'. The ellipsis silently swallows paragraph (c) in its entirety, and presents the flush-left ranking sentence -- which governs ALL of subsection (5), (a) through (c) alike -- as though it trailed paragraph (b). Same defect in the (5)(a), (10)(a), (10)(b), (12), and (15) quotes, all of which splice non-adjacent passages into a single quotation string. The elisions are marked, so this is disclosed rather than concealed, but a spliced quote is not the verbatim single passage the field implies, and here it moves a subsection-wide sentence under one paragraph.

scope field is free-text prose, not a typed classification. Values used include 'purpose', 'public record', 'impersonation by defendant', 'law enforcement activity', 'counterfeit or fictitious information', and 'relationship to victim'. Several of these describe the TRIGGER, not the dimension being measured, and duplicate what the trigger field already says; 'law enforcement activity' on the (14) exemption row is not a scope of anything. Checked specifically per the rubric: the dangerous misuses are NOT present -- 'prior' appears nowhere, and 'item' appears nowhere, so no criminal-history or thing-taken value has been repurposed.
