817.568.notes:
COVERAGE IS GENUINELY STRONG; CORRECTNESS IS NOT. Every provision in 817.568 that assigns a degree, a mandatory minimum, or a reclassification has a row, and the no-lower-bound traps this audit exists to catch were all caught. I walked (1) through (19) independently before opening the table and confirm: (2)(a); both prongs of (2)(b) plus its 3-year minimum; both prongs of (2)(c) plus its 5-year minimum plus BOTH prongs of the buried third-sentence 10-year minimum; (3); (4); (5)(a)-(c); (6); (7); (8)(a); both prongs of (8)(b) plus its 3-year minimum; both prongs of (8)(c) plus its 5-year minimum plus both prongs of its 10-year minimum; (9); (10)(a)-(d) including the life-felony top rung; (11); (12)-(19). Nothing operative is absent. Completeness is therefore whole-section, and the guard should not be disabled on coverage grounds.

VERDICT IS FAIL ON CORRECTNESS. Three defects carry real weight.

(1) The level-8 and level-9 assignments on (6) and (7) are half-verified. I opened the chart the builder said it did not open. The chart entries exist and the NUMBERS are right, but both descriptions are confined to victims 'under the age of 18.' The '60 years of age or older' branch of each subsection -- added by amendment, never reflected in the chart -- has no entry. Assigning a flat level to a provision the chart only half-covers is exactly the guessed-level failure mode, arrived at by a different road: the builder guessed right for the minor-victim branch and inherited a wrong answer for the elder-victim branch.

(2) The (8)(a) trigger states as fact that (8) is 'the only route to entity victims.' It is not. (1)(e) defines 'person' by s. 1.01(3), which I fetched and which expressly includes corporations, partnerships, trusts, and estates. Subsection (2) reaches existing entities on its face. The same error propagates into the (2)(b) and (2)(c) count-prong rows, which count 'persons' -- entities included -- but are written throughout in the language of human victims, so a reader counting only natural persons will undercount toward a 10, 20, or 30 threshold and land a degree too low.

(3) That error has a single structural cause worth naming, because it is the failure pattern this audit was built around wearing new clothes. Subsection (1) is the one subsection in the section with no row. The builder went into (1), pulled out (1)(c), (1)(d), and (1)(g) because three offense rows needed them, and stopped -- never reaching (1)(e), which sat one paragraph later and controlled the reach of four offense rows. Opened the paragraph, found what was being looked for, stopped. The table recorded venue, the statewide-prosecutor clause, and a legislative finding about county of residence, and left the definitions subsection unrecorded.

ON THE unread FIELD: honest, and unusually so -- it over-discloses. It flatly states the ranking chart was 'NOT OPENED AT ALL in this repair pass' and instructs that levels 4, 5, 8, and 9 be treated as unconfirmed. That is a true statement about process and it is the reason this audit could go straight to the levels. Two things temper the credit. First, shipping four numbers into a typed level field while telling the reader not to trust them is still shipping unverified data; a disclosed guess in a typed field is a guess. Second, the final 'scope note' bullet claims 'every quote in this table was string-verified against that fetch.' I spot-checked well beyond three -- (2)(a), (2)(b), (2)(c), (11), (14), (8)(b), (8)(c) third sentence, (12)(d) -- and every contiguous quote is verbatim, including the fine detail that (8)(c) says 'minimum mandatory' where (2)(c) says 'mandatory minimum,' which the table flags. But six quotes are ellipsis-splices of non-adjacent passages, and the (5)(b) splice moves a sentence governing all of subsection (5) under a single paragraph. 'String-verified' overstates what those six are.

WHAT THE TABLE GOT RIGHT AND SHOULD BE KEPT: the (2)(b) count prong at any dollar value is present and correctly flagged as the trap -- the specific error this audit was chartered to find is not here. So is its twin at (8)(b), and the far easier-to-miss third-sentence 10-year minimum at 30-or-more persons in both (2)(c) and (8)(c), at $0. The (10)(d) life-felony rung, sitting in the last subparagraph of the subsection, is present. The observation that subsection (3) forces the (2)(b)/(2)(c) minimums past the Criminal Punishment Code maximum but says nothing about the parallel (8)(b)/(8)(c) minimums is correct and is not obvious from the text. The observation that subsection (19)'s limitations period names only (2), (6), and (7), leaving (8) through (11) to the general law, is correct. The refusal to fabricate a max on any of the value prongs is correct: no upper bound appears in the text of (2)(b), (2)(c), (8)(b), or (8)(c), and treating the next tier's floor as this tier's ceiling would have been an invention.

missing: 775.082(3)(a)4.a.(I) and (II) have no rows of their own -- they are folded into the 4.a. row. This is the exact structural shape this audit exists to catch: (I) is mandatory life, (II) is a materially different sentence (a 25-year prison floor, not exceeding life, followed by probation or community control for the person's NATURAL LIFE under s. 948.012(4)). A consumer reading (I) and stopping never sees the lifetime supervision tail. Both are quoted, so coverage survives, but they warrant separate rows.

SUBSTANTIVE OMISSION in the (9)(a)3. lead-in row and the (9)(a)2. row: the first sentence of (9)(a)3. authorizes the state attorney to seek PRR sentencing only for a defendant who is a prison releasee reoffender 'as defined in subparagraph 1.' -- it does NOT cite subparagraph 2. The second sentence then broadens to 'as defined in this section.' The (9)(a)2. row asserts a 'FULLY INDEPENDENT PRISON RELEASEE REOFFENDER PATHWAY' without ever confronting whether (9)(a)3.'s election clause reaches it. That asymmetry is on the face of the text the row quotes verbatim, and neither the row nor the unread field flags it.

The unread field does not disclose that the `scope` field was populated with 14 free-text prose strings outside the enum (see `wrong`). A coverage disclosure that omits a systematic typed-field violation is incomplete as a disclosure, even though the provision-level coverage claim it makes is accurate.
wrong: SYSTEMATIC MISUSE OF THE TYPED `scope` FIELD -- 14 rows. The table itself states the enum in the (1)(b)3. row ('not a value, item, place, or prior-record narrowing'), then writes free-text prose into `scope` on: (3)(a)5.a., 5.b., 5.c. ('juvenile life-felony track under (3)(a)5.'); (3)(b)2.a., 2.b., 2.c. ('juvenile first-degree-punishable-by-life track under (3)(b)2.'); (8)(a) ('all felonies except capital felonies (pre-10/1/1983 branch also excepts life felonies)'); (8)(b), (8)(c), (8)(d) ('all felonies except capital felonies'); (8)(e) ('all felonies except capital felonies, continuing dates of enterprise'); (9)(a)1. named row ('prison releasee reoffender predicate offenses (named)'); (9)(a)1.o. ('any felony of any degree involving use or threat of physical force or violence'); (9)(a)1.r. ('any felony violation of ss. 790.07, 800.04, 827.03, 827.071, 847.0135(5)'). None of these is 'value', 'item', 'place', 'prior', or null. The table spent four rows loudly correcting five wrong 'prior' tags and one wrong 'item' tag inherited from a prior version, and in the same pass introduced a larger and more basic violation of the same field. Any consumer filtering on scope gets 14 unmatched strings.

SCOPE 'prior' MISAPPLIED to non-criminal-history provisions -- 775.082(9)(c) and 775.082(9)(d)2. (9)(c) is a savings clause ('Nothing in this subsection shall prevent a court from imposing a greater sentence...'); (9)(d)2. is a recordkeeping mandate on the state attorney. Neither is narrowed by criminal history. This is the identical category error the table condemns in its (1)(b)1. and (3)(a)4.b. rows ('there is NO prior-record, recidivist, or criminal-history element here'). (9)(b) is borderline for the same reason -- it is a service-of-sentence rule, not a history narrowing.

SCOPE TYPING IS INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT INSIDE ONE PARAGRAPH. (9)(a)2. is tagged scope='prior'. (9)(a)1.o. and (9)(a)1.r. -- which (9)(a)2. incorporates wholesale by reference to 'sub-subparagraphs (a)1.a.-r.' -- are tagged with prose. The same predicate list carries two different field types depending on which row you read.

FACTUAL CONTRADICTION between two rows. The (3)(a)1. trigger asserts it is 'The only life-felony tier with an express minimum term (30 years).' That is false. 775.082(3)(a)4.a.(II) expressly requires 'a term of at least 25 years' imprisonment' -- and the table's own (3)(a)4.a. row says so ('a split sentence with a 25-year prison floor'). One of the two statements has to be wrong, and it is the (3)(a)1. one.

OVERBROAD BLANKET ASSERTION repeated in all 52 trigger fields: 'no dollar, quantity, or weight element anywhere in s. 775.082.' Subsection (10) is gated on a QUANTITY -- 'total sentence points pursuant to s. 921.0024 are 22 points or fewer' -- and (9)(a)1. is gated on a 3-year quantity. Neither is a value element in the 812.014 sense, so min/max null is defensible, but the absolute phrasing 'anywhere in s. 775.082' is stated as fact and is not true.

DEGREE INCONSISTENCY across the two halves of subsection (2). Sentence 1 is tagged degree='capital felony'; sentence 2 is tagged degree='no degree assigned'. Both operate exclusively on death sentences for capital felonies. The table's own rationale for sentence 1 ('capital felony here describes the OFFENSE OF CONVICTION, not the resulting penalty class') applies with equal force to sentence 2, which the table then declines to apply.
unread: Verified honest on its central claim. I independently confirmed the coverage assertion: all 52 rows exist as listed, and every operative provision I found in my own walk of the fetched text has a row. The row count claim ('52 rows against the prior 24') is accurate.

Verified honest on `level`. 775.082 assigns no severity levels and is not itself a ranked offense; level is null in all 52 rows and nothing was guessed. The unread field's correction identifying s. 921.0023 (not s. 921.0022) as the source of DEFAULT levels for unranked felonies is substantively right, and adding a row for (8)(d) as the provision that switches the Code on is a genuine improvement.

Verified honest on the four residual in-section ambiguities disclosed -- (9)(a)1.o.'s undefined outer boundary, (5)'s chapter 316 / local-ordinance carve-out, (3)(c)'s missing written-finding subparagraph and anomalous 20-year threshold, and (9)(a)3.a.'s degreeless 'felony punishable by life'. All four are real and all four are correctly characterized as unresolved from this text.

DISHONEST BY OMISSION on one point: the field does not disclose the 14 free-text values written into the typed `scope` column. Given that the field's own opening paragraph attacks the prior version for 'a cross-reference bibliography dressed as a coverage disclosure' driving 'a false whole-section pass through a build guard', an undisclosed systematic typed-field violation is exactly the class of defect this field is supposed to surface.

Quote spot-checks (six, not three) all passed against the text I fetched: (1)(a), (3)(a)1., (3)(a)4.a., (8)(a), (9)(a)3. lead-in, and both sentences of (2) are verbatim. The (9)(a)1. named-offense row's elisions at o. and before r. are correctly marked with ellipses and the row states plainly that it is not the whole of subparagraph 1. 775.082.notes:
COMPLETENESS = whole-section, and I set it after my own walk, not on the builder's say-so. Every provision I independently enumerated has a row, including the ones the audit brief predicts get dropped: the terminal sub-subparagraphs (1)(b)3., (3)(a)5.c., (3)(b)2.c., (9)(a)1.r., (9)(d)2., (8)(e), and (11).

VERDICT = FAIL on correctness, not coverage.

The table's headline achievement is real and I confirm it: 775.082(9)(a)1.o. -- 'Any felony that involves the use or threat of physical force or violence against an individual' -- is the exact structural trap named in the brief. It sits at position o. between sixteen named offenses, it has no degree floor, and it drags the (9)(a)3. mandatory minimums (life / 30 / 15 / flat 5 years at 100 percent under (9)(b)) onto ANY violent felony including a third degree felony satisfied by threat alone. The table surfaces it, gives it its own row, and propagates the consequence into all four (9)(a)3. tier rows. 775.082(9)(a)1.r.'s 'any felony violation' of five cross-referenced sections is the same shape and is also caught. That is the danger class this audit exists for, and on that axis the table is right.

But correctness is a separate axis and the table loses it. The `scope` column is a typed field and it holds 14 prose sentences that match no enum value. The brief's check 5 is explicit that a wrong value in a typed field is a wrong value; these are not even wrong-but-typed, they are untyped. Compounding it, 'prior' is applied to (9)(c) and (9)(d)2., which carry no criminal-history element -- the precise error the table wrote four separate correction notices about. A table cannot spend its trigger prose litigating five inherited scope tags while committing fourteen worse ones and one repeat of the original.

Secondary: the (3)(a)1. row contradicts the (3)(a)4.a. row on whether any other life-felony tier states an express minimum term (4.a.(II) does -- 25 years). The universal 'no dollar, quantity, or weight element anywhere in s. 775.082' is false as to subsection (10)'s 22-point gate. And (9)(a)3.'s election clause cites only 'subparagraph 1.', which the (9)(a)2. row's 'fully independent pathway' claim never addresses.

Fix the scope column to enum values, reconcile (3)(a)1. against 4.a.(II), split (3)(a)4.a.(I)/(II), address the subparagraph-1-only election clause, and this passes.

fs 741.2901.notes:
INDEPENDENT FETCH FIRST. I pulled https://www.flsenate.gov/Laws/Statutes/2025/741.2901 via WebFetch, then re-pulled the raw HTML with curl and stripped tags to avoid trusting a summarizing model. Both agree exactly.

MY OWN PROVISION WALK (built before reading their table). Structure is: (1), (2), (3), History. That is the complete section. There are NO paragraphs ((a)/(b)) and NO subparagraphs (1./2.) at any level - confirmed against raw HTML, not just the summary. Provisions assigning a degree, mandatory minimum, or enhancement: ZERO.
- (1) Directive to state attorneys to create DV units and train staff. Administrative. No degree, no minimum, no enhancement.
- (2) Legislative intent; pro-prosecution policy; prosecutors decide over victim objection. Contains the phrase "both length and severity of sentence ... can be greater," but that is a statement of legislative rationale describing why criminal prosecution is preferred over contempt. It assigns nothing and enhances nothing. Correctly given no row.
- (3) Pre-first-appearance investigation of defendant's history; that information presented at first appearance, bond, and sentencing; mandatory pretrial custody until first appearance; victim-safety factor in bail. Procedural/custody. No degree, no minimum, no enhancement.

1. MISSING PROVISIONS - none. Every provision that assigns a degree, mandatory minimum, or enhancement is represented, because there are none. Subsections (1) and (2) carry no row, and correctly so: neither is penal, so neither warrants a row. I deliberately did NOT list them under "missing," because in this schema "missing" means a provision that should have a row and doesn't. Flagging them there would falsely signal a defect. Reporting them here instead, as required.

2. NO-LOWER-BOUND PROVISIONS - none, and none possible. But that language governs an investigation-and-disclosure duty, not a penalty scoped by criminal history, so tagging it would have been a misuse. Null is correct.

6. QUOTES - only one quote exists in the table, so I could not spot-check three. I verified that one character-by-character against the raw HTML. It is verbatim, not paraphrase. Its central factual claim - "the section consists of exactly three subsections ... no paragraphs or subparagraphs (no (a)/(b), no 1./2.) at any level" - is the one claim that, if false, would hide the exact error class this audit hunts. From the rows alone a reader cannot tell whether (1) and (2) were examined and cleared or simply skipped. It does not produce an error here, because that first half assigns no degree, minimum, or enhancement; it is a consideration-and-disclosure directive addressed to the court and the State Attorney. fs-784.041.notes:
INDEPENDENT FETCH FIRST. I pulled the raw HTML of 784.041 (2025) and stripped tags before reading the table, then pulled and parsed 921.0022 separately.

MY OWN PROVISION LIST (built before comparison): (1) chapeau, (1)(a), (1)(b), (2)(a), (2)(b) chapeau, (2)(b)1., (2)(b)2., (3), History (s. 1, ch. 97-183; s. 1, ch. 2007-133). Section ends at (3); there is no (4). Exactly one provision in the entire section assigns a degree: (3).

1. MISSING PROVISIONS — none. Every provision that assigns a degree, mandatory minimum, or enhancement has a row. The table merges (1)(a)+(1)(b) into the (1) row and folds the (2)(b) chapeau into the (2)(b)1. row. I considered flagging this as three rowless provisions, but declined: all three are quoted verbatim in the rows that absorb them, all three are correctly characterized (the (1) row explicitly states both paragraphs are required and joined by "and"), and none assigns a degree, minimum, or enhancement. This is a granularity nit, not a coverage gap. It is inconsistent, though — the table gave standalone rows to the purely definitional (2)(b)1. and (2)(b)2. while merging the equally non-assigning (1)(a) and (1)(b).

2. NO-LOWER-BOUND — this is where I pushed hardest, and the table holds. The trap-shaped construct in this section is (2)(b): first subparagraph is a named item ("Family or household member"), later subparagraph is a different thing entirely ("Dating relationship") with no shared qualifier. Both have rows. I checked (1)(a)/(1)(b) for the same shape; covered. The real substantive no-lower-bound hazard here is (2)(a)'s disjunctive "so as to create a risk of OR cause great bodily harm" — strangulation is complete on RISK alone, with no requirement of actual great bodily harm, unlike felony battery under (1)(b) which requires actual great bodily harm, permanent disability, or permanent disfigurement. The table caught this and called it out in capitals. It also correctly records that the section has no dollar tier, no quantity threshold, and no floor of any kind anywhere.

3. DEGREES — correct. Operative words of (3): "commits a felony of the third degree." One flat degree covering both offenses. No tiering, no prior-conviction bump, no victim-class or place-based enhancement in the section. Verified against the raw text.

4. LEVEL — verified independently, not taken on trust. I parsed 921.0022's full chart, enumerated all ten level headings with their paragraph letters ((a)=LEVEL 1 through (j)=LEVEL 10), and searched every occurrence of "784.04". Result: `784.041 | 3rd | Felony battery; domestic battery by strangulation.` appears exactly once, inside paragraph (f) LEVEL 6. Whole section, no subsection split, no duplicate entry at any other level. The table's level 6 and its (3)(f) paragraph cite are both correct. For contrast I confirmed the neighbors are different statutes: 784.045(1)(a)1., (1)(a)2., (1)(b) and 784.048(4), (7) are LEVEL 7; 784.048(3) and (5) are LEVEL 6.

5. SCOPE VALUES — no misuse. The table never uses "prior" or "item," so neither can be misapplied. "victim" appears on (2)(a), (2)(b)1., and (2)(b)2., which is the correct sense: the family/household-member and dating-relationship elements are exactly what narrows the victim class and distinguishes strangulation from ordinary battery. scope is null on (1) and (3), correct — felony battery has no victim-class element and (3) applies to both offenses generally.

6. QUOTES — I spot-checked more than three; I diffed all five against the stripped source. All five are verbatim, including the curly quotation marks around the defined terms, the medical-act carve-out sentence in (2)(a), and the full s. 775.082/775.083/775.084 string in (3). No paraphrase is presented as quotation. Only artifact is collapsed whitespace at run-in boundaries ("he or she:(a) Actually", "the term:1. "Family"), which reflects the source's inline markup, not altered wording.

7. THE unread FIELD — honest, and unusually so. It correctly volunteers that 921.0022 was searched programmatically rather than read in full, and that only the single Level 6 entry was inspected. It correctly separates in-section coverage from cross-referenced statutes. Two small imprecisions, neither dishonest: s. 775.0877 is the HIV-testing statute, not a reclassification statute, so naming it in that clause is a mislabel; and it does not name 784.08, 784.081, or 784.083 specifically, relying on the catch-all "any reclassification statute that could elevate a 784.041 offense from outside this section," which does cover them.

ONE WORDING CAUTION, not scored as an error: the (3) row asserts there is no "victim-class ... enhancement anywhere in the section." True as to enhancements, but a careless reader could take it to mean victim class is irrelevant to 784.041, when (2)(a) is entirely victim-class-defined as a matter of elements. fs-784.07.notes:
I fetched https://www.flsenate.gov/Laws/Statutes/2025/784.07 twice (WebFetch plus a raw curl + tag-strip of the HTML, saved at /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-wyattbensman-Library-Mobile-Documents-com-apple-CloudDocs-The-Digital-Wash-client-sites-hines-mccarty-site/f479602a-ea97-4d2d-a022-47b21330898b/scratchpad/78407.html) and built my own provision list before reading the table.

MY INDEPENDENT LIST -- 11 operative provisions. (1)(a)-(h) are definitions only, no degree/min/enhancement. (2) preamble sets the victim trigger but assigns nothing on its own. Then: (2)(a) assault 2d misd -> 1st misd; (2)(b) sent.1 battery 1st misd -> 3d deg fel; (2)(b) sent.2 6-month min, LEO victim + riot/aggravated riot; (2)(c) sent.1 agg assault 3d fel -> 2d fel; (2)(c) sent.2 3-year min, LEO victim; (2)(d) sent.1 agg battery 2d fel -> 1st fel; (2)(d) sent.2 5-year min, LEO victim; (3)(a) 3-year min, firearm or destructive device possessed; (3)(b) 8-year min, semiauto + high-capacity magazine OR machine gun; (3) undesignated flush-left closing paragraph, no suspension/deferral/withholding, no gain-time or discretionary early release; (4) one-level bump under 921.0022 for any felony violation in furtherance of a riot. Statute ends at (4) -- I confirmed against the raw HTML that there is no (5) and no further paragraph the markdown converter could have swallowed.

The table has exactly 11 rows and they map 1:1 onto that list. Nothing is missing.

NO-LOWER-BOUND CHECK (the reason this audit exists). I went looking specifically for the 812.014(2)(b)2 / 775.082(9)(a)1.o / 817.568(2)(b) pattern and the candidates here are (3)(a) and (4). The table caught both. Row (4) states in terms "Applies to any felony under this section ... with no lower bound on severity beyond felony status" -- correct; it reaches (2)(b) third-degree felonies, not just the aggravated offenses. Row (3)(a) states "Possession alone suffices; no discharge, use, or display element and no victim-injury element" -- correct; it reaches ANY firearm or destructive device, and it is triggered by a (2)(b) battery, which is the LOWEST felony in the section. Neither row implies a floor. This is the failure mode the audit exists to catch and it is not present.

DEGREES CHECKED WORD BY WORD against the operative text: 2d misd -> 1st misd (a); 1st misd -> 3d fel (b); 3d fel -> 2d fel (c); 2d fel -> 1st fel (d). All four match. The four mandatory-minimum rows and the flush-left row correctly carry degree "no degree assigned" -- none of them reclassifies anything, they attach to the degree set by the preceding sentence. Row (4) likewise correctly assigns no degree: it moves the 921.0022 ranking, not the degree, and the table says so explicitly rather than sliding it into a degree bump.

LEVELS: every level is null and the unread field states why. No guessed level, so nothing to fail on under criterion 4. Note the gap though: 784.07(2)(b), (2)(c), (2)(d) are ranked in 921.0022, and row (4) is entirely about a 921.0022 level, so this table cannot actually compute what (4) does. Disclosed, not concealed.

SCOPE VALUES: "victim" on all seven subsection (2) rows is right -- the reclassification turns on who was assaulted or battered. "prior" is not used anywhere, so it cannot be misused. "item" on (3)(a)/(3)(b) is the only arguable call: the possessed firearm/machine gun is the thing involved in the offense, which fits the stated definition, though the subject of the offense is a person. I do not treat it as a wrong value. Nulls on the flush-left row and (4) are honest non-claims rather than filler.

QUOTES: I spot-checked more than three against the raw text -- (2)(b) sent.2, (2)(d) sent.2, (3)(b), the flush-left paragraph, and (4) are all verbatim, punctuation included. One formatting caveat, not a substantive defect: the (3)(a) quote splices the subsection (3) preamble onto paragraph (a) with the "(a)" designator embedded mid-sentence and no ellipsis or bracket marking the join. The words are accurate and nothing is dropped -- the preamble is genuinely required for the sentence to parse -- but it is an assembled quotation presented as contiguous text.

TWO CAUTIONS THAT ARE NOT ERRORS BUT SHOULD BE KNOWN. First, the (2)(a) trigger lists "public transit employee or agent" among the protected persons. That phrase does appear in subsection (2) and is defined at (1)(f), so the table's phrasing ("listed in subsection (2)") is literally true -- but it appears ONLY in the second, "while the ... is engaged in the lawful performance" enumeration, not in the first charging enumeration of who may be assaulted or battered. That drafting gap is litigable and the table does not flag it. Second, the (2)(c) mandatory-minimum row says "No riot element and no weapon element is required," which is correct and useful; the parallel (2)(d) 5-year row omits the same statement. The (2)(d) trigger does not assert a riot element, so it is not wrong, but the asymmetry could let a reader carry the riot element down from (2)(b).

It claims nothing inside 784.07 was left unread and enumerates the actual structure -- (1)(a)-(h), (2) preamble, (2)(a)-(d), (3) preamble, (3)(a)-(b), the flush-left closer, (4), History -- which matches the real section exactly. fs-784.08.notes:
NO MISSING PROVISIONS. I fetched the statute myself and parsed the raw HTML rather than the rendered text: the SectionBody contains exactly three div.Subsection nodes ((1), (2), (3)) and four div.Paragraph nodes ((a)-(d)) nested under (2), plus the History block. That is 7 provision nodes and the table has a row for each. Coverage is genuinely whole-section, so completeness is set accordingly.

NO-LOWER-BOUND CHECK -- the pattern this audit exists to catch does not apply and was not fallen into. 784.08 has no subparagraph layer at all, so there is no "paragraph whose first subparagraph is a tier and whose later subparagraphs have no floor." The statute's actual no-floor feature is different: the (2) introductory language imposes strict liability as to the victim's age ("regardless of whether he or she knows or has reason to know the age of the victim"). There is no knowledge floor whatsoever. The builder DID capture this, both in the 784.08(2) row and restated in each of (a) through (d). Credit where due -- this is the analogue of the trap and it was not missed. I also confirmed the converse: subsection (1) does NOT contain the knowledge clause, and the builder correctly did not extend it there.

QUOTES -- I checked all seven, not three. I extracted every span.Text-Intro-Justify from the source HTML, normalized whitespace and unescaped entities, and compared each table quote by exact string equality. All 7 returned EXACT. No paraphrase presented as quotation, no truncation, no silent joining. The 784.08(3) quote correctly inlines the "s. 948.01" cross-reference that the source renders as a separate anchor element.

DEGREES -- all correct against the operative words. (2)(a) "to a felony of the first degree" = first degree felony. (2)(b) "to a felony of the second degree" = second degree felony. (2)(c) "to a felony of the third degree" = third degree felony. (2)(d) "to a misdemeanor of the first degree" = first degree misdemeanor. Rows (1), (2) intro, and (3) correctly carry "no degree assigned" -- none of the three assigns a degree, and (2) intro is correctly flagged as governing (a)-(d) rather than standing alone.

SCOPE VALUES -- not misused. "victim" is used on the six rows keyed to the 65-and-older victim class, which is the correct sense. "prior" is never used, and correctly so: nothing in 784.08 turns on criminal history. "item" is never used, correctly, since nothing is taken. Row (3) carries scope null; that is defensible for a pure sentencing-procedure rule, though it is mildly inconsistent with the other six rows given that (3) governs the same victim-defined offense set.

WHY FAIL DESPITE FULL COVERAGE AND CLEAN QUOTES/DEGREES. The sole basis is the three unpopulated level values. I want the parent to see the reasoning explicitly because it is a close call and cuts against rewarding honest disclosure:

Arguing for PASS -- nulls are not "wrong or guessed levels" under criterion 4. The builder declined to guess and disclosed the omission accurately, which is exactly the behavior the audit's criterion 7 rewards. Failing that behavior punishes the right instinct.

Arguing for FAIL, which is where I landed -- the rows carry a typed level field, three of the seven rows are ranked felonies, and those three are enumerated in 921.0022 by their own 784.08 subsection cites with zero interpretive judgment required. One additional fetch fills them. Under "PASS only if complete AND correct," the table's typed data is not complete. Given the stated stake that this feeds a live build guard, shipping null where a scoresheet level is unambiguously determinable is a material gap. Note also that (2)(d) SHOULD stay null -- a first degree misdemeanor is unranked -- so this is not a blanket "populate everything," it is three specific determinable values plus one correct null.

I found nothing affirmatively wrong, hence an empty "wrong" array. This is a narrow, data-completeness fail on an otherwise accurate table, not a broad one. If the schema treats level as optional, this flips to PASS.

SOFT NOTES, not fail-worthy. (a) Row (3) is labeled a "sentencing enhancement"; it is more precisely a prohibition on withholding or suspending, not an enhancement, though it falls in the enhancement bucket by elimination. (b) Its parenthetical gloss "no probation in lieu of sentence" initially read as an overreach, since probation imposed AS a sentence remains available for the (2)(c) and (2)(d) offenses; on closer reading the builder's phrase "in lieu of sentence" correctly targets only the barred form, so this is accurate as written. (c) The (2)(c) and (2)(d) triggers gloss the statutory "battery" and "assault" as "simple battery" and "simple assault." That is standard usage and consistent with the reclassification operating from the first degree misdemeanor and second degree misdemeanor baselines respectively, so it is not a misstatement.

UNREAD FIELD IS HONEST. Every claim verified. The assertion that the section contains only (1), (2)(a)-(d), (3) and History is true against the raw markup. The 921.0022 disclosure is not merely honest but unusually candid -- it volunteers that the (2) offenses "are ranked in the chart by their own listed entries," which is precisely the fact that makes the omission fixable, and it correctly explains the nulls as refusal-to-guess rather than absence-of-ranking. The remaining items (784.011/.021/.03/.045 baselines, 948.01, 775.082-.084, sibling 784.07x sections, session laws, case law) are all genuinely outside the section and correctly scoped out. I spot-checked the four baseline degrees the builder declined to verify -- assault 2nd deg misd, aggravated assault 3rd deg fel, battery 1st deg misd, aggravated battery 2nd deg fel -- and they are consistent with what (2)(a)-(d) recite, so the unverified baselines happen to be right even though the builder properly refused to claim so.

missing: Introductory flush paragraph (before subsection (1)) -- the 21 C.F.R. carve-out has NO ROW. 'The provisions of this section shall not be construed to include within any of the schedules contained in this section any excluded drugs listed within the purview of 21 C.F.R. s. 1308.22, styled "Excluded Substances"; 21 C.F.R. s. 1308.24, styled "Exempt Chemical Preparations"; 21 C.F.R. s. 1308.32, styled "Exempted Prescription Products"; or 21 C.F.R. s. 1308.34, styled "Exempt Anabolic Steroid Products."' This is a NO-LOWER-BOUND scope rule: it applies to ANY quantity of ANY substance in ANY of the five schedules, and it determines whether conduct is chargeable at all under s. 893.13 / s. 893.135. The builder read it (it is listed as read in the unread field) and elected to give it no row while giving a row to a structurally identical scope rule at (3)(c). Inconsistent inclusion.

F.S. 893.03(3)(d)2., SECOND SENTENCE -- has NO ROW, and it is the precise failure pattern this audit exists to prevent. Subparagraph 2 opens with an EXCLUSION: 'The term does not include an anabolic steroid that is expressly intended for administration through implants to cattle or other nonhuman species and that has been approved by the United States Secretary of Health and Human Services for such administration.' The very next sentence REVERSES it with no threshold, no quantity, and no lower bound of any kind: 'However, any person who prescribes, dispenses, or distributes such a steroid for human use is considered to have prescribed, dispensed, or distributed an anabolic steroid within the meaning of this paragraph.' A reader who opens (3)(d)2 to learn whether cattle-implant steroids are covered finds 'no' in sentence one and stops -- which is exactly the 812.014(2)(b)2 / 775.082(9)(a)1.o / 817.568(2)(b) error. The deeming sentence pulls otherwise-excluded substances back into Schedule III for ANY person who prescribes, dispenses, or distributes for human use, which is what makes the conduct chargeable.
wrong: ROW 1, trigger field -- FALSE UNIVERSAL CLAIM stated as verified fact: 'This is the only penalty-affecting sentence in the entire section.' It is not. The introductory flush paragraph's 21 C.F.R. exclusion rule and the second sentence of (3)(d)2 are both penalty-affecting scope rules under the same standard the builder used to admit this row. A downstream consumer reading 'the only penalty-affecting sentence in the entire section' stops looking -- the claim actively suppresses the two provisions above. This is a correctness defect in a typed field, independently verifiable against the statute text.

ROW 1, trigger field -- material qualifier dropped when describing the covered items. The row characterizes (3)(c)3. as 'not more than 300 mg hydrocodone per 100 ml, or not more than 15 mg per dosage unit, with an isoquinoline alkaloid of opium'. The statute reads 'with a FOURFOLD OR GREATER QUANTITY of an isoquinoline alkaloid of opium.' Omitting 'fourfold or greater quantity of' makes the description over-broad -- it would sweep in preparations containing any trace of an isoquinoline alkaloid, which (3)(c)3. does not reach. Not presented as a quotation, so not a quote-integrity violation, but it is a substantive misdescription of the provision the row exists to describe.
fs-893.03.notes:
INDEPENDENT FETCH FIRST. I pulled https://www.flsenate.gov/Laws/Statutes/2025/893.03 with curl, stripped it to 1,152 lines of text, and built my own provision list before opening the table.

EXHAUSTIVE SEARCH: grep -iE '893\.135|felony|degree|punish|penalt|mandatory|minimum|charging|misdemeanor|s\. 775|921\.0022|enhance' returns EXACTLY ONE hit across the whole section -- the (3)(c) flush language. Cross-reference sweep returns only s. 893.135 (3x), 21 C.F.R. ss. 1308.22/.24/.32/.34, and s. 505 of the FDCA in (3)(g). There is no reference anywhere in this section to s. 893.13, s. 775.082, s. 775.083, s. 775.084, or the s. 921.0022 ranking chart.

CONFIRMED CORRECT (I tried to break these and could not):
- Row 1 quote is VERBATIM. I diffed it character-by-character against source; the only deltas are whitespace artifacts introduced by HTML anchor tags wrapping 's. 893.135' and 's. 893.135(6)'. No paraphrase presented as quotation.
- Row 1 placement is correct: the flush language does immediately follow (3)(c)7., and it does govern subparagraphs 3. and 4.
- degree 'no degree assigned' is CORRECT. F.S. 893.03 assigns no degree of offense, no mandatory minimum, and no enhancement anywhere. It is a pure scheduling section. A table with zero degree rows is the right answer here.
- level null is CORRECT and honestly reasoned -- not guessed, and the builder said why.
- scope 'item' is a LEGITIMATE use: the thing involved is the hydrocodone preparation. Not a misuse of 'prior' or 'item'.

unread FIELD IS HONEST. I verified its structural enumeration against the source and it is exactly right: (1)(a)-(d), (2)(a)-(d), (3)(a)-(g), (4)(a)-(b), (5)(a)-(c), plus intro flush, History, and footnote 1. It correctly and voluntarily discloses that s. 893.135, s. 893.13, the s. 921.0022 chart, and the four C.F.R. carve-out sections were NOT read. No dishonesty found here. Returned unread as empty because I found no unread-field defect to report.

COMPLETENESS vs VERDICT (separate axes, per instructions):
- completeness = 'whole-section'. Every paragraph and subparagraph was in fact walked -- I confirmed this against the real structure -- and the class of provisions that assign a degree, mandatory minimum, or enhancement is EMPTY in this section and therefore fully covered. Claiming partial coverage would itself be false and I will not assert it to manufacture a finding.
- verdict = 'FAIL' on CORRECTNESS. The table covers the section but states a falsehood: 'This is the only penalty-affecting sentence in the entire section.' That claim is refutable from the text, and it is the specific kind of claim that stops a downstream reader from finding (3)(d)2's second sentence -- a no-lower-bound re-inclusion rule hiding behind a first-sentence exclusion, i.e. the exact recurring error named in the audit brief. Per the rule that a table can be complete and still wrong, this is whole-section + FAIL.

SEVERITY ORDER: (1) the false 'only penalty-affecting sentence' claim, (2) omitted (3)(d)2 second sentence, (3) omitted intro C.F.R. carve-out, (4) dropped 'fourfold or greater quantity' qualifier.

wrong: 896.104(4)(a)1. — level is null, but the offense IS ranked: F.S. 921.0022(3)(g) LEVEL 7, entry '896.104 (4)(a)1. 3rd Structuring transactions to evade reporting or registration requirements, financial transactions exceeding $300 but less than $20,000.' Verifiable field left empty.

896.104(4)(a)2. — level is null, but it is ranked at F.S. 921.0022(3)(h) LEVEL 8, entry '896.104 (4)(a)2. 2nd Structuring transactions to evade reporting or registration requirements, financial transactions totaling or exceeding $20,000 but less than $100,000.'

896.104(4)(a)3. — level is null, but it is ranked at F.S. 921.0022(3)(i) LEVEL 9, entry '896.104 (4)(a)3. 1st Structuring transactions to evade reporting or registration requirements, financial transactions totaling or exceeding $100,000.'

896.104(4)(a)1. — min:300 misencodes an EXCLUSIVE bound as an inclusive floor. The statute reaches transactions 'exceeding $300'; exactly $300.00 is not this offense. min:300 and row 2's inclusive min:20000 ('totaling or exceeding') are typed identically despite opposite semantics, so the field cannot be read correctly by a consumer. fs-896.104.notes:
METHOD: fetched https://www.flsenate.gov/Laws/Statutes/2025/896.104 as raw HTML and stripped tags myself before opening the table, then independently enumerated every provision. Also fetched F.S. 921.0022 raw HTML (387KB) and programmatically mapped each 896.104 entry to its LEVEL heading.

1. MISSING PROVISIONS: none. Every provision that assigns a degree or enhancement has a row. (1), (2)(a)-(c), (3)(a)-(c), and (6) correctly have no rows -- (2) and (3) define the prohibited conduct and (6) is a construction clause; none assigns a degree, minimum, or enhancement.

2. NO-LOWER-BOUND CHECK (the reason this audit exists): I specifically hunted the 812.014(2)(b)2 / 817.568(2)(b) pattern here and it does NOT occur. Paragraph (4)(a) has exactly three subparagraphs and ALL THREE are dollar tiers -- there is no later subparagraph that switches to a non-dollar trigger with no floor. The genuinely floorless provisions in this section are (4)(b), (4)(b)'s second-or-subsequent clause, and (4)(c), and the builder caught all three and correctly marked them as having no lower bound. Splitting (4)(b) into two rows to isolate the recidivist trigger was the right call. This axis is clean.

3. DEGREES: verified word-for-word against the operative text. 3rd / 2nd / 1st on (4)(a)1./2./3. are all correct. No degree is misstated.

4. LEVELS: this is the failure. All three degree-bearing rows carry level:null while 921.0022 ranks them 7, 8, and 9. The rows are not guessed, but they are empty where a published, checkable value exists, and level drives the scoresheet. Note the ranking is one level higher than intuition suggests for each tier (a 3rd-degree felony at Level 7), so a downstream consumer cannot infer it -- the null is load-bearing.

5. SCOPE: 'prior' on the second-or-subsequent row is defensible; it is a recidivist trigger keyed to a repeat violation, not to an amount or an item. No misuse of 'item'. Worth flagging only that 'second or subsequent violation' is not strictly criminal history -- it can be a second violation charged in the same proceeding -- but 'prior' is the closest correct value available.

6. QUOTES: spot-checked five, not three, against the raw text. (4)(a)1., (4)(a)2., (4)(c), and the second-or-subsequent clause are all exact. No paraphrase is presented as quotation anywhere. One nit: the (4)(b) general-fine quote stops at '...whichever is greater' and silently drops the ', except that...' continuation with no ellipsis; the retained words are verbatim and the dropped text is quoted in the adjacent row, so this is a formatting nit, not a fabrication.

7. UNREAD FIELD: the inventory is honest and matches the actual structure exactly, including all nine lettered/numbered subdivisions and the History note. readWhole:true is accurate. The one dishonest note is the level excuse addressed above.

VERDICT RATIONALE: coverage is whole-section and no provision was missed, so completeness is 'whole-section'. Verdict is FAIL on the correctness axis only -- three verifiable 921.0022 levels left null on every degree-bearing row, plus two exclusive dollar thresholds encoded as inclusive minimums. Fixes: set level 7/8/9 on (4)(a)1./2./3., and resolve the min semantics for 'exceeding $300' and 'more than $10,000'.

wrong: 817.034(3)(e)2 row -- trigger misstates the reach of the deemed-value rule. It says the less-than-$300 default 'bears on which tier of (4)(b) applies.' (3)(e) defines 'Value' for the entire section ('As used in this section, the term'), and (4)(a) grades on 'aggregate value.' An unascertainable value deemed less than $300 therefore also feeds (3)(e)3 aggregation and lands the case in (4)(a)3, the third degree felony tier. The builder correctly confined (3)(e)3 to (4)(a) because the statute expressly says 'under paragraph (4)(a)' -- then mirrored that limitation onto (3)(e)2 in reverse, where the statute contains no such limiting language. A reader of this row would conclude the default only affects the misdemeanor grading. It affects felony grading too.

unread[4] -- the entry is labeled 'NOT READ (out of scope, non-penal)' and then states in its own text that 817.034(4)(d) and (4)(f) 'were read but generate no penalty rows.' The label is false on its face and contradicts unread[0], which asserts nothing in the section was left unread. The field is being used as a no-row justification list rather than an unread list, so a consumer keying on membership in unread would wrongly conclude (4)(d) and (4)(f) were never opened. Note the error runs in the conservative direction -- it over-declares non-reading rather than concealing it -- and unread[0]'s coverage claim independently verifies as true against the raw text.

fs-817.034.notes:
COVERAGE: verified complete. I fetched https://www.flsenate.gov/Laws/Statutes/2025/817.034 twice (WebFetch plus a raw curl + tag-strip to guard against summarizer dropout) and walked every subsection in order before reading the table. All nine provisions that assign a degree or an enhancement have rows: (4)(a)1-3, (4)(b)1-2, (4)(c)1-4. There are no mandatory minimums in this section. Nothing is missing.

NO-LOWER-BOUND CHECK -- the reason this audit exists -- PASSES CLEANLY. (4)(a)3 (F3, any aggregate value under $20,000) and (4)(b)2 (M1, any value under $300) both carry min:null with explicit NO LOWER BOUND language. More importantly, the builder did NOT fall into the target failure mode on (4)(c): paragraph (4)(c)'s first subparagraph is a reclassification of a misdemeanor, and someone opening (4)(c) to answer a felony question could easily have read (c)2 or (c)3 and stopped. All four subparagraphs have rows, all four carry min:null/max:null, and all four triggers say 'value-independent.' This matters concretely -- the only M1 in the section is (4)(b)2, which has no floor, so (4)(c)1 converts a one-dollar communications fraud against a minor into a third degree felony. That is captured.

DEGREES: all nine check out against the operative words. 'felony of the first degree' -> first degree felony (4)(a)1; second (4)(a)2; third (4)(a)3; 'third degree felony' (4)(b)1; 'misdemeanor of the first degree' -> first degree misdemeanor (4)(b)2; F3, F2, F1, life felony for (4)(c)1-4 respectively. Min/max boundary convention is internally consistent and exclusive-max throughout (50000/20000/300 each appear as one row's min and the adjacent row's max, never double-counted).

QUOTES: spot-checked four, not three -- (4)(a)1 (paragraph intro plus subparagraph, correctly concatenated), (3)(e)2, (4)(c)1 (intro plus subparagraph), and (4)(e) -- character-for-character against the raw HTML. All verbatim. No paraphrase presented as quotation.

SCOPE VALUES: 'victim' on the four (4)(c) rows is used correctly for victim characteristics. No misuse of 'prior' or 'item'; neither appears.

LEVELS: all null with explicit disclosure that 921.0022 was not fetched. Not guessed, so no violation of the level rule. This does leave the table without sentencing-score data, which is a gap in usefulness but not in correctness.

WHY FAIL RATHER THAN PASS: neither defect misstates a degree, a dollar threshold, or a floor, and no penalty row is wrong. The verdict turns on the (3)(e)2 trigger, which is an affirmative misstatement about how the statute operates -- it tells the reader the deemed-value default is a (4)(b) problem when it is a section-wide valuation rule that reaches felony grading under (4)(a). Under the stated standard (PASS only if complete AND correct) that is a correctness failure, though a narrower one than the misstated-degree failures cited from the previous batch. The fix is two sentences in one trigger plus relabeling unread[4]; the nine penalty rows need no change.

MINOR, NOT COUNTED AGAINST THE VERDICT: (3)(e)1.a-c (market value, written instruments, trade secrets) get no row while (3)(e)2 and (3)(e)3 do. Inconsistent treatment of the valuation definitions, but (e)1 assigns no degree, minimum, or enhancement, so it is not a completeness miss. Separately, the four (4)(c) rows put the OUTPUT degree in the typed degree field with no field carrying the input degree -- so (4)(c)1 renders as a 'third degree felony' row with null min and null max, which a consumer filtering on degree alone could misread as a standalone F3 at any value. The trigger text disambiguates, but the typed field does not.

wrong: unread[3] states a verifiable falsehood about the F.S. 921.0022 ranking chart: 'only 815.04(4)(a) at level 3 and 815.04(4)(b) at level 4.' I fetched https://www.flsenate.gov/Laws/Statutes/2025/921.0022 in full (all ten level tables, (3)(a) LEVEL 1 through (3)(j) LEVEL 10, History line present, so the page was not truncated) and grepped every occurrence of '815'. The builder's own disclosed method -- 'I searched the chart rather than reading all ten level tables line by line' -- is what produced the error: it found the citation strings but never confirmed which LEVEL heading they fell under. The downstream conclusion ('no entry for 815.06 exists anywhere in the chart') is independently CORRECT -- I confirmed no 815.06 string appears at any level -- so every row's level:null is right by the stated rule. But the field asserting the verification is itself wrong on the only two data points it offers, which is exactly the class of unverified-assertion-presented-as-verified that this audit exists to catch. unread: s. 775.082, s. 775.083, s. 775.084 -- not read by me; any habitual/violent-career-offender enhancement in 775.084 is outside the scope of this audit and outside this table, as the builder correctly disclosed.
