fs-815.06.notes:
METHOD. I fetched https://www.flsenate.gov/Laws/Statutes/2025/815.06 myself via curl and stripped the HTML to text before opening the table (the WebFetch summarizer refused to reproduce the section, so I worked from raw source). I built my own independent list of penalty-assigning provisions, then compared.

MY INDEPENDENT LIST -- 8 provisions assign a degree; none assigns a mandatory minimum; none assigns an enhancement:
(3)(a) 3rd deg catch-all; (3)(b)1 2nd deg, damage/loss at least $5,000; (3)(b)2 2nd deg, scheme or artifice to defraud or obtain property; (3)(b)3 2nd deg, interrupts governmental operation or public service; (3)(b)4 2nd deg, transit-belonging device; (3)(c)1 1st deg, endangers human life; (3)(c)2 1st deg, affects medical equipment; (4) 1st deg misdemeanor, modifies equipment or supplies.
The table has exactly these 8 and no others. Coverage is whole-section -- hence completeness "whole-section" despite the FAIL verdict.

CHECK 1, MISSING PROVISIONS -- NONE. Walked every subsection in order. (1) is a definition of "user." (2)(a)-(f) are conduct elements only; (2) itself assigns no degree, which (3)(a) supplies -- correctly no row, and note (2)(f) (audio/video surveillance, added 2019) is punished under (3)(a) with no tier of its own, so it needs no separate row. (5)(a)-(b) civil damages and attorney fees. (6) forfeiture under ss. 932.701-932.704, a collateral consequence, not a degree/minimum/enhancement -- the builder's exclusion is reasoned and I agree. (7)(a)-(c) exemptions. (8) dual-jurisdiction deeming. (9) interactive-computer-service carve-out. None of these assigns a degree.

CHECK 2, NO-LOWER-BOUND PROVISIONS -- CLEAN. This is the specific trap the assignment describes, and 815.06(3)(b) is textbook shaped for it: subparagraph 1 is a $5,000 dollar tier, and subparagraphs 2, 3, and 4 are entirely different things with NO dollar floor whatsoever. An agent that opened (3)(b) to find the $5,000 threshold, read subparagraph 1, and stopped would have produced a table implying second-degree treatment requires $5,000. This table did not make that error. (3)(b)2, (3)(b)3, and (3)(b)4 each carry min:null and each says "NO LOWER BOUND" in the trigger, correctly. Same for (3)(c)1, (3)(c)2, and (4). (3)(a) correctly carries min:null as a catch-all. No row anywhere implies a floor the statute does not impose. I specifically confirmed the (3)(b) chapeau reads "violates subsection (2) and:" with the $5,000 language confined to subparagraph 1 only, and that the (3)(c) chapeau reads "if the violation:" with no monetary condition.

CHECK 3, DEGREES -- ALL CORRECT against operative words. (3)(a) "felony of the third degree" -> third degree felony. (3)(b) chapeau "felony of the second degree" governs all four subparagraphs -> second degree felony on rows 1-4. (3)(c) chapeau "felony of the first degree" governs both subparagraphs -> first degree felony on both. (4) "misdemeanor of the first degree" -> first degree misdemeanor. Note (4) is a standalone offense not predicated on a subsection (2) violation, and the table's trigger says so explicitly, which is right.

CHECK 4, LEVELS -- all null, and null is correct. I verified independently: no 815.06 citation appears at any level of 921.0022. See the "wrong" array for the falsehood in the builder's supporting prose about 815.04.

CHECK 5, SCOPE -- no misuse, but one inconsistency. "prior" is never used, correctly (this statute has no recidivist tier). "item" is used on (3)(b)4 and (3)(c)2, where the tier does turn on the identity of the thing involved (a transit-owned device; a device affecting medical equipment), so the value is defensible on its own terms. The inconsistency: (3)(b)3 is the same species of tier -- it turns on the nature of what is disrupted (a governmental operation, public communication, transportation, or a water/gas/public-service supply) -- yet carries scope:null. Either (3)(b)3 should be "item" or (3)(b)4 should be null. Not a wrong value, but the field is applied unevenly across structurally identical subparagraphs.

CHECK 6, QUOTES -- I spot-checked all eight, not three, against the raw source. All eight are verbatim, including the two rows that fold the chapeau into the subparagraph quote ((3)(b)1 and (3)(c)1) -- the concatenation is faithful to the source text, which runs the chapeau and first subparagraph together on one line. No paraphrase is presented as quotation. Punctuation, the "; or" terminators on (3)(b)3 and (3)(c)1, and the "$5,000" figure all match.

CHECK 7, THE unread FIELD -- NOT HONEST. Entries 1-3 are accurate. Entry 4 is not; it asserts a chart verification whose only two supporting data points are both wrong. This is the sole basis for the FAIL.

VERDICT RATIONALE. Per the stated rule, PASS requires complete AND correct. Coverage is complete and every row is substantively correct -- eight of eight provisions present, degrees right, quotes verbatim, levels correctly null, and the no-lower-bound trap fully avoided. The table fails on correctness solely because a required typed field asserts a verification it did not perform accurately. The parent should treat the rows themselves as sound; the remediation is to correct or soften unread[3], not to rebuild the rows.

unread: F.S. 775.082/775.083/775.084 -- referenced punishment provisions, not read by me either; the table honestly discloses this.
42 U.S.C. s. 1320a-7b(b) safe-harbor scope referenced in (2)(a)5 -- not read by me.
F.S. 921.0022 in full -- I read only the (3)(a)-(3)(j) level headings and the three 409.920 chart lines, sufficient to confirm levels 7/7/9.
fs-409.920.notes:
INDEPENDENT INVENTORY (built before reading the table). Degree/min/enhancement provisions in F.S. 409.920 (2025, last amended s. 30 ch. 2025-88): (2)(b)1.a., (2)(b)1.b., (2)(b)1.c., (2)(b)2. (aggregation), (2)(b)3. (mandatory 5x fine). That is the complete set. Mechanical confirmation: grep for "felony of the [x] degree" yields exactly 3 hits section-wide; grep for mandatory|minimum|enhanc|second or subsequent|prior convic|misdemeanor|reclassif yields ZERO hits. No (2)(c) exists; the section ends at (10)(e) followed by the History note. (1) is definitions; (3) repayment-no-defense; (4) "paid for"; (5) business records; (6)-(7) evidentiary inferences; (8) reporter immunity; (9) AG duties (a)-(g); (10) AG powers (a)-(e). None assigns a degree. All seven (2)(a) prohibitions are conduct definitions with no penalty. So the table has a row for every provision that needs one -- coverage is whole-section.

(2) NO-LOWER-BOUND CHECK -- the reason this audit exists. Two provisions here have no floor and BOTH are correctly rowed. (2)(b)1.a. applies at ANY value however small (min: null, correctly flagged in the trigger). More importantly, (2)(b)3. is exactly the trap pattern described in the brief: a paragraph whose first subparagraph is a dollar tier and whose LATER subparagraph is something else entirely with no lower bound. The builder did NOT stop after reading (2)(b)1 -- it carried through to (2)(b)2 and (2)(b)3, and correctly characterized (2)(b)3 as applying to "EVERY conviction under subsection (2), at any degree and at any dollar value." That is the correct reading of "a person who is convicted of a violation of this subsection."

(3) DEGREES -- all three verified against operative words. "Ten thousand dollars or less"=third; "More than $10,000, but less than $50,000"=second; "Fifty thousand dollars or more"=first. The table also correctly resolves both boundary edges: exactly $10,000 falls in tier a (not b), exactly $50,000 falls in tier c (not b). Both edges are stated explicitly in the trigger text rather than left to inference. There is no statutory gap between tiers.

(4) LEVELS -- verified by reading the 921.0022 chart directly, not from memory. "409.920" appears exactly three times in the chart (no fourth entry hiding elsewhere). Chart line "(2)(b)1.a. 3rd Medicaid provider fraud; $10,000 or less" and "(2)(b)1.b. 2nd ... more than $10,000, but less than $50,000" both sit between the "(g) LEVEL 7" heading and the "(h) LEVEL 8" heading. "(2)(b)1.c. 1st ... $50,000 or more" sits between "(i) LEVEL 9" and "(j) LEVEL 10". Table's 7/7/9 is correct. The unusual pairing of a third-degree and a second-degree felony at the same level 7 is what the chart actually says and is not a builder error. Rows 4 and 5 correctly carry level null since they are not ranked offenses.

(5) SCOPE -- every row has scope null, which is correct. 409.920 contains no prior-conviction enhancement, so no "prior" value should appear, and none does. No provision keys off a particular item taken, so no "item" value should appear, and none does. Nothing misused.

(6) QUOTES -- I checked all five, not the three requested. Every quote is verbatim against flsenate.gov, including the ungainly chapeau-plus-subparagraph splice in row 1 ("...anything of value of: a. Ten thousand dollars or less commits...") which reproduces the source exactly, and the complete "whichever is greater" tail in row 5. No paraphrase is presented as quotation. Only dropped material is leading subparagraph letters ("b.", "c."), which is not a misquote.

(7) UNREAD FIELD -- honest, and unusually specific. Its claims are independently verifiable and I verified them: the section really does have only subsections (1)-(10) plus History; (2)(a) really does have exactly seven subparagraphs and none carries a penalty; the History note really does end with "s. 30, ch. 2025-88". It correctly discloses that 775.082/083/084, 42 U.S.C. 1320a-7b(b), and the bulk of 921.0022 were not read, and it does not overclaim on the chart -- it says only the three matching lines were located, which is exactly what is needed and exactly what I confirmed. No false "whole-section" signal.

ONE NON-DISQUALIFYING CAVEAT, recorded for downstream consumers rather than as a defect. The min/max numeric fields do not use a single consistent inclusivity convention across rows: row 1's max=10000 is inclusive, row 2's min=10000 is exclusive, row 2's max=50000 is exclusive, row 3's min=50000 is inclusive. A consumer that naively treats min as an inclusive floor everywhere would match a $10,000 case to both row 1 and row 2 and could over-charge it as a second-degree felony. I did not score this as a wrong value because the numbers themselves are the statute's literal figures and every boundary's inclusivity is stated explicitly and correctly in the trigger prose, so the table is internally unambiguous. If the consuming code reads only the typed fields and never the trigger, pin the convention (e.g. set row 2 min to 10001) before shipping.

VERDICT RATIONALE. Complete on coverage and correct on degrees, levels, boundaries, scope, and quotations. I went looking for the three-time-repeated later-subparagraph failure and it is not present here -- (2)(b)2 and (2)(b)3 were both read and both rowed. PASS.

wrong: 812.014(2)(d)3. -- min: 21 is a WRONG VALUE IN A TYPED FIELD and it manufactures the exact false floor this audit exists to prevent. The operative words are 'if the property stolen is taken from more than 20 dwellings ... or any combination thereof' -- 21 is a COUNT OF DWELLINGS, not a dollar value. Every other min in this table is a dollar figure, so a consumer filtering on min will read this as 'property valued at $21 or more.' The row's own trigger text contradicts the field it sits next to: it states 'NO LOWER BOUND ON VALUE -- any dollar amount, including under $40, qualifies' while min is populated with 21. A $15 theft from 25 dwellings is a SECOND DEGREE FELONY under this subparagraph and this row will not return it. min must be null. This is the third-subparagraph-of-a-dollar-tier-paragraph pattern verbatim: (d)1 and (d)2 are dollar tiers, (d)3 is not, and the builder half-caught it in prose and then re-broke it in the typed field.

812.014(2)(c)9. -- min: 2000 is a WRONG VALUE IN A TYPED FIELD creating a second false floor. Operative words: 'Any amount of citrus fruit consisting of 2,000 or more individual pieces of fruit.' 2,000 is a COUNT OF PIECES OF FRUIT. The subparagraph sits inside paragraph (c), whose subparagraphs 1.-3. ARE dollar tiers ($750-$5,000, $5,000-$10,000, $10,000-$20,000), so min in this table demonstrably means dollars. Citrus theft has NO dollar lower bound whatsoever -- 2,000 pieces of fruit worth $400 is a third degree felony. A value query at $400 will miss it. The trigger prose says 'Dollar value is irrelevant' and then the field asserts a $2,000 dollar floor. min must be null.

812.014(2)(a)3.b. -- min: 1000 is a WRONG VALUE IN A TYPED FIELD, third instance of the same class. Operative words: 'In the course of committing the offense the offender causes damage to the real or personal property of another in excess of $1,000.' $1,000 measures DAMAGE CAUSED TO A THIRD PARTY'S PROPERTY, not the value of the property stolen -- which is what min means in every other row of this table (see (2)(a)1, (2)(b)1, (2)(c)1-3, (2)(d)1-2, (2)(f)). The value stolen under (a)3.b has NO lower bound beyond whatever made the offense grand theft, and grand theft includes value-free named items -- so a stolen firearm worth $200, or a stolen will worth nothing, plus $5,000 of collateral damage, is a FIRST DEGREE FELONY. A min:1000 filter excludes that case entirely. Compare the builder's own handling of the sibling (2)(a)3.a, which it correctly gave min: null. Disclosing the mismatch in the trigger string does not cure a wrong value in a typed field. min must be null, with the $1,000 damage threshold carried in trigger only.

812.014(5)(b)1. -- scope: 'item' is a MISUSED SCOPE VALUE. 'item' must denote the thing taken or involved. This row is 'The first suspension of a driver license under this subsection shall be for a period of up to 6 months' -- a count of prior license suspensions and a maximum suspension term. Nothing about it turns on the thing taken. The correct value is null (or, if suspensions are treated as history, 'prior' as the builder itself used on the adjacent (5)(b)2 -- the two sibling rows are given DIFFERENT scope values for the same axis, which is internally inconsistent on its face).
unread: The unread field is SUBSTANTIALLY HONEST but not complete. Its claim that all level fields are null because s. 921.0022 was never fetched is verified true -- I checked every row and no level is populated, so nothing was guessed. Its cross-reference disclosures (s. 775.082/083/084, s. 810.011(2), s. 810.09, s. 316.003, s. 395.002(9), s. 943.10, s. 893.02, s. 870.01, ch. 252, s. 322.25, s. 921.241, s. 933.40, s. 921.0023) are accurate and appropriately scoped.

GAP: the unread field enumerates (3)(d), (4), and (7) as 'read in full but produced no rows' and omits subsection (5)(a) and subsection (1), which likewise produced no rows. (5)(a) is the substantive gasoline drive-off prohibition on which the (5)(b) license-suspension rows depend and which is penalized through (3)(a); silently dropping it from both the rows and the produced-no-rows list is the one place the accounting does not close. (1) is definitional and its omission is defensible, but it is also unlisted.
NOT a defect, recorded for the record: the History note was correctly identified as assigning no penalty.
fs-812.014.notes:
FETCHED INDEPENDENTLY. WebFetch refused to return verbatim text, so I pulled the page with curl and stripped it to plain text at /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-wyattbensman-Library-Mobile-Documents-com-apple-CloudDocs-The-Digital-Wash-client-sites-hines-mccarty-site/f479602a-ea97-4d2d-a022-47b21330898b/scratchpad/812014.txt, then built my own provision list BEFORE opening the table.

1. MISSING PROVISIONS -- NONE. I walked (1); (2)(a)1, (2)(a)2, (2)(a)3.a, (2)(a)3.b and the (a) closing flush; (2)(b)1-4 and every sentence of the (b) flush block; (2)(c)1-13 and every sentence of the (c) flush block; (2)(d)1-3; (2)(e)1-3; (2)(f); (2)(g); (3)(a)-(d); (4); (5)(a)-(b) incl. 1.-2.; (6); (7); History. Every provision assigning a degree, a mandatory minimum, a mandatory fine, or an enhancement has a row. Coverage is genuinely whole-section, which is why completeness is set to whole-section despite the FAIL.

2. NO-LOWER-BOUND PROVISIONS -- the builder caught the headline traps in PROSE and then re-introduced false floors in the TYPED FIELDS. It correctly gave min:null to the (2)(a)1 semitrailer branch, to (2)(b)2 cargo under $50,000 (the named trap), to (2)(a)3.a, to (2)(c)4-8 and 10-13, to (2)(e)1, (2)(g), and both riot/emergency reclassifications. But three provisions with NO dollar floor carry a populated dollar min: (2)(d)3 (min 21, a dwelling count), (2)(c)9 (min 2000, a fruit count), and (2)(a)3.b (min 1000, third-party damage). All three are felonies -- second, third, and FIRST degree respectively -- that a value-based query will silently fail to return. In (2)(d)3 the trigger string literally says 'NO LOWER BOUND ON VALUE' while min says 21. A table whose prose and whose machine-readable field disagree is worse than one that is merely silent, because the field is what gets consumed.

3. WRONG DEGREES -- none. I checked each against the operative words. Non-obvious ones that are CORRECT and should not be second-guessed: (2)(e)2 and (2)(e)3 both yield a third degree felony (the statute does not escalate for the second-plus prior at this tier); (2)(b) flush reclassifies to FIRST degree while (2)(c) flush reclassifies to SECOND degree; the (2)(c) flush reaches ONLY subparagraphs 2. and 3. and not subparagraph 1. or the named-item subparagraphs 4.-13., which the builder read correctly and bounded at 5000/20000.

4. LEVELS -- all null, none guessed, consistent with the disclosed non-fetch of s. 921.0022. No defect.

5. SCOPE -- one clear misuse ((5)(b)1, listed above). Two softer ones I am NOT counting as failures but flagging: (a) the two riot/emergency flush rows carry scope 'place', but the riot branch is a circumstance, not a location -- only the state-of-emergency-county branch is locational, so 'place' is at best half-right; (b) (5)(b)2 scope 'prior' stretches 'criminal history' to mean a prior license suspension, which is downstream of a prior conviction and therefore defensible. All uses of 'prior' on (2)(e)2, (2)(e)3, (2)(g), (3)(b), (3)(c) are correct criminal-history uses. All uses of 'item' on the semitrailer, cargo, medical/LE equipment, and (2)(c) named-item rows are correct.

6. QUOTES -- spot-checked five, not three: (2)(b) flush riot sentence, (2)(b)4 with its run-together 's. 316.003,the offender' (the source page genuinely lacks that space -- faithful transcription, not a typo introduced by the builder), (2)(c)7 including the mandatory $10,000 fine sentence, (6), and (5)(b). All are verbatim against the source, ellipses are used honestly to elide intervening subparagraphs and definition sentences, and no paraphrase is presented as quotation. This axis passes cleanly.

7. VERDICT RATIONALE -- coverage is complete, so completeness is whole-section. Correctness is not: three dollar-typed min fields carry non-dollar quantities and thereby impose floors the statute does not impose, one of them on a first degree felony. Per the instruction that a complete-but-wrong table is whole-section + FAIL, verdict is FAIL. The fix is narrow and mechanical: set min to null on 812.014(2)(a)3.b, (2)(c)9, and (2)(d)3, move the 1,000 / 2,000 / 20 thresholds into trigger text only, and correct or null the scope on (5)(b)1.

missing: 800.04(6)(a)1. and (6)(a)2. have no rows of their own -- they are collapsed into a single 800.04(6)(a) row. The builder gave separate rows to (4)(a)1./(4)(a)2. and to (5)(c)1./(5)(c)2., so the granularity is inconsistent. Neither subparagraph independently assigns a degree and the merged trigger does describe both branches (touching vs. solicitation-with-no-touching), so this is a granularity gap rather than an invisible provision.

800.04(7)(a)1., (7)(a)2., and (7)(a)3. have no rows of their own -- collapsed into one 800.04(7)(a) row. (7)(a)3. is the provision that most deserves its own row in this section: it is an express catch-all ('any other sexual act that does not involve actual physical or sexual contact with the victim, including, but not limited to...') with no lower bound on conduct type -- the direct structural analogue of the F.S. 775.082(9)(a)1.o failure this audit exists to catch. It is described in the merged trigger, so it is not lost, but it is buried.

No row states that the (4)(c) and (5)(e) prior-conviction predicates have NO minimum severity. Subparagraph 4. reaches all of chapter 794 excluding s. 794.011(10) at ANY degree, and subparagraph 7. reaches ANY violation of this section at any degree -- including a third-degree felony under (5)(d), (6)(c), or (7)(c), and including a prior committed by an offender who was himself under 18. Both rows say only 'any of the seven enumerated offenses,' which reads as a list of named items and hides that there is no degree floor on the predicate. This is exactly the 775.082(9)(a)1.o 'any degree' pattern.
wrong: 800.04(5)(e) -- MISUSED scope. scope is 'prior' but min=12 / max=16 encode the VICTIM'S AGE, not criminal history. Read as typed, the row says the first-degree enhancement requires 12 to 15 prior convictions. The statute requires exactly one qualifying prior. Compare the builder's own 800.04(4)(c) row, which also uses scope 'prior' but sets min/max to null -- the same scope value carries two different meanings across two rows of the same table. Under the rule that 'prior' must mean criminal history, 12/16 is a wrong value in a typed field, and the trigger prose disclosing that they are ages does not cure it.

800.04(4)(c) -- typed fields drop the victim-age reach entirely (min null / max null). Because scope was spent on 'prior', nothing typed records that this enhancement rides on lewd or lascivious battery, which under (4)(a)1. reaches victims 12-15 and under (4)(a)2. reaches ANY victim under 16. Additionally, if scope is 'prior' then min should be 1 (the statute requires at least one prior conviction), not null. Null reads as no prior threshold at all.

TYPED-FIELD COLLISION, molestation grid -- offender age is the operative differentiator in (5)(b), (5)(c)1., (5)(c)2., (5)(d), and (5)(e), and it is encoded in NO typed field on any row. Result: 800.04(5)(b) (scope victim, min null, max 12, LIFE FELONY) and 800.04(5)(c)1. (scope victim, min null, max 12, SECOND DEGREE) are byte-identical on every typed field and carry different degrees. Likewise 800.04(5)(c)2., 800.04(5)(d), and 800.04(5)(e) are all (scope victim, min 12, max 16) and carry SECOND, THIRD, and FIRST degree respectively. Any consumer resolving a degree from the typed fields gets an arbitrary answer, and the worst case is returning 'second degree' for an offender 18 or older against a victim under 12, which is a life felony.

QUOTE SPLICE -- 800.04(5)(c)2. The quote is presented as one continuous verbatim sentence ending '...but less than 16 years of age commits a felony of the second degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.' In the statute, subparagraph 2. ends at 'less than 16 years of age'; the words 'commits a felony of the second degree...' are FLUSH closing language governing subparagraphs 1. AND 2. equally. The builder marked this elision correctly on the (5)(c)1. row with '...' and then presented the splice unmarked on the (5)(c)2. row. As quoted, subparagraph 2. looks self-contained and subparagraph 1. looks dependent, when both depend on the flush text identically.

QUOTE SPLICE -- 800.04(7)(a). The quote runs subparagraph 3. straight into '...or the simulation of any act involving sexual activity in the presence of a victim who is less than 16 years of age, commits lewd or lascivious exhibition.' The statute breaks after 'sexual activity'; 'in the presence of a victim who is less than 16 years of age, commits lewd or lascivious exhibition' is FLUSH language governing subparagraphs 1., 2., AND 3. As spliced, the victim-presence element reads as an element of branch 3 only, which would mean intentional masturbation (1.) and lewd exposure of the genitals (2.) require no victim present at all. That is a substantive misstatement of the elements. The trigger prose states the correct reading, so the row is self-contradicting rather than uniformly wrong.

QUOTE SPLICE -- 800.04(6)(a). Same defect, third instance: '2. Solicits a person under 16 years of age to commit a lewd or lascivious act commits lewd or lascivious conduct.' The trailing 'commits lewd or lascivious conduct' is flush language closing both subparagraphs, not the tail of subparagraph 2. Three of three spot-checked quotes are unmarked splices across flush-language breaks, so this is a systematic habit in this table, not a one-off typo.
unread: The unread field is substantially honest and I found no false claim in it. Independent verification of the full 2025 text against both a rendered fetch and the raw HTML confirms nothing inside s. 800.04 was skipped: (1)(a)-(e), (2), (3), (4)(a)1.-2./(b)/(c)1.-7., (5)(a)-(e) incl. 1.-7., (6)(a)1.-2./(b)/(c), (7)(a)1.-3./(b)/(c), and (8) are all accounted for.

The declared external non-reads are correct and appropriately scoped: s. 921.0022 (which is why every level is null -- levels are honestly withheld, not guessed, and no unverifiable level is asserted anywhere), s. 775.082 incl. 775.082(3)(a)4., s. 775.083, s. 775.084, and the (4)(c)/(5)(e) predicate statutes.
The claim 's. 800.04 itself states no mandatory minimum in its own text' is accurate -- I confirmed no mandatory minimum term appears anywhere in the section.

One caveat: the field asserts the section was read 'start to finish from the verbatim 2025 text,' yet three of the table's quotations splice flush closing language into subparagraphs without marking the elision. That does not falsify the claim of having read the text, but it means 'verbatim' overstates the fidelity of what was transcribed.

One undisclosed item: the field does not mention that (6)(a)1.-2. and (7)(a)1.-3. were merged into single rows rather than given individual rows, while (4)(a) and (5)(c) subparagraphs were split. Listing them as 'read' is accurate; the granularity choice is simply not surfaced.
fs-800.04.notes:
COVERAGE: complete. Every provision in s. 800.04 that assigns a degree or an enhancement has a row -- (4)(b), (4)(c), (5)(b), (5)(c)1., (5)(c)2., (5)(d), (5)(e), (6)(b), (6)(c), (7)(b), (7)(c) -- plus definitional rows for (4)(a)1./2., (5)(a), (6)(a), (7)(a) and the (8) exception. The section contains no mandatory minimum in its own text. Hence completeness "whole-section".

DEGREES: all eleven degree assignments check out verbatim against the operative words. Second (4)(b), first (4)(c), LIFE (5)(b), second (5)(c), third (5)(d), first (5)(e), second (6)(b), third (6)(c), second (7)(b), third (7)(c). No wrong degree found.

WHY THIS STILL FAILS: correctness, not coverage. The single most serious item is 800.04(5)(e), where scope="prior" is paired with min=12/max=16 -- victim ages sitting in a criminal-history field. Read as typed it says "12 to 15 prior convictions." The prose disclosure does not rescue a wrong typed value. Compounding it, the same scope value means something different one row earlier at (4)(c) (null/null), so there is no consistent reading of "prior" anywhere in this table.

Second: offender age is the differentiator across the entire molestation grid and it is encoded in no typed field on any row. (5)(b) and (5)(c)1. are typed-identical and differ by life-felony vs second-degree; (5)(c)2., (5)(d), and (5)(e) are typed-identical and differ by second, third, and first. Any typed-field lookup on victim-under-12 can return "second degree" for what is actually a life felony.

ON THE PATTERN THIS AUDIT EXISTS TO CATCH: the builder did catch the primary instance. 800.04(4)(a)2. -- second subparagraph, different conduct, ANY victim under 16 with the 12-year floor from (4)(a)1. NOT carrying over -- is correctly rowed with min null and called out explicitly. (5)(c)2.'s age re-pairing is likewise caught. The residual no-lower-bound exposure is in the (4)(c)/(5)(e) predicate lists: chapter 794 at any degree and "this section" at any degree, including third-degree felonies, with no severity floor stated anywhere. That is the 775.082(9)(a)1.o shape and it is currently invisible in the typed data.

Levels: all null with an honest disclosure that 921.0022 was never opened. Nothing guessed, so no level failure -- but the table asserts no severity level for any offense in the section.

wrong: 775.087(3)(f)1 -- NO-LOWER-BOUND ERROR, the reason this audit exists. The row sets min:21 and states the >20-cartridge definition is a 'Definitional quantity threshold gating every subsection (3) mandatory minimum.' That is false. Every subsection (3) penalty is written in the DISJUNCTIVE: '...possessed a semiautomatic firearm and its high-capacity detachable box magazine OR a machine gun as defined in s. 790.001, shall be sentenced to a minimum term of imprisonment of 15 years.' The machine-gun prong carries NO magazine-capacity floor and NO quantity element of any kind -- a belt-fed machine gun, or a machine gun with a 10-round magazine, or a machine gun with no detachable box magazine at all, triggers the full 15-year / 20-year / 25-to-life ladder. By encoding min:21 on the only row in subsection (3) that carries a number, and describing it as gating 'every' subsection (3) minimum, the table implies a quantity floor for all of subsection (3) that half of subsection (3) does not have. This is structurally identical to the 812.014(2)(b)2 and 817.568(2)(b) failures: a threshold read out of one branch and projected onto the whole paragraph.

775.087(3)(f)1 min:21 is asserted despite s. 790.001 being expressly listed as UNREAD in the table's own unread field. The 'machine gun' definition in s. 790.001 is precisely what establishes that the alternative prong has no magazine requirement. The builder made a scope claim about the whole subsection that its own admitted reading gap could not support.

775.087(3)(a)1, (3)(a)2, (3)(a)3 -- each trigger ends with the flat assertion 'NO dollar or quantity trigger.' Subsection (3)'s first prong is gated on a magazine 'capable of being loaded with more than 20 centerfire cartridges,' which IS a quantity element, and the table itself encodes it as min:21 one row later. The table cannot be right in both places. Either the three penalty rows understate the trigger, or the definition row overstates it; as written the two are contradictory.

775.087(3)(f)1 scope:'item' with min:21 -- misused typed value. min:21 is a capacity count of centerfire cartridges, not a count or valuation of 'the thing taken or involved.' The item is the magazine (quantity one); 21 is an attribute of it. Compounding this, the threshold is not a pure quantity ladder at all: it counts only CENTERFIRE cartridges, so a rimfire magazine of any capacity is outside the definition entirely -- an exclusion the min:21 encoding erases.

775.087(3)(f)2 scope:'item' on a row with min:null and max:null -- a typed scope value applied to a pure definitional row that carries no threshold, no degree, and no penalty. The field asserts a dimension the row does not measure.

775.087(3)(a)2 and (3)(a)3 -- quoted accurately but the divergence is unflagged: both operative provisions say 'high-capacity box magazine,' dropping 'detachable,' while the defined term supplied by (3)(f)1 is 'High-capacity DETACHABLE box magazine.' The table treats (3)(f)1 as controlling all of subsection (3) without noting that two of the three penalty subparagraphs use a term the section never defines.
unread: The unread field is substantially honest and unusually thorough -- it correctly declines to guess any 921.0022 level and leaves every level null, and it discloses s. 790.001, s. 775.084(1)(b)1., s. 893.135(1), s. 921.0023, s. 775.082, ch. 921, s. 944.275, s. 947.149, and s. 948.01 as unread.

It is nonetheless internally inconsistent in one respect that matters: it lists s. 790.001 as unread ('these define the trigger items for (2) and (3)') while the (3)(f)1 row simultaneously asserts an affirmative, section-wide claim about how the magazine threshold gates subsection (3). A disclosed gap does not license an undisclosed inference built on top of it.

The claim 'Nothing within F.S. 775.087 was left unread' is verified true against the source text -- I confirmed all of (1)(a)-(c) plus flush text, (2)(a)1.a.-r., (2)(a)2.-3., (2)(b)-(e), (3)(a)1.a.-r., (3)(a)2.-3., (3)(b)-(f), (4), (5), and the History note are present and accounted for.
readWhole:true is accurate.
fs-775.087.notes:
Completeness and correctness split cleanly here. COMPLETENESS is whole-section: I walked the statute independently from the flsenate.gov source before opening the table, and every provision that assigns a degree, a mandatory minimum, or an enhancement has a row -- including the two easily-dropped inline clauses inside (2)(a)1. (the 3-year felon-in-possession/burglary-of-a-conveyance exception and the 10-year prior-conviction proviso), which the builder correctly split out as separate rows. Nothing is missing. VERDICT is FAIL on correctness.

Degrees check out against the operative words: (1)(a) first degree to life felony, (1)(b) second to first, (1)(c) third to second -- all three verbatim correct. Levels are all null with an honest disclosure, which is the right call and not a defect. Scope 'prior' on the (2)(a)1 final-sentence row is correctly used -- it genuinely means criminal history ('has a previous conviction of committing or attempting to commit a felony listed in s. 775.084(1)(b)1.').

Quote spot-checks (I checked six, not three, against the raw source): (1)(a), the (2)(a)1 3-year exception clause, (3)(f)1, (2)(b), (3)(d), and (4) are all verbatim -- no paraphrase presented as quotation. The only quote defects are cosmetic: whitespace inserted into the run-together sub-subparagraph lists ('a. Murder;b. Sexual battery;' rendered with spaces), and the (2)(a)1 quote truncating mid-sentence at '...10 years' without an ellipsis before the 'except that' clause. Neither changes meaning.

The two carve-outs that are easy to get backwards were both gotten right and deserve credit: (2)(a)2 and (2)(a)3 reach only 'sub-subparagraphs 1.a.-p. or sub-subparagraph 1.r.,' excluding 1.q. felon-in-possession, while (3)(a)2 and (3)(a)3 reach the entire (3)(a)1 list with no carve-out. The table states both correctly. It also correctly flags 'actually possessed' in (2)(a)1 versus bare 'possessed' in (3)(a)1 and in the 3-year exception.

What sinks it is (3)(f)1. This statute has no dollar ladder, so the builder found the one number in the section, encoded it as min:21, and then narrated it as a universal gate on subsection (3). The disjunctive 'or a machine gun' prong makes that wrong, and wrong in the specific direction that produces under-inclusive output: a user filtering subsection (3) by a magazine-capacity floor drops every machine-gun case, all of which carry the identical 15/20/25-to-life exposure at any capacity or none. Fixing it requires (a) restating the (3)(f)1 trigger as gating only the semiautomatic-firearm prong, and (b) either dropping min from that row or adding an explicit no-floor machine-gun row so the alternative branch is visible.

wrong: 847.0135(6) -- NO-LOWER-BOUND / TRIGGER NARROWER THAN THE OPERATIVE WORDS. The subsection has two sentences. The first creates owner/operator liability. The SECOND is something else entirely and has no limiting element: 'Any person who violates this section commits a misdemeanor of the first degree, punishable by a fine not exceeding $2,000.' It says 'this SECTION,' not 'this subsection,' and it is not restricted to owners or operators. The row's trigger states the rule as 'Owner or operator ... knowingly permits a subscriber to use the service to commit a violation of this section,' which is contradicted by the row's own quote. This is the exact failure pattern the audit targets: the builder opened the paragraph, read the sentence that answered the owner/operator question, and encoded that, without flagging that the penalty sentence as written reaches any person and any violation of the whole section. The row must either carry a second entry for the unbounded literal reach or explicitly record the 'this section' vs 'this subsection' anomaly.

847.0135(5)(a) -- WRONG TYPED VALUE (off-by-one) AND MISUSED FIELDS. Row sets max: 16 and scope: 'victim'. The statute reads 'a victim who is LESS THAN 16 years of age.' If max is an inclusive ceiling, 16 is wrong on its face (the ceiling is 15). Worse, min/max are value/quantity fields and here they hold a person's AGE, and scope 'victim' is being used to relabel them. Rule 5 applies squarely: a disclosed wrong value in a typed field is still a wrong value. The row also assigns no degree, so it carries typed penalty-selection data that selects nothing.

847.0135(2) -- LEVEL NULL BUT VERIFIABLE. F.S. 921.0022(3)(f), LEVEL 6: '847.0135(2) | 3rd | Facilitates sexual conduct of or with a minor or the visual depiction of such conduct.' Level is 6, not null.

847.0135(3) base offense -- LEVEL NULL BUT VERIFIABLE. F.S. 921.0022(3)(g), LEVEL 7: '847.0135(3) | 3rd | Solicitation of a child, via a computer service, to commit an unlawful sex act.' Level is 7, not null.
847.0135(4) -- LEVEL NULL BUT VERIFIABLE. F.S. 921.0022(3)(g), LEVEL 7: '847.0135(4) | 2nd | Traveling to meet a minor to commit an unlawful sex act.' Level is 7, not null.
847.0135(5)(b) -- LEVEL NULL BUT VERIFIABLE. F.S. 921.0022(3)(e), LEVEL 5: '847.0135(5)(b) | 2nd | Lewd or lascivious exhibition using computer; offender 18 years or older.' Level is 5, not null.
847.0135(5)(c) -- LEVEL NULL BUT VERIFIABLE. F.S. 921.0022(3)(d), LEVEL 4: '847.0135(5)(c) | 3rd | Lewd or lascivious exhibition using computer; offender less than 18 years.' Level is 4, not null.

847.0135(5)(b) and (5)(c) -- offender-age thresholds (18 or older / less than 18) exist only in prose. The table encoded a victim age into typed fields on (5)(a) but left the offender-age split that actually SELECTS the degree entirely untyped (min/max/scope all null on both rows). Inconsistent encoding: the one age that decides nothing is typed, the two ages that decide the degree are not.
fs-847.0135.notes:
METHOD. Fetched https://www.flsenate.gov/Laws/Statutes/2025/847.0135 twice -- once via WebFetch, once via raw curl with tags stripped -- and built an independent provision list before opening the table. Also fetched F.S. 921.0022 raw and grepped every 847.0135 row out of the ranking chart. Raw HTML (52,971 bytes) confirms the section ends at subsection (8); History ends s. 7, ch. 2009-194; there is no subsection (9) and no 2025 amendment.

MY INDEPENDENT LIST OF DEGREE/ENHANCEMENT PROVISIONS (8 items):
1. (2) flush closing, after paragraphs (a)-(d) -- 3rd degree felony.
2. (3) flush closing sentence 1 -- 3rd degree felony.
3. (3) flush closing sentence 2, misrepresents age -- 2nd degree felony (enhancement).
4. (4) flush closing -- 2nd degree felony.
5. (5)(a) -- defines the offense, assigns no degree.
6. (5)(b) offender 18+ -- 2nd degree felony.
7. (5)(c) offender under 18 -- 3rd degree felony.
8. (6) sentence 2 -- 1st degree misdemeanor, fine not exceeding $2,000.
Non-penalty: (1) short title, (5)(d) breastfeeding exception, (7) jurisdiction, (8) effect of prosecution, plus the two undercover-operative no-defense sentences in (2) and (5)(a), and the separate-offense unit-of-prosecution sentence in (3).

1. MISSING PROVISIONS: none. Every one of the eight has a row, and the four non-penalty subsections are each accounted for in the unread field. Provision coverage is genuinely whole-section. That is why completeness is 'whole-section' despite the FAIL.

2. NO-LOWER-BOUND: one hit, and it is the headline finding -- 847.0135(6) sentence 2. See the wrong[] entry. Structurally identical to 812.014(2)(b)2 and 817.568(2)(b): a first clause that answers the obvious question (owner/operator liability), followed by a later clause with no limiting element ('Any person who violates this section') that the builder folded into the first clause's scope. Separately, I checked every other row for an implied floor the table invents and found none -- the table is actually good about saying 'any distance,' 'no value trigger,' 'no lower bound of any kind.' The (5)(a)3 catch-all ('any other sexual act ... including, but not limited to') is correctly flagged as open-ended.

3. WRONG DEGREES: none. All seven degree assignments match the operative words verbatim -- (2) third, (3) third, (3)-misrep second, (4) second, (5)(b) second, (5)(c) third, (6) first-degree misdemeanor. The (5)(b)/(5)(c) offender-age direction is not inverted, which is the usual error here.

4. LEVELS: all null, with a disclosure that 921.0022 was never opened. Five of the seven penalty rows are expressly ranked in the chart and I pulled the exact rows: (2)=Level 6, (3)=Level 7, (4)=Level 7, (5)(b)=Level 5, (5)(c)=Level 4. Nothing was guessed, so no level is WRONG in the falsified sense, but five verifiable values were left empty because the builder declined to open a chart it cites by name. Note for the record: the (3) misrepresent-age 2nd-degree enhancement has NO chart entry of its own -- it is unranked and falls to the 921.0023 default for an unlisted 2nd-degree felony -- and (6) is a misdemeanor and unrankable. So nulls are correct on exactly two rows and wrong on five.

5. SCOPE: one misuse -- scope 'victim' on (5)(a) paired with max: 16 to encode 'less than 16 years of age.' No misuse of 'prior' or 'item' anywhere; the table correctly declines to call the (5)(b)/(5)(c) offender-age split a 'prior,' and its triggers explicitly say 'Trigger is the offender's own age, not criminal history and not victim characteristics,' which is the right instinct.

6. QUOTES: spot-checked five, not three, against the raw text. (2), (3)-misrep, (4), (5)(a), and (6) are all verbatim, including the ellipsis in (4) standing in for the paragraph list and the ellipsis in the (3) base row standing in for the misrepresent-age sentence. No paraphrase is presented as quotation. The (5)(a) quote drops a space after 'A person who:' -- formatting only. The (5)(a) trigger asserts the undercover-operative rule, which is true from statute text not included in the quote; that is an unquoted true statement, not a fabricated quotation.

7. UNREAD FIELD: honest, and unusually so. I verified its claims against the raw text -- (1), (5)(d), (7), (8) all exist as described and none assigns a degree, and its characterization of (8) ('preserves other prosecutions, including under laws providing greater penalties, but assigns no degree itself') is accurate. The external cross-reference disclosures are correct. The only thing I would call a soft spot is that 'every level field is null rather than guessed' is offered as a virtue when the chart entries were one fetch away.

WHY FAIL DESPITE FULL COVERAGE: the 847.0135(6) trigger contradicts its own quote and suppresses an unbounded penalty clause, and max: 16 is a wrong inclusive boundary for a 'less than 16' element sitting in a value/quantity field. Correctness and coverage are separate axes and this table passes only one of them.

unread: 896.101(2)(d) $10,000 'knowing' definitional threshold and 896.101(8)(e) $10,000 injunction-dissolution floor were read and correctly excluded: neither assigns a degree, mandatory minimum, nor enhancement. Their omission from rows is correct, not a gap.
fs-896.101.notes:
INDEPENDENT BUILD FIRST. I fetched flsenate.gov/2025/896.101 and leg.state.fl.us, then curled the raw HTML and stripped tags to text so no summarizer could elide a subparagraph, and grepped for felony|misdemeanor|degree|mandator|minimum|$N. My pre-comparison list: (5)(a) 3rd, (5)(b) 2nd, (5)(c) 1st, (6) base fine, (6) second-or-subsequent fine, (7) civil penalty. Six provisions. The table has exactly those six rows. Nothing missed.

TARGETED HUNT FOR THE THREE-TIME FAILURE PATTERN. I attacked subsection (5) specifically looking for a later paragraph that is NOT a dollar tier and carries no lower bound. There is none. Raw-text confirmation: (5) is a chapeau plus (a), (b), (c) only; all three are dollar tiers; there is no (5)(d) and no flush/closing language after (5)(c). Verified against raw HTML rather than a model-rendered summary precisely because that rendering layer is where an elided subparagraph would hide. Both independent sources agree. No mandatory minimum exists anywhere in the section. The genuinely unbounded provisions are (6) and (7), and both are captured with min null and explicit NO LOWER BOUND trigger text.

DEGREES vs OPERATIVE WORDS. (5)(a) "exceeding $300 but less than $20,000" = third degree, correct. (5)(b) "totaling or exceeding $20,000 but less than $100,000" = second degree, correct. (5)(c) "totaling or exceeding $100,000" = first degree, correct. Boundary inclusivity is right in all three: (a) exclusive lower, (b) and (c) inclusive lower, matching "exceeding" vs "totaling or exceeding".

QUOTES. I did not spot-check three; I exact-substring-matched all six against normalized raw text. All six verbatim, including the mid-sentence split of (6) at "except that". No paraphrase presented as quotation.

SCOPE. Only one non-null scope: "prior" on the (6) second-or-subsequent row. "A second or subsequent violation of this section" is criminal history, so "prior" is used correctly. No "item" misuse. No wrong value in a typed field.

THE ONE REAL GAP (does not change verdict). All three level fields are null, but all three ARE verifiable in 921.0022. I resolved them by parsing the chart and mapping each entry to its enclosing LEVEL header: 896.101(5)(a) = LEVEL 7 (line 1675, inside (g) LEVEL 7 block 1271-1716); 896.101(5)(b) = LEVEL 8 (line 1960, inside (h) LEVEL 8 block 1717-1965); 896.101(5)(c) = LEVEL 9 (line 2164, inside (i) LEVEL 9 block 1966-2169). Chart descriptions confirm each match. Recommend filling these in. This is a closable gap, not an error: null is neither wrong nor guessed, and the unread field discloses exactly why they are null. Under rubric item 4 a null level cannot fail.

CHART-vs-STATUTE TRAP THE TABLE AVOIDED. The 921.0022 entry for (5)(c) reads "financial instruments totaling or exceeding $100,000" while the statute reads "financial transactions". The table quoted the statute, not the chart. Correct.

TWO OBSERVATIONS, NEITHER A DEFECT. (1) min 300 on (5)(a) encodes an exclusive "exceeding $300" threshold, so a downstream consumer treating min as inclusive would misclassify an exact-$300 total as a third-degree felony. It is the only available integer encoding and is disclosed at length in the trigger, so I did not score it as a wrong typed value. (2) The statute assigns NO degree to violations involving $300 or less, while the (6) and (7) rows correctly attach at any value. That asymmetry is the legislature's gap, not the table's, and the table's "ANY violation" language for (6) and (7) is textually accurate.

UNREAD FIELD IS HONEST. I verified its designator inventory against the real structure item for item, including the easily-missed flush sentence after (4)(c) ("This subsection does not preclude the defense of entrapment."). Its structural note claiming (b) and (c) were opened in full and are not unbounded non-value triggers is independently true. External cross-references are correctly declared unread and correctly used to justify null levels rather than guesses.

COMPLETENESS set by me on coverage: whole-section, all six degree/enhancement/penalty provisions have rows. VERDICT set on coverage AND correctness: PASS. Degrees correct, quotes verbatim, scope correct, no fabricated levels.

missing: 943.0435(9)(d) -- NO ROW. THE CORE MISS, and it is the exact failure pattern this audit exists to catch. Subsection (9) was opened, (a) answered 'what degree' and (b) answered 'what mandatory minimum', and the walk stopped there. Paragraphs (c) and (d) were never surfaced anywhere in the table. (9)(d) is a charge-multiplying / defense-stripping enhancement: 'An arrest on charges of failure to register when the offender has been provided and advised of his or her statutory obligations to register under subsection (2), the service of an information or a complaint for a violation of this section, or an arraignment on charges for a violation of this section constitutes actual notice of the duty to register. A sexual offender's failure to immediately register as required by this section following such arrest, service, or arraignment constitutes grounds for a subsequent charge of failure to register. ... A sexual offender who is charged with a subsequent failure to register may not assert the defense of a lack of notice of the duty to register. Registration following such arrest, service, or arraignment is not a defense and does not relieve the sexual offender of criminal liability for the failure to register.' It manufactures an additional third-degree felony count, and it is the mechanism that produces the 'second offense' and 'third or subsequent offense' inputs the table's own (9)(b)2 and (9)(b)3 rows depend on. Omitting it understates both exposure and the escalation path the table already claims to model.

943.0435(9)(c) -- NO ROW. Venue/prosecutorial-reach provision reaching 'any act or omission in violation of this section': prosecutable in the county of the act or omission, the county of the last registered address, the county of the qualifying conviction, the county of release from incarceration, or the county of the intended address reported before release. Not a degree assignment, but it is the second of the two paragraphs in subsection (9) that the table claims exhaustive coverage of and does not mention.

943.0435(5) -- NO ROW and no note anywhere. 'This section does not apply to a sexual offender who is also a sexual predator, as defined in s. 775.21. A sexual predator must register as required under s. 775.21.' This is a categorical carve-out that switches off EVERY degree in this table for an entire class of registrants. A table of penalties under this section with no record that the section does not reach predators is incomplete on scope.

943.0435(9)(a) trigger recites the limiter 'Except as otherwise specifically provided' but never identifies what is otherwise provided. The carve-outs are (4)(c) and (8), which are SECOND degree, not third. The rows exist separately but nothing links them, so the (9)(a) row reads as if it swallows conduct that is actually a degree more serious.
wrong: (9)(b)1., 2., 3. -- typed numeric fields misused. min/max are populated with offense ORDINALS (1/2, 2/3, 3/null) rather than any value or quantity threshold, and the builder concedes this in the trigger text ('Quantity is the offense number, not a dollar value'). A disclosed wrong value in a typed field is still a wrong value. Worse, (9)(b)1 max=2 and (9)(b)2 max=3 assert upper bounds the statute never states -- 'a first offense' is exactly one, not a 1-to-2 range. And the actual numeric payload of these three rows, the mandatory minimum TERMS of 6 months / 1 year / 2 years, appears in no numeric field at all, only buried in prose.

(9)(b)1. scope is null while (9)(b)2. and (9)(b)3. carry scope 'prior', on the same single criminal-history ladder. Either all three rows are keyed to prior offense count or none are. The inconsistency means a consumer filtering on scope='prior' silently loses the first-offense tier of the ladder.

943.0435(4)(d) degree 'no degree assigned' -- under-specified to the point of being misleading. The cross-reference resolves determinately: subsection (9) contains exactly one degree assignment, (9)(a)'s third degree felony. Failure by a transient registrant to make the 30-day in-person report is a third degree felony. Reporting 'no degree assigned' on a row whose degree is fixed and unambiguous drops a real felony exposure out of any degree-based query.

943.0435(7) degree 'no degree assigned' -- same defect. Failure to report intended out-of-state residence (48 hours) or intended international travel (21 days) is punishable under (9), which means third degree felony. The row should carry the resolved degree, flagged as cross-referenced, not null.
readWhole:true is not supportable on this output. Two of the four paragraphs of subsection (9) produced no row and are not referenced in any trigger.
unread: The unread field is NOT honest. Its first entry claims 'No subsection of s. 943.0435 went unread. Subsections (1) through (14), including every paragraph, subparagraph, sub-subparagraph, sub-sub-subparagraph and flush language ... were read start to finish.' That assertion is contradicted by the table itself: 943.0435(9)(c) and 943.0435(9)(d) appear in no row, no cite, and no trigger string. Whether they were skipped or read-and-dropped, the field asserts total coverage that the rows do not support, and it is the single field an automated consumer would trust to decide no further reading is needed.

The remaining unread entries are accurate and appropriately scoped: s. 775.082/.083/.084, F.S. 921.0022, s. 775.21, s. 943.04354, s. 948.001, s. 668.602, the enumerated qualifying-offense statutes, and the procedural cross-references were correctly declared as not opened.

Declaring 921.0022 unopened and leaving every level null is the correct call -- no level is guessed anywhere in the table, so there is no fabricated-level finding. But it does mean the table supplies zero sentencing levels and cannot be used for scoresheet work as-is.
fs-943.0435.notes:
METHOD: fetched https://www.flsenate.gov/Laws/Statutes/2025/943.0435 directly and parsed the raw HTML myself after the fetch summarizer declined to reproduce the text. Built an independent provision list, then compared.

MY INDEPENDENT LIST of every provision assigning a degree, mandatory minimum, or enhancement: (4)(c) 2d deg; (4)(d) cross-ref to (9); (7) cross-ref to (9); (8) 2d deg; (9)(a) 3d deg + 'each instance ... separate offense' multiplier; (9)(b) intro + 1./2./3. mandatory minimum community control; (9)(c) venue expansion; (9)(d) actual-notice / subsequent-charge / defense-stripping enhancement; (13) flush + (a)-(d) 3d deg. Nine of these are on the table. (9)(c) and (9)(d) are not.

NO-LOWER-BOUND CHECK: (9)(d) applies to ANY registrant, at ANY point, on ANY qualifying arrest, information, complaint, or arraignment -- no value, quantity, prior-offense, or victim-age floor whatsoever. It sits in the same paragraph as (9)(b)'s tiered ladder, and the table's presence of a tiered ladder in (9)(b) with nothing after it implies (9) bottoms out at those tiers. It does not. This is precisely the 812.014(2)(b)2 / 775.082(9)(a)1.o / 817.568(2)(b) shape: paragraph opened, the tiered subparagraph answered the question, the later unbounded subparagraph never read out.

WHAT THE TABLE GOT RIGHT (stated so the failure is not misread as a total failure): all four degree assignments are correct against the operative words -- (4)(c) 'commits a felony of the second degree', (8) 'commits a felony of the second degree', (9)(a) 'commits a felony of the third degree', (13) flush 'commits a felony of the third degree'. The (13) flush-language analysis is genuinely well done: the builder correctly recognized that the degree sits in the run-on clause after (d) and attaches to all four of (a)-(d), and gave each alternative act its own row. The (9)(a) row correctly flags the catch-all as having no lower bound and correctly captures the separate-offense multiplier.

QUOTES -- six checked, more than the three required, all against the fetched text: (4)(c) verbatim; (9)(a) verbatim across its full ~1,400 characters including the trailing separate-offense sentence; (7) verbatim; (8) verbatim; (9)(b)1. verbatim; (13)(d) verbatim. No paraphrase is presented as quotation anywhere. Two typographic notes only, neither substantive: the (13) row uses a mid-quote ellipsis, which is proper; and the (13)(d) quote inserts a space at 'false information,commits', which is run together in the source because the flush language begins there.

AXES: correctness fails independently of coverage. Even setting the two missing paragraphs aside, the typed-field misuse across (9)(b)1.-3. and the null degrees on (4)(d) and (7) would carry a FAIL. Coverage fails on (9)(c), (9)(d), and (5), so completeness is 'partial', not the 'whole-section' the readWhole flag and unread field assert.

F.S. 921.0022 -- I read only the three lines matching 827.071 plus every LEVEL header line, which is what was needed to place them by line position. The remainder of the chart was not read.

F.S. 775.0847 -- I read (1) and the opening of (2) only, enough to confirm s. 827.071 is an enumerated predicate for next-higher-degree reclassification. The reclassification mechanics in (2)(a)-(b) and (3) were not read in full.
F.S. 794.0115 -- I read (1) through (6) partially, enough to confirm s. 827.071(2), (3), (4) are enumerated predicates and the 25-year/50-year mandatory minimum. Subsections beyond (6) not read.
Case law construing 'intentionally view', the (1)(f) more-than-a-single-image proof limit, or unit-of-prosecution under the (5)(a) separate-offense clause -- not researched. This audit is text-only.
fs-827.071.notes:
AUDIT METHOD: fetched the statute independently and extracted raw HTML via curl+regex rather than relying on a summarizing fetch, built my own provision list, and only then opened the table.

1. MISSING PROVISIONS -- none. Independent walk of s. 827.071 (2025): (1)(a)-(n) definitions incl. (1)(b)1.-2., (1)(e)1.-2., (1)(l)1.-2., (1)(l)2.a.-e. assign no degree; degree-assigning provisions are exactly (2), (3), (4), (5)(a); non-degree operative provisions are (5)(b) exemption and (6) non-preclusion. Section ends at (6) -- confirmed against raw text and History line (s. 2, ch. 2025-99). No (7). Every one of the six has a row.

2. NO-LOWER-BOUND -- the pattern this audit exists to catch has no host in this section: no paragraph here opens with a tier or named item and continues into unbounded subparagraphs. The two places where a builder would most plausibly invent a false floor were both handled correctly. (a) The "three or more copies" figure in (4) is correctly characterized as prima facie evidence of the intent-to-promote element, NOT a quantity threshold -- encoding min:3 would have been the error, and the table explicitly refuses it and states possession of a single item with intent is a second degree felony. (b) The (1)(f) "more than a single image" limit is correctly confined to the "intentionally view" modality of (5)(a) and not allowed to leak onto solicit/possess/control. All four offense rows carry min:null/max:null, which is right.

3. DEGREES -- verified against operative words. (2) "commits a felony of the second degree" = 2nd; (3) 2nd; (4) 2nd; (5)(a) "commits a felony of the third degree" = 3rd. All four match. (5)(b) and (6) correctly carry "no degree assigned".

4. LEVELS -- verified by line position between LEVEL headers in the live 2025 s. 921.0022, not from memory. 827.071(5)|3rd at line 788 falls between the LEVEL 6 header (736) and LEVEL 7 header (804) => Level 6, matching the table. This is a real trap: this entry ranked Level 5 in older chart versions and a memory-guessed 5 would have been wrong. 827.071(2)&(3)|2nd (line 895) and 827.071(4)|2nd (line 896) fall between LEVEL 7 (804) and LEVEL 8 (946) => Level 7, matching. Note the chart cites (5) without paragraph designation, which the table itself flags.

5. SCOPE -- every row is scope:null. No "prior" and no "item" is asserted anywhere, so there is no misuse. This is correct: nothing in s. 827.071 turns on criminal history or on a valued item, and the table correctly declines to invent one for the (4) three-copy figure.

6. QUOTES -- I checked all six, not three. After normalizing smart quotes, non-breaking spaces and whitespace, every quote string is a verbatim substring of the statute. Zero paraphrase presented as quotation.

7. UNREAD FIELD -- honest, and its two out-of-section flags are real, which I confirmed rather than took on faith. F.S. 775.0847(2) does reclassify a violation of s. 827.071 to the next higher degree. F.S. 794.0115(2) does enumerate "s. 827.071(2), (3), or (4)" as predicates for a mandatory minimum of 25 years, rising to 50 years for offenses committed on or after 10/1/2014. Both are genuinely outside s. 827.071 and both were disclosed, so this is a strength. Consumers must understand the four degrees here are not a ceiling on exposure -- a point the (6) row independently makes.

NITS (do not move the verdict): (i) the (5)(b) trigger calls it "the second subparagraph of paragraph (5)"; it is a paragraph of subsection (5), not a subparagraph. Terminology only, no legal effect. (ii) the (5)(a) trigger compresses (1)(f)'s enumerated list ("more than a single image, motion picture, exhibition, show, image, data, computer depiction, representation, or other presentation") to "more than a single image" -- substantively accurate and it sits in a prose field, not the quote field, so it does not implicate the quotation rule.

VERDICT REASONING: completeness set on coverage = whole-section (all six provisions rowed). Verdict set on coverage AND correctness: degrees correct against operative words, levels independently verifiable and verified in the ranking chart, no fabricated bounds, scope clean, quotes exact, unread honest. I was instructed to find what was missed and not to confirm; I applied all seven checks adversarially and found nothing altering a degree, level, bound, or scope value. Reporting a manufactured finding to satisfy that framing would itself be the failure, so I am returning PASS on the evidence.

wrong: 893.13(8)(d) -- THE NO-LOWER-BOUND FAILURE. Typed min:1000 asserts a $1,000 floor on a DISJUNCTIVE paragraph whose second prong has no dollar bound at all. The statute reads '...received $1,000 or more in payment for writing one or more prescriptions OR, in the case of a prescription written for a controlled substance described in s. 893.135, has written one or more prescriptions for a quantity ... which, individually or in the aggregate, meets the threshold for the offense of trafficking...'. A practitioner who wrote a trafficking-quantity prescription and was paid $0 commits the reclassified second degree felony. The row's own trigger admits this ('Prong two has NO dollar bound at all') and then leaves min:1000 standing. This is structurally identical to 817.568(2)(b) and 812.014(2)(b)2: prose disclosure, typed floor. Any consumer filtering on min, or rendering the typed fields as '2nd deg felony, $1,000+', loses the trafficking-quantity prong entirely. Must be split into two rows: min 1000 (payment prong) and min null (s. 893.135 quantity prong).

893.13(8)(d) -- UNIT COLLISION IN A TYPED FIELD. min:1000 is DOLLARS. Every other populated min/max in the table -- (1)(b) min:10, (2)(b) min:10, (6)(c) min:10, (3) max:20, (6)(b) max:20 -- is GRAMS. Same typed field, two incompatible dimensions, no unit discriminator anywhere in the schema. The only signal is prose inside trigger. Cross-row comparison or sorting on min is meaningless as typed.

893.13(3) -- max:20 is off by one against the statute and the row admits it. Statute: 'delivers, without consideration, 20 grams or less of cannabis' -- INCLUSIVE at 20. The row's own trigger says 'the upper bound is INCLUSIVE in the statute ... so exactly 20 grams IS covered even though max is recorded as exclusive.' Under the exclusive-max convention the row itself declares, exactly 20.0 grams falls OUTSIDE the typed range while the statute squarely covers it. Disclosure in a prose field does not cure a wrong value in a typed field.

893.13(6)(b) -- same off-by-one as (3), and this one is the single most-litigated dividing line in Florida drug practice. Statute: 'possession of 20 grams or less of cannabis' -- inclusive. Typed max:20 under the row's self-declared exclusive-max convention excludes exactly 20 grams, flipping a first degree misdemeanor to a third degree felony under 893.13(6)(a) at the precise boundary a defense intake tool would be consulted about.

893.13(1)(b), (2)(b), (6)(c) -- min:10 is off by one in the opposite direction, again disclosed and again left wrong. Statutes read 'in excess of 10 grams' ((1)(b)) and 'more than 10 grams' ((2)(b), (6)(c)) -- strictly EXCLUSIVE at 10. The rows say so in prose ('strictly exclusive at the bottom: exactly 10 grams is NOT covered'), which only confirms the typed min:10 is inconsistent with the half-open [min,max) convention the same table asserts for max. Exactly 10.0 grams is typed as in-range for a first degree felony the statute does not reach.

893.13(6)(a) -- trigger mischaracterizes the paragraph's relationship to (6)(c). It says '(b), (c), and (d) carve out cannabis 20g or less, quantities over 10 grams, and Schedule V.' (6)(c) is not a carve-out reducing or excepting (6)(a); it is an independent first degree felony prohibition that aggravates the same conduct. Calling it a carve-out inverts the direction of the relationship for the one paragraph where getting it backwards moves a client from a third degree to a first degree felony.

893.13(1)(e)1. and (1)(e)2. -- trigger drops the statutory qualifier unique to paragraph (e). Statute: 'may not sell, manufacture, or deliver, or possess with intent to sell, manufacture, or deliver, a controlled substance NOT AUTHORIZED BY LAW in, on, or within 1,000 feet of a physical place for worship...'. Paragraph (e) is the only 1,000-foot paragraph carrying that phrase; the triggers reproduce the (c)/(d)/(f)/(h) formulation instead, silently normalizing away a distinction the Legislature drew.
unread: s. 921.0022 offense severity ranking chart -- I did not fetch it either, so I cannot independently verify the one populated level (893.13(8)(d) level 4). That level is however stated expressly in the quoted statutory text ('reclassified as a felony of the second degree and ranked in level 4 of the Criminal Punishment Code'), so it is verifiable on the face of 893.13 without the chart. The other 42 rows carry level null, which is an honest omission rather than a guess.

s. 893.03 schedules, s. 893.033, s. 893.0356, s. 893.06, s. 893.135, s. 893.149 -- not fetched by me either. The table's tier assignments are verifiable against 893.13's own text without them.
fs-893.13.notes:
COVERAGE (verified independently before reading the table): I extracted the section from the flsenate HTML and counted penalty-assigning language directly -- 32 'commits a felony', 7 'commits a misdemeanor', 4 'minimum term', 1 'reclassified ... ranked in level', 1 'second or subsequent', 5 '$500 fine / 100 hours of public service', and exactly 2 flush paragraphs (HTML class='Reversion'). Enumerating them: (1)(a)1-3, (1)(b), (1)(c)1-3, (1)(d)1-3, (1)(e)1-3, (1)(f)1-3, (1)(g)1-2, (1)(h)1-3, (1)(i), (2)(a)1-3, (2)(b), (3), (4)(a)-(c) + flush, (5)(a)-(c), (6)(a)-(d), (7)(c) x2, (7)(d), (7)(e), (8)(c), (8)(d), (10) x2 = 43. The table has 43 rows and they map one-to-one. Nothing is missing. Completeness is genuinely whole-section. THE TRAP PATTERN WAS HANDLED WELL, WHICH IS WHY THE ONE MISS MATTERS. The builder correctly caught all six 'Any other controlled substance' catch-alls -- (1)(c)3, (1)(d)3, (1)(e)3, (1)(f)3, (1)(h)3, (4)(c) -- which are precisely the later-subparagraph-with-no-lower-bound shape. It also correctly noticed that five of those six assign NO degree (fine + public service only) while (4)(c) alone assigns a third degree felony, and that (1)(d)1 has no mandatory minimum where the parallel (1)(c)1 does. Those are hard calls made right. The failure is that the same discipline was not applied to 893.13(8)(d), where the unbounded prong was identified in prose and then contradicted by the typed min:1000 sitting on the same row. FLUSH-LANGUAGE PLACEMENT VERIFIED AT THE MARKUP LEVEL. I checked the raw HTML rather than the flattened text. 'Imposition of sentence may not be suspended or deferred...' sits in a class='Reversion'

AFTER the paragraph (c)

closes but INSIDE the subsection (4)
. The table's reading -- that it applies to all of (a), (b), and (c), not just (c) -- is correct and non-obvious from flattened text. The (1)(c) signage precondition likewise sits inside paragraph (c) and is correctly folded into the (1)(c)1 trigger. DEGREES: all 43 checked against the operative words. All correct. Including the ones easy to invert: (5)(a) second / (5)(b) third / (5)(c) first misd; (6)(a) third felony / (6)(b) first misd / (6)(c) first felony / (6)(d) SECOND misd (the only second degree misdemeanor in the section); (7)(c) first misd escalating to third felony; (10) third escalating to second on death or great bodily harm. The schedule lists in every tier row match the statute exactly, including the difference the builder flagged -- (6)(c) covers 893.03(1)(a), (1)(b), or (2)(b) while (1)(b) and (2)(b) cover only (1)(a) and (1)(b). QUOTES: spot-checked five, not three. (1)(i), (6)(c), (7)(c) second-or-subsequent, (1)(c)3, and (10) first sentence are all verbatim. The (1)(i) quote correctly reconstructs 'or g.' from the source's run-together 'org.' rendering artifact and 'and 2.' from 'and2.' -- normalization of a scraping artifact, not paraphrase. No paraphrase presented as quotation anywhere I sampled. SCOPE VALUES: 'prior' appears once, on (7)(c) second-or-subsequent, and correctly means criminal history. 'item' appears twice -- (1)(i) (form and packaging of the substance involved) and (7)(e) (schedule of the substance that is the subject of the offense) -- both are the thing involved, both legitimate. No misuse found. One inconsistency worth noting but not counted as wrong: (8)(d) carries scope null despite having both a payment-amount and a substance-quantity trigger, while (7)(e) gets 'item' for a thinner substance-identity qualifier. THE unread FIELD IS HONEST. Its four claims all hold up. The assertion that the section was read in full from verbatim page text rather than a summarizer is corroborated by the quote fidelity -- summarizer output does not reproduce 'or g.' artifacts or preserve the (1)(c)1 mandatory-minimum carve-out verbatim. The admission that 921.0022 was not fetched is honest and is why 42 of 43 levels are null rather than guessed, which is the right failure mode. The list of non-penal provisions read but rowless -- (1)(c) signage, (1)(c) community center definition, (1)(f) public housing definition, (6)(e) warrantless arrest, (7)(a)/(7)(b) conduct definitions, (8)(a)/(8)(b), (9)(a)-(h) exemptions -- is accurate and complete; I found no penalty-assigning language in any of them. VERDICT RATIONALE: complete on coverage, so completeness is whole-section. But the typed min:1000 on (8)(d) reimplements the exact defect this audit was built to catch, and five further rows carry typed bounds that their own trigger text declares inconsistent with the statute. Correctness fails, so verdict is FAIL. FETCH HAZARD FOR THE NEXT RUN: curl -sL against https://www.flsenate.gov/Laws/Statutes/2025/893.13 without a browser User-Agent returned a page titled 'F.S. 943.0435' -- an entirely different statute, at a byte length identical to the correct response. It fails silently and looks like a successful fetch. A User-Agent header was required to get 893.13. Any builder or auditor that trusted the first response would have audited the wrong statute without any error signal.

Paragraphs (2), (3), and (4) were never given rows.

18 U.S.C. §1956(b)(2)(A) - NO ROW, and NO LOWER BOUND. 'the foreign person commits an offense under subsection (a) involving a financial transaction that occurs in whole or in part in the United States'. Reaches a foreign person at ANY dollar value.

18 U.S.C. §1956(b)(2)(C) - NO ROW. Foreign person is a financial institution maintaining a bank account at a U.S. financial institution. Status-based, no value element.

18 U.S.C. §1956(c)(7)(A) - NO ROW, and NO LOWER BOUND. 'any act or activity constituting an offense listed in section 1961(1) of this title except an act which is indictable under subchapter II of chapter 53 of title 31.' 18 U.S.C. §1956(c)(7)(E) - NO ROW, and NO LOWER BOUND. Felony violations of the Clean Water Act, Ocean Dumping Act, Act to Prevent Pollution from Ships, Safe Drinking Water Act, and RCRA. Predicates at ANY value.
18 U.S.C. §1956(c)(7)(F) - NO ROW, and NO LOWER BOUND. 'any act or activity constituting an offense involving a Federal health care offense.' ANY value.

wrong: NO-LOWER-BOUND, table implies a floor: the (f)(2) row states 'Extraterritorial jurisdiction requires BOTH (f)(1) ... AND (f)(2) value exceeding $10,000,' and it is the only row in the table addressing reach over foreign conduct. That leaves a reader with a $10,000 floor for reaching foreign actors. §1956(b)(2)(A) contradicts this: a foreign person is subject to district-court jurisdiction for a civil penalty whenever he 'commits an offense under subsection (a) involving a financial transaction that occurs in whole or in part in the United States,' at ANY dollar value. (b)(2)(B) and (b)(2)(C) likewise attach on conversion of forfeited property and on maintaining a U.S. correspondent account, with no value element. The table has no row for any of them.

NO-LOWER-BOUND, table implies a floor: the only two (c)(7) predicate rows in the table are the food-benefits clause (min 5000) and (c)(7)(G) (min 10000). Both carry dollar minimums. A reader consulting the table for 'what qualifies as specified unlawful activity' sees only dollar-gated predicates. In fact (c)(7)(A), (B), (C), (E), (F) and the entire remainder of (D) qualify at ANY value. The builder's prose caveat inside the (c)(7)(D) trigger does not cure the absence of rows, and it is precisely the F.S. 812.014(2)(b)2 / 817.568(2)(b) shape: open the paragraph, find the one clause with a number, stop.

MISUSED TYPED FIELD, §1956(b)(1)(B): min is set to 10000. The row's own trigger concedes 'it is NOT a value threshold for liability' -- it is the flat amount of a civil penalty. A penalty amount recorded in a minimum-threshold field is a wrong value, and the disclosure in the prose does not fix the typed field. Any downstream consumer reading min will treat $10,000 as a liability floor for §1956 civil penalties, which is the exact opposite of the statute (the penalty attaches at any value and $10,000 is the floor on the AMOUNT).

MISUSED scope, §1956(a)(2): scope is set to 'place'. Every other row in the table with no value element has scope null, and 'place' is not a recognized scope semantic (the documented values are 'prior' = criminal history and 'item' = the thing taken or involved). (a)(2) has min null and max null; there is nothing for a scope to qualify. This is a guessed field value.

EXCLUSIVE-vs-INCLUSIVE error carried into a typed field, §1956(f)(2): the statute reads 'a value exceeding $10,000.' The inclusive minimum is $10,000.01; a transaction of exactly $10,000 does NOT satisfy (f)(2). min is recorded as 10000, which is a value that does not trigger the provision. The row admits this in prose ('the recorded min of 10000 is the exclusive floor, not an inclusive one') -- a disclosed wrong value in a typed field is still a wrong value.

Same exclusive/inclusive error, §1956(c)(7)(G): statute reads 'a total value of more than $10,000.' min recorded as 10000; exactly $10,000 does not qualify. Again disclosed in prose, still wrong in the field.

MISCHARACTERIZATION, §1956(j): the row labels it 'PUNISHMENT LIMIT.' It is a statute of limitations (a bar on commencing prosecution), not a limit on punishment. The trigger prose then describes it correctly, so the label contradicts the body. Minor but it is a typed characterization that would sort this row with penalty caps.

CITE/CONTENT MISMATCH, §1956(f): the row is cited '18 U.S.C. §1956(f)(2)' but the quote and trigger reproduce all of subsection (f), including the (f)(1) chapeau and the citizenship prong. The row cannot be relied on as a (f)(2)-specific entry, and (f)(1) gets no row of its own.

UNREAD FIELD IS NOT HONEST. It asserts: 'Nothing in the operative text of §1956 was left unread: subsections (a), (b), (c), (d), (e), (f), (g), (h), (i), and (j) were each read start to finish, including every paragraph and subparagraph.' The rows contradict this. Subsection (b) has four paragraphs and three of them ((b)(2), (b)(3), (b)(4)) produced no row at all. Subsections (e), (g), and (i) are named as read and produced no row. (c)(2) through (c)(6), (c)(8), (c)(9), and five of the seven (c)(7) subparagraphs produced no row. Whether or not the text was physically read, the field is used to certify coverage and it certifies coverage that does not exist. This is the field that has previously disabled a live build guard, and here it would have done so again.
