usc-18-1956.notes:
Fetched the statute independently from uscode.house.gov (WebFetch refused to reproduce the text, so I pulled the page with curl and stripped it to plain text at /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-wyattbensman-Library-Mobile-Documents-com-apple-CloudDocs-The-Digital-Wash-client-sites-hines-mccarty-site/f479602a-ea97-4d2d-a022-47b21330898b/scratchpad/s1956.txt) and built my own provision inventory before opening the table.

HEADLINE FINDING. Subsection (b) is captioned "Penalties." It has four paragraphs. The table rows (b)(1), (b)(1)(A), and (b)(1)(B) -- the ones containing the $10,000 figure -- and then stops. (b)(2) Jurisdiction over foreign persons (with three subparagraphs), (b)(3) Court authority over assets, and (b)(4) Federal receiver (with a full subparagraph tree) have no rows at all. That is the identical failure to F.S. 812.014(2)(b)2, F.S. 775.082(9)(a)1.o, and F.S. 817.568(2)(b): the builder opened the paragraph to find the dollar tier, read the subparagraph that answered it, and stopped reading. It is also substantively dangerous, because (b)(2)(A) subjects a foreign person to jurisdiction on a subsection (a) offense at ANY value, while the table's only foreign-reach row ((f)(2)) tells the reader extraterritorial reach requires more than $10,000.

SECOND NO-LOWER-BOUND FINDING. The table's only two "specified unlawful activity" rows are the two clauses in all of (c)(7) that carry dollar floors ($5,000 food benefits inside (D); $10,000 wildlife in (G)). Everything else in (c)(7) -- (A) the entire §1961(1) RICO predicate list, (B) foreign offenses with seven clauses, (C) CCE, the ~100 offenses enumerated in (D), (E) environmental felonies, (F) federal health care offenses -- qualifies as a predicate at ANY value and has no row. The builder's inline caveat is not a substitute for rows.

QUOTE SPOT-CHECKS (three checked, plus five more). §1956(a)(1) flush penalty, §1956(h), §1956(c)(7)(G): all three are verbatim against the source, including punctuation and the trailing semicolon on (G). I additionally verified (a)(2), (a)(3), (b)(1), (f), (j), and the food-benefits clause of (c)(7)(D) -- all verbatim. Ellipses in the (a)(1), (a)(2), (a)(3), and (f) quotes are disclosed with "...". No paraphrase-as-quotation found. Quotes are the strongest part of this table.

DEGREES AND LEVELS. "no degree assigned" is correct for every row -- §1956 is a federal statute and assigns no Florida felony degree. level is null throughout, which is correct because 921.0022 does not rank federal offenses; no level was guessed. No degree errors found. The failures are in coverage, in the typed min and scope fields, and in the unread certification.

COMPLETENESS is set to partial-section on coverage alone: three of four paragraphs of the "Penalties" subsection, most of the definitions subsection including five of seven predicate subparagraphs, and all of subsections (e), (g), and (i) have no rows. 817.568(19) -- statute of limitations. NO ROW. 3 years after the offense for offenses under subsection (2), (6), or (7); alternatively within 1 year after discovery by an aggrieved party if commenced within 5 years after the violation. This is a hard bound on prosecutability of the exact offenses the table catalogs, and it is selective (it names (2), (6), (7) and does NOT reach (4), (8), (9), (11)), which is a substantive distinction the table nowhere records.

They appear only as passing prose inside two trigger strings, never as rows.
wrong: SCOPE MISUSE, MOST DANGEROUS FINDING. Row 817.568(8)(b) value branch carries min=5000 with scope="victim". Row 817.568(8)(c) value branch carries min=50000 with scope="victim". In a typed table, scope is what tells a consumer WHAT the number counts. These rows therefore assert 5,000 deceased individuals and 50,000 deceased individuals as the thresholds. The statute's actual thresholds are DOLLARS: '$5,000 or more' and '$50,000 or more'. The builder's own parallel rows prove it knew better -- the (2)(b) and (2)(c) value rows carry scope=null with min=5000 / min=50000, and the (8)(b)/(8)(c) COUNT rows carry scope="victim" with min=10 / min=20. Same table, same construct, contradictory typing. Nothing in the trigger prose discloses it, and a disclosed wrong typed value would still be wrong.

SCOPE MISUSE. Row 817.568(8)(a) carries scope="victim" with min and max both null, while the structurally identical base-offense row 817.568(2)(a) carries scope=null. One of the two is wrong; (8)(a) assigns no count and no value, so scope on it is meaningless at best.

SCOPE MISUSE. Rows 817.568(5)(a), (5)(b), (5)(c) and the (5) closing paragraph all carry scope="item". The reclassifier in (5) is 'the use of a public record, as defined in s. 119.011' -- an instrumentality by which the offense was 'facilitated or furthered', not the thing taken or involved. The thing involved throughout s. 817.568 is personal identification information, not the public record. Proof this is unprincipled rather than a judgment call: subsection (10) is the structurally identical reclassification ladder (impersonating law enforcement or a bank/credit representative), it reclassifies by the same next-higher-degree mechanism, and the builder assigned scope=null to every one of (10)(a) through (10)(d). Two identical constructs, two different typings. Related: (9) carries scope="item" for personal identification information while (2)(a), same subject matter, carries scope=null.

LEVEL LEFT NULL WHERE THE LEVEL IS STATED IN THE STATUTE ITSELF, NOT IN AN EXTERNAL CHART. The closing paragraph of (5) states that a reclassified misdemeanor 'is ranked in level 2 of the offense severity ranking chart in s. 921.0022', and the closing paragraph of (10) states the same. That is a level supplied by the operative text under audit. It required no external lookup. Yet level=null on the (5) closing row, the (10) closing row, the (5)(a) row (first degree misdemeanor reclassified to third degree felony) and the (10)(a) row (misdemeanor reclassified to third degree felony) -- the very offenses the level-2 sentence governs. The builder's unread field even recites the level-2 ranking verbatim and then declines to populate the field, which converts a known, in-text, verifiable value into a null. The other nulls (felony rankings, which genuinely require the s. 921.0022 chart) are correctly null.

QUOTE INTEGRITY. Two of the quoted strings are spliced, not continuous, and the splice is unmarked as to what was removed. The (12) row's quote joins the introductory surcharge sentence directly to (12)(d) with a bare '...', silently dropping the whole of (12)(a), (12)(b), and (12)(c) -- three paragraphs of distribution provisions, including the clerk's $1 service charge. The (13) row's quote joins the first sentence to the last with a bare '...', dropping the arresting agency's right to be heard in aggravation or mitigation and the in-camera filing provision, both of which are operative conditions on the only downward mechanism in the section. Every fragment presented is verbatim and no paraphrase was found masquerading as quotation, but a reader cannot tell from these two rows that entire paragraphs were elided. Spot-checks of (2)(b) value branch, (5)(a), (8)(b) count branch, (8)(c) five-year mandatory minimum ('minimum mandatory', correctly preserved), (10) closing, and (11) were all verbatim and clean.

fs-817.568.notes:
HONESTY OF THE unread FIELD: partially honest, with one soft overclaim. It is unusually forthright about the s. 921.0022 chart and enumerates the external cross-references, which is better than most. But it asserts that 'All nineteen subsections (1) through (19) ... were read start to finish', and subsections (14) through (19) leave no trace anywhere in the table -- no row, no mention in any trigger, no note. (1) at least surfaces indirectly via references to (1)(d) and (1)(g). A full-read claim covering six subsections that produced nothing verifiable is not disprovable, but it is not corroborated either, and (15) and (19) are precisely the two that should have produced rows under the builder's own inclusion standard.

WHAT THE BUILDER GOT RIGHT, so the parent does not re-litigate it: the (2)(b) trap named in the audit brief was caught. The 10-or-more-but-fewer-than-20 victim-count branch is present as its own row, flagged as disjunctive, with an explicit statement that it is second degree at ANY dollar value including zero. The same treatment is correctly applied to the (2)(c) 20-to-29 branch, the (2)(c) 30-or-more ten-year branch, the (8)(b) 10-to-19 branch, the (8)(c) 20-to-29 branch, and the (8)(c) 30-or-more branch. All six count branches are separated from their value branches. The builder also correctly recorded, without inferring past the text, that the degree-assigning clauses of (2)(c) and (8)(c) stop at 'fewer than 30' so that 30-or-more appears expressly only in a mandatory-minimum sentence, and that subsection (5) has no rung for a first degree felony while (10) reaches life felony.

DEGREES: every degree in the table was checked against the operative words and every one is correct. (2)(a) third, (2)(b) second, (2)(c) first, (4) first degree misdemeanor, (5)(a) third / (5)(b) second / (5)(c) first, (6) second, (7) second, (8)(a) third / (8)(b) second / (8)(c) first, (9) third, (10)(a) third / (10)(b) second / (10)(c) first / (10)(d) life felony, (11) second. The mandatory-minimum-only rows are correctly marked 'no degree assigned'. (10)(a) is correctly rendered as reaching any misdemeanor, not just a first degree misdemeanor as in (5)(a). No wrong degrees found. No guessed levels found -- every level is null, which is under-population rather than fabrication.

COMPLETENESS is set to whole-section on coverage: every provision in s. 817.568 that assigns a degree, a mandatory minimum, or an enhancement has at least one row, and the four items in missing[] are non-penalty provisions ((14), (15), (19)) and definitions ((1)(d), (1)(g)).

VERDICT is FAIL on correctness, not coverage. The controlling defect is scope=\"victim\" sitting on two dollar-threshold rows, (8)(b) min=5000 and (8)(c) min=50000. Any downstream consumer that trusts the typed fields reads those as victim counts three and four orders of magnitude above the real 10-and-20-person thresholds in the same paragraphs. Secondary: level 2 left null where the statute itself supplies it. Both are mechanical to fix; neither is a judgment call.

wrong: 924(p)(1)(A)(ii): max=2500 puts the civil-penalty CAP into the trigger-threshold field. Table conventions make min/max trigger-quantity bounds (e(1) min=3 priors; c(1)(A)(i) min is null despite its 5-year sentence floor), so max=2500 falsely types a $2,500 trigger ceiling onto a provision that applies to every 922(z)(1) violation at ANY value. Disclosed in the trigger text, but a disclosed wrong value in a typed field is still a wrong value. Should be max=null.

924(d)(1): quote truncated mid-sentence without an ellipsis marker. It ends at 'shall be subject to seizure and forfeiture' but the statutory sentence continues ', and all provisions of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986...'. Every other elision in the table is marked '...'; this one presents a partial sentence as complete. Words quoted are verbatim.

Non-penalty paragraphs (definitions in c(2)-(4) and e(2), fee rules d(2), the d(3) list, i(2), p(1)(B), p(2)) are disclosed as read-but-no-row. Verdict is FAIL solely on the two correctness defects listed in wrong: the typed max=2500 on p(1)(A)(ii) (a penalty cap masquerading as a trigger ceiling, exactly the kind of typed-field value a downstream guard would misread) and the unmarked mid-sentence truncation in the d(1) quote. wrong: All eight (b)(1)(B) rows record a typed numeric max (heroin 1000g, coca/cocaine 5000g, cocaine base 280g, PCP 100g, LSD 10g, fentanyl-analogue 100g, marihuana 1000000g, meth 50g) that the statute does not state. The text reads 'or more' with NO upper bound, and subparagraph (A) does not textually displace (B) at the (A) threshold: a quantity above the (A) floor still satisfies (B)'s element and may be charged and sentenced under (B). This is the inverted form of the no-lower-bound failure this audit exists to catch: a typed field implying a statutory ceiling that does not exist. Disclosed in the trigger text, but a disclosed wrong value in a typed field is still a wrong value.

Quotes in the (h)(1), (h)(2), and (h)(4) rows splice the OLRC heading and body text with an inserted em dash that is not in the statute and is not marked with an ellipsis; editorial text presented inside quotation marks.

The (b)(1)(A) and (b)(1)(B) death/SBI rows quote the fine clause ($10M/$50M and $5M/$25M) as the continuation of the death/SBI branch, but in the statute that fine ceiling governs the entire first sentence including the base 10-year and 5-year branches; the quote placement implies the fine attaches only to the death/SBI enhancement.
